News.title: Four dogs killed and three people injured after multiple vans and car go up in flames – as cops probe ‘suspicious’ blaze
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

FIRE TRAGEDY Four dogs killed and three people injured after multiple vans and car go up in flames – as cops probe ‘suspicious’ blaze







Next

FOUR dogs have been killed and three people injured in a horror blaze after four vehicles burst into flames.

The “suspicious” fire broke out shortly after 12.40am today (November 1) on a residential street in Allhallows, Kent.

Three vans and a car were engulfed by the flames, prompting a major emergency response.

Three people were treated by ambulance crews for smoke inhalation and minor burns.





Tragically, four dogs died in the blaze.

Four fire engines and a bulk water carrier were sent to the scene by Kent Fire and Rescue Service.

Crews spent more than an hour and a half dealing with the fire before leaving the scene at around 2.20am.

Kent Police also attended and the blaze is currently being treated as suspicious.

A spokesperson for Kent Fire and Rescue Service said: “Four fire engines and a bulk water carrier attended, crews wearing breathing apparatus used hose-reel jets to extinguish the fire.

“Three people were passed into the care of SECAmb who were treated for smoke inhalation and minor burns.

“Four dogs sadly passed away.”

News.title: Costa Rica completes new mega-jail for thousands of ‘most dangerous’ lags to rival infamous El Salvador hellhole prison
News.content:
Next

COSTA Rica has locked up the first 123 inmates in its newly opened mega-jail – a 5,100-bed maximum security fortress built over nine months.

Rows and rows of prisoners dressed in orange jumpsuits, and with shaved heads are seated with their hands behind their necks in photos from the $35 million fort.



Located on the outskirts of the capital, San Jose, the prison is modelled on El Salvador’s CECOT, which critics have described as a “black hole of human rights.”

The new prison is called the High-Containment Centre Against Organised Crime (CACCO) and constitutes a symbol of Costa Rica‘s new “tough on crime” approach.



Justice Minister Gabriel Aguilar ‌said: “Costa ​Rica is writing a new chapter in its penitentiary history.

“CACCO is a monument to national security, a forceful response to organised crime, and a guarantee that the state will exercise its authority without hesitation.”

Aguilar has said the new facility will also ​help reduce overcrowding in ​the prison ⁠system.

President Laura Fernández used the ribbon-cutting ceremony last month to put the country’s most dangerous inmates on notice – cartel leaders, hitmen and gang figures, who are the first names on the transfer list.



The government justified the new prison, saying the current facilities are nearly 30 percent overpopulated.

This creates conditions that allow incarcerated gang leaders to continue running criminal enterprises from the inside.

Long ​regarded as one of the safest countries in Latin ​America, Costa Rica has in recent years experienced a sharp jump in violence linked to drug trafficking and organised crime.

The country recorded a record number of homicides ⁠in 2023, ​although figures have since stabilized.

Authorities attribute ​most killings to disputes between criminal groups over drug trafficking routes and markets.



Earlier this year, Richard Madeley visited El Salvador’s notorious CECOT for a Channel 5 show.

The £8 5million mega-jail has become the key component of El Salvador President Nayib Bukele’s war on drug cartels.

Alleged mass murderers are seen stacked from floor to ceiling on metal beds.



He is taken inside a huge unit which he comments looks like an “aircraft hangar”, where the lights are on 24/7 and inmates receive no family visits.

“Whatever reason the men are here, we accept that they’re very, very dangerous criminals. This is a terrible sight,” Madeley remarks.

“It plucks at the heart.”

He also comments on the distinct sense of boredom the inmates must feel.

“Nothing absolutely nothing, can prepare you for the sight of 3,000 shaven-headed men crammed behind floor-to-ceiling bars,” he said. “No doors. No screening.



“They sit there in permanently open view through the bars, on tiers of metal bunks four-high – no mattresses, just thin cotton sheets – staring out. It’s one hell of a sight.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Madeley added: “All meals must be taken in their cells, inside which they spend 23 and a half hours every day, with just 30 minutes outside for brief, heavily-guarded exercise.

“They just sit on their bunks, day in, day out, and the prison lights stay on 24/7, never dimmed. All will die in this prison. It’s a living death.”

News.title: Twisted rapist, 18, who arranged victim’s funeral in front of her during sick abuse campaign is jailed
News.content:
VILE THREAT Twisted rapist, 18, who arranged victim’s funeral in front of her during sick abuse campaign is jailed







Next

A VILE rapist who contacted a funeral director in front of one of his victims to arrange her funeral has been jailed.

Mike Loveridge, 18, of Newbury Road, Didcot, was convicted of three counts of rape, as well as one count each of coercive and controlling behaviour and several other offences involving multiple victims.

He was also found guilty of exposure, causing a female aged 13 or over to engage in sexual activity without consent and causing unnecessary suffering to a protected animal.

Loveridge was sentenced at Oxford Crown Court on Thursday to eight years in prison, followed by a further four years on licence.





A four-day trial at High Wycombe Magistrates’ Court heard that Loveridge subjected one of his victims to violence and controlling behaviour between January and June this year.

He isolated, threatened and intimidated her, a court heard.

And one on occasion, twistedLoveridge even contacted a funeral director in her presence to arrange her funeral.

Between April and May this year, Loveridge committed further offences against other victims, including one count each of harassment, harassment by breaching a restraining order, sending grossly offensive, indecent or menacing communications, and intimidating a witness.

The court imposed five restraining orders to protect his victims and made an indefinite animal disqualification order.

This prevents him from keeping horses or being involved in their care.

Detective Constable Angelique Lihou, of Thames Valley Police, said: “Mike Loveridge’s offending was serious, persistent and caused significant harm to a number of victims.

“Thanks to their courage in coming forward and supporting the investigation, he has now been held fully accountable for his actions.



“This outcome is the result of a thorough investigation and demonstrates our determination to pursue offenders and put them before the courts, regardless of their age.

“The sentence imposed reflects the gravity of these offences and the risk Loveridge poses to others.

“I would encourage anyone who has been the victim of crime to come forward and report it.

“We will listen, investigate thoroughly and do everything we can to bring offenders to justice.”

News.title: Fitness influencer, 23, bedridden and left fighting for life in Bali hospital after contracting deadly brain infection
News.content:
'ABSOLUTELY HELPLESS' Fitness influencer, 23, bedridden and left fighting for life in Bali hospital after contracting deadly brain infection







Next

A FITNESS influencer has been left fighting for her life after contracting a deadly infection in Bali.

Khiana Smith has been battling a brain infection from bacterial meningitis – tragically caught while on her “dream holiday”.



The rising social media star, from Australia‘s Gold Coast, has so far spent nine days in intensive care.

Taking to TikTok to share her terrifying ordeal, the star revealed that she has been struggling with memory loss, blurred vision and slurred speech.



Khiana told followers that her symptoms started with a headache before spiralling into dizziness, extreme pain, problems speaking and seeing with a severe sensitivity to light.

She said: “I don’t know what happened, like I seriously don’t, I just woke up one day and I just had the worst headache, like I couldn’t even get out of bed.



“I think I really underestimated the severity of the situation.”

“Life is so precious, one minute I’m healthy travelling the world, living my dream life and the next I’m bed bound in ICU in Bali with a brain infection that could have killed me.”

The stricken influencer said that her memory issues and the language barrier made it difficut to speak with doctors and medical staff.

She said: “I have lost a lot of memory, like I really struggle to remember things.



“Being in a foreign country, they’re doing their best, but the language barrier is hard and feeling like your whole life is in other people’s hands and you don’t have proper answers.”

The terrifying ordeal has left Khiana constantly exhausted, “absolutely helpless” and desperate to go home.

Sadly the influencer is unable to fly back to Australia due to the effect of cabin pressure on her brain infection.



In an emotinal sign-off, the influencer told her followers: “Don’t take your life or health for granted ever.”

“Only a few weeks ago, I was travelling Europe on my dream holiday. Healthy, happy and living life.

“Never did I imagine I’d be lying in a hospital bed fighting something so serious just weeks later.

“Going from being so active and independent to barely having the energy to get out of bed has been incredibly confronting.”

Bacterial meningitis is a life-threatening inflammation of the protective membranes that surround the brain and spinal cord.

News.title: Child stars of new Harry Potter series pulled from Oxford Street Christmas event over trans-rights protests
News.content:
Next

THE child stars of the Harry Potter TV series have been pulled from appearing at London’s Oxford Street Christmas lights switch-on due to safety concerns.

Harry Potter actor Dominic McLaughlin, Arabella Stanton, who plays Hermione ­Granger and Ron Weasley star Alastair Stout, were set to appear.



But insiders said HBO Max bosses met with the Metropolitan Police and key stakeholders who raised concerns about public disorder linked to trans-rights groups.

A source said: “The Harry Potter cast, including the child actors, were due to be a part of the light switch- on later this month.



“It was all looking really exciting but sadly there are concerns about their safety. With the police and stakeholders, it was decided the child actors won’t appear.

“No one wants to risk their safety if protests go ahead.”

The partnership between the show and the lights switch-on has seen a backlash from lobbying groups.

It comes after Potter author JK Rowling, 61, advocated for the legal definition of women to be based on their biological sex.

The Good Law Project petitioned Mayor of London Sadiq Khan to scrap the event.

In a statement, they said: “Harry Potter lights will not make trans people feel Christmassy, welcome, or safe.



“JK Rowling has promised she’ll use money from the series to fund the anti-trans rights movement.”

HBO Max said of the three actors: “We’re judicious when it comes to asks of their time and have decided not to involve them in the switch-on.”

News.title: Twisted mum slapped with seven life sentences after daughter, 11, gives birth at home to stepdad’s baby
News.content:
SICK ABUSE Twisted mum slapped with seven life sentences after daughter, 11, gives birth at home to stepdad’s baby







Next

A MOTHER who forced her 11-year-old daughter to give birth without any medical care after being raped by her stepfather has been sentenced to seven consecutive life sentences.

Cherie Walker, 34, will spend the rest of her days behind bars after she was found guilty on all charges of child sexual abuse and neglect in July.



She was arrested alongside her husband Dustin, 35, when their victim was taken to a hospital after giving birth inside their faeces-infested home in Muskogee, Oklahoma.

DNA tests established a 99 percent certainty that Walker was the infant’s father.



Assistant District Attorney Janet Hutson told KOTV at the time: “The child is traumatised.

“She has been through a horrific ordeal. Not only has somebody got her pregnant, but she gave birth at home without medical assistance, and this will be her life for the rest of her life.”



She added: “This is one of the most – if not the most – serious child sexual abuse and neglect cases I have ever prosecuted.”

Prosecutors later argued that Walker knew that her partner was sexually abusing her daughter – but did nothing to stop it.

Separately, the stepfather pleaded guilty to multiple counts of child neglect and one count of sexual abuse of a child under 12.

Hutson highlighted that their victim had been kept out of school, which prevented others from detecting the pregnancy.



At court, she pushed back at statements from family members who said they were unaware of the pregnancy, describing the child as normally “rather petite,” and so it would be impossible not to notice.

At the stepfather’s sentencing, the prosecutor said: “It’s very emotional to realise that a child at the age of 10 and 11 was having sex with their stepfather, that she became pregnant and no one took her to the doctor and she gave birth at home.

“When you complicate that with the severe, deplorable, uninhabitable conditions of that home, to know that’s where she gave birth, where those children lived, without even the ability to get a drink of water in the middle of the night.”



Altogether, six children, aged two, four, six, seven, nine and 11, lived in the deplorable conditions.

They were found to be in a home with dog faeces and had no clothing on, according to court documents obtained by NBC News.

It is understood there was also no running water or air conditioning at the property.

All children were removed from the household and it is understood they are now in state care.

News.content:
Queen Camilla joins King Charles for the first time in Antigua ahead of major Commonwealth meeting

Charles and Camilla’s first official engagement of their trip to Antigua saw them enjoy a special Sunday service celebrating the Commonwealth "family of nations"

View 4 Images Queen Camilla and King Charles attending a Sunday church service at St John's Pentecostal House of Restoration in Saint John's, Antigua (Image: Chris Jackson/Press Association)

Queen Camilla today joined the King for the first time in Antigua as they attended a church service celebrating the Commonwealth.

‌



‌



The couple were told the voices of small states must be heard for there to be “true partnerships” in the Commonwealth as Caribbean nations welcomed the UK’s offer of slavery apology talks.

‌



Charles and Camilla’s first official engagement of their trip to the Caribbean island, for a summit of Commonwealth leaders on Tuesday, saw them sit at the head of a congregation for a special Sunday service celebrating the “family of nations”.

‌

They were greeted by Charles’ official representative Sir Rodney Williams, the Governor-General of Antigua and Barbuda and also shared a few words of welcome at the church door with Sir Vivian Richards, the legendary West Indies cricketer.

‌



Anglican Bishop Ernest Flemming delivered the message and told those gathered, including cricket legend Sir Viv Richards and Antigua and Barbuda Prime Minister Gaston Browne, the “prosperity” of the Commonwealth must be a “shared prosperity”.

The royals led the applause for Desrie Markham, Miss Caribbean Universe 2025, who received spontaneous applause for her rendition of the song You Raise Me Up and among the performs was pianist Isata Kanneh-Mason, whose siblings are all accomplished musicians, including her brother cellist Sheku Kanney-Mason.

‌



View 4 Images The Very Reverend Dwane Cassius greets Camilla and Charles (Image: Chris Jackson/Press Association)

Antigua’s prime minister gave a bible reading as did the Governor-General and prayers were said to “grant discernment, courage, integrity and compassion to all heads of Government”.

‌



The Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting, held every two years, has the theme, Accelerating Partnerships and Investment for a Prosperous Commonwealth, but talks are expected to be dominated by discussions of Andy Burnham’s offer to Commonwealth nations to discuss a slavery apology from Britain.

View 4 Images Charles and Camilla carried out their first official engagement of their trip to the Caribbean island (Image: Chris Jackson/Press Association)

‌



The Prime Minister expressed “my sorrow and regret for the pain and suffering of so many millions” but ruled out considering financial reparations.

The senior cleric, bishop of the North Eastern Caribbean and Aruba, said: “…accelerating partnerships must mean more than signing agreements or exchanging promises.

‌

“True partnership requires mutual respect, it requires listening, it requires fairness.

‌



“It requires that the voices of small states, young people, women, persons with disabilities, indigenous communities, and those living at the margins are not merely heard ceremonially but included meaningfully in decision making.

“A genuine partnership does not ask what can I take; it asks what can we build together?”

News.title: 'Henry Nowak never came home - his family deserve answers and justice for their boy'
News.content:
'Henry Nowak never came home - his family deserve answers and justice for their boy'

Henry Nowak's family deserve answers, accountability and the absolute assurance that lessons will be learned. Above all, they deserve justice for Henry.

View Image Voice of the Mirror has its say...

Lessons to be learned

The anguish of Henry Nowak’s family is almost too painful to comprehend.

‌



‌



A mother recalling the knock on the door that brought news of her son’s murder. A father collapsing in grief. A sister clinging to her brother’s clothes as they still carry his scent.

‌



These are the heartbreaking memories of a family whose lives were destroyed by an act of senseless violence.

‌



And his family’s suffering was deepened by his appalling treatment in his final moments.

As he lay bleeding, desperately pleading for help, police handcuffed him. His cries that he had been stabbed were dismissed.

Eight agonising minutes passed and 18-year-old Henry never came home.

‌



His family deserve answers, accountability and the assurance that lessons will be learned.

Above all, they deserve justice. No family should ever have to endure such suffering.

‌



Dignity vital

Britain cannot change the horrors of its involvement in slavery, but it has a duty to confront that shameful chapter with honesty, humility and compassion.

Andy Burnham’s willingness to discuss a formal apology is a welcome recognition that the wounds of slavery still run deep.

‌



Chancellor John Healey is right to acknowledge the tough questions about financial reparations, particularly the responsibility of today’s taxpayers for atrocities centuries ago.

At the Commonwealth summit, the Prime Minister has an opportunity to demonstrate Britain’s willingness to listen.

Article continues below

A meaningful dialogue, conducted with dignity and goodwill, could help build a stronger, more united Commonwealth.

Hull of a trek

After 28 years, 30,000 miles and countless adventures, Karl Bushby has finally made it home to Hull. What an incredible feat of courage, determination and endurance. His mum’s first question? “What time do you call this?” Some things never change.

News.title: Britain's top nursing leader issues last-ditch plea on migration 'betrayal' of care workers
News.content:
Britain's top nursing leader issues last-ditch plea on migration 'betrayal' of care workers

EXCLUSIVE: Professor Nicola Ranger, head at the Royal College of Nursing (RCN) has called on Shabana Mahmood to tear up controversial migration proposals as a decision draws closer

View 3 Images Migrant care workers at a protest outside the Labour Party Conference in October

Britain's top nursing leader has issued a last-ditch plea to the Government to pull back from "illogical and unfair" immigration reforms for care workers.

‌



‌



Professor Nicola Ranger called on Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood to tear up draconian changes to settlement rules. The head of the Royal College of Nursing (RCN) said it is "deeply upsetting" that a Labour government is poised to "betray" tens of thousands of nursing staff in the social care sector.

‌



Under Ms Mahmood's plans, care workers from overseas will have to wait 15 years before they can qualify for indefinite leave to remain (ILR) - three times the current level. This would apply to those already in the UK - a proposal that has sparked an outcry.

‌



Spies may have lost thousands of hard drives filled with secrets, report warns READ MORE :

View 3 Images Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood is set to announce her decision in the coming days (Image: ADAM VAUGHAN/EPA/Shutterstock)

The Home Secretary is expected to announce her final decision this week, with speculation that she is poised to exempt care workers from the longer wait. But most other workers will likely have to live and work in the UK for 10 years before being eligible for permanent settlement.

Writing for The Mirror, Prof Ranger said: "In 2020, as Chief Nurse at King’s College Hospital, I worked alongside hundreds of migrant nursing staff who sacrificed so much to help the Covid-19 response. I know so many did the same in social care.

‌



"That only a few years later a Labour government is set to betray those very same migrant nursing staff is deeply upsetting and the reforms are clearly unfair."

She warned that extending the wait for settlement could lead to an exodus from the overstretched sector.

‌



Ms Mahmood is currently weighing up a radical shake-up of migration and asylum rules. Last November she set out a system of earned settlement, warning that failure to get a grip of the immigration system could help pave the way for a Nigel Farage government.

Her proposals would double the standard time to qualify for ILR to 10 years - although high earners and NHS staff are among the groups with much shorter waits. Care workers would qualify after 15 years, but this could be reduced by doing volunteer work in their communities.

‌



Angela Rayner has previously branded the proposals "un-British", and Ms Mahmood faces calls to water down plans to change the rules for people already in the country. The Home Secretary said that unless the rules change, 1.6million people will be eligible for settlement - and therefore access to public services and funds - by 2029.

View 3 Images Prof Nicola Ranger has issued a last-ditch plea to the Home Secretary (Image: PA)

‌



More than 200,000 responses were received to a consultation on the proposals. Prof Ranger has warned that unless an exemption is made for care workers, Andy Burnham's ambition of creating a National Care Service will be impossible.

At a protest outside the Labour Party Conference in Liverpool, care worker Barbara Tanyanyiwa told The Mirror: "They promised us five years, so we want them to keep the promise. We want Shabana Mahmood to keep the promise, we do not want them to change the goalposts when we are already at the doorstep."

‌



Under current rules, people who come to the UK on a health and social care visa are unable to work in other sectors. Home Office minister Jo White told a fringe event at the party conference in October that many may leave care work once they are granted ILR.

She said: "We have, rather than looked to see where our skills gaps are, we've constantly imported from abroad and this is why we're in this situation and why we've got a crisis in the care sector." And she added: "I don't want us to get into that spiral where people move out of the care sector because they've got leave to remain. And this is what we hear from people coming from other countries, that they're here to work, but they then want to go on to other things."

Article continues below

A Home Office spokesperson said: “This Government has announced reforms that mean settlement must be earned and not automatic. We are currently considering responses to our consultation on elements of these reforms."

News.title: Russian strikes cut power to thousands in Ukraine as Kherson ceasefire to end
News.content:
A rare humanitarian ceasefire in Ukraine's Kherson region, that has allowed civilians to evacuate the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky, is due to end on Sunday night.

While the localised ceasefire on the front line has held since it was implemented last week, fighting has continued elsewhere.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russia had struck energy infrastructure in four regions overnight on Saturday, leaving hundreds of thousands of homes without power.

Another overnight strike killed two people, including a 13-year-old girl, in the Vinnytsia region, the State Emergency Service of Ukraine said.

Meanwhile, Ukraine hit a major missile fuel producer in Russia's Rostov region, which caused a fire and damaged four production facilities, Zelensky said.

In Ukraine, repair works to restore power continued throughout the day. Most customers in the Dnipropetrovsk region had their connections restored by early evening, but more than 60,000 were still without power, the governor said.

Because of regular attacks on energy infrastructure, emergency power cuts have been introduced across the country. Even in the capital Kyiv, electricity is cut off for most of the day, and water supplies are also disrupted.

Zelensky said in a social media post that the intensity of Russian strikes has been "extremely high" over the past week, adding that Russia was "trying to take maximum advantage of the shortage of ballistic missile interceptors".

He added that "every day" Ukraine communicated its need for Patriot missiles - the only effective weapon for downing Russia's deadly ballistic missiles - to the US, Europe and other partners. He thanked countries for their support so far and longer-term commitments, but called again for more immediate aid.

News.title: Five teenagers stabbed at Halloween party
News.content:
Five teenagers have been seriously injured after being stabbed at a Halloween party, police have said.

Officers were called to Park Road in Chandler's Ford, near Eastleigh, shortly after 22:30 GMT on Saturday.

The injured teens - three boys aged 16 and two aged 17 - were taken to hospital.

Hampshire Police said it believes an unknown group gained entry to a party at an address on Park Road before the stabbings.

The force has appealed for witnesses and anyone with information to come forward.

A police cordon remained in place on Sunday while officers continue their investigation.

Senior investigating officer Det Ch Insp Elizabeth Pirie acknowledged the impact on local residents and thanked the community for its patience.

Earlier, an eyewitness told the BBC ambulances and an air ambulance had attended.

Another eyewitness said they saw someone running out of the house involved, shouting that he had been stabbed and that he was being chased by two people.

News.title: Thousands of jobs at Virgin Media O2 to be cut
News.content:
Thousands of Virgin Media O2 staff face redundancy risk as the telecoms firm looks to save money in the face of billions of pounds of debt and tougher competition.

The broadband provider has not finalised the number of roles to be cut but it is likely be a sizeable chunk of its 16,000 workforce, the BBC understands.

VMO2 has billions of debt on its balance sheet and is tackling competition from both smaller providers as well as giants like BT, which has agreed a deal to acquire rival TalkTalk, a move which VMO2 has firmly opposed.

VMO2 declined to comment. The Prospect union, which represents VMO2 staff, said the cuts were "disappointing and very unsettling".

Deputy general secretary Noel McClean said it is "committed to supporting our members through what is a difficult time, as well as also working with employers to explore ways to mitigate the number of redundancies and ensure retraining and redeployment of staff affected".

The majority of the affected staff will be in non-customer facing roles and a number of senior leadership changes are already under way, the BBC has been told.

VMO2 is also expected to review its use of contractors and suppliers in conjunction with the job cuts that were first reported by Sky News.

As of 30 June, VMO2's total debt stands at Â£27.2bn while it holds assets worth Â£45.9bn, according to the firm's latest accounts.

Meanwhile, the company is dealing with fierce competition from cheaper "altnets" like Hyperoptic, Community Fibre, Gigaclear, and YouFibre.

VMO2's had attempted to respond to this growing threat by buying altnet competitor Netomnia for Â£2bn via nexfibre, a joint venture owned by VMO2's owners.

However, the Competition Markets Authority (CMA) has provisionally found competition concerns in the deal, external, with a final decision to come in December, sparking anger from VMO2.

News.title: Nowak family tell of 'unbelievable pain' of seeing footage of dying son handcuffed
News.content:
Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has announced an independent review into the murder, led by former lord chancellor Alex Chalk, which will look at "any missed opportunities to intervene".

Henry, 18, from Chafford Hundred in Essex, was a first-year accountancy and finance student at the University of Southampton when he was murdered.

He was stabbed five times as he walked home from a night out with friends from his football team in Southampton on 3 December 2025.

Digwa, 23, was jailed for life with a minimum term of 21 years.

It took officers another 24 hours to identify Henry's body and tell his family.

"I jumped out of bed and I saw the police car on our driveway," said Katie.

"One of the police officers was holding his hat in his hand, and I just knew straight away that something horrific had happened."

She said Mark fell to his knees when he heard the news.

"He let out a cry that I'll never forget," she said.

"I just remember saying 'it's Henry' and breaking down in tears," Mark said. "It's just unbelievable pain."

News.title: King to address slavery in Antigua as PM says he is open to possible UK apology
News.content:
King Charles III is to speak with "unflinching honesty" and "sincere sorrow" on the lasting pain of the transatlantic slave trade, during the final leg of his Caribbean tour in Antigua, Buckingham Palace has said.

The King will address Commonwealth leaders on Tuesday in a speech which will touch on the issue.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said earlier he was "open" to the possibility of the UK formally apologising for its role in slavery - a change in the government's stance.

It is understood the Palace was told in advance of Burnham's comments in an opinion piece on Friday night, and the King has not made any changes to his speech in light of them.

The British government has never formally apologised for slavery or offered to pay reparations.

Burnham has previously stuck with the policy of his predecessors, and stopped short of offering any consideration of reparation payments.

Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch described "endless talk about apologies" as a "distraction" from solving current problems.

She told BBC Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg: "The transatlantic slave trade happened centuries ago. It is time for the Commonwealth to start looking forwards, not endlessly backwards."

The King will make his speech at the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM).

He "will not shy away from confronting the most shameful aspects of the past during this visit", a Palace spokesperson said.

"You may therefore expect him to address them in his speech with unflinching honesty, sincere sorrow, and respect for the wider discussions that will be taking place between relevant governments on this issue at CHOGM and beyond."

When asked about the King's reaction to the prime minister's comments, the spokesperson said it would "not be appropriate" for the King to address matters of policy relating to "the UK government's position".

The Caribbean tour has again thrust King Charles into the difficult debates over the UK's colonial legacy in the region.

On his first stop in the Bahamas, the King delivered a speech where he spoke of the "suffering of the past".

In Guyana, he visited the site of a Slave Rebellion where hundreds of enslaved people were killed.

Buckingham Palace said it was a moment for the King to learn more about the history of slavery and resistance. His engagements have also covered the environment, opportunities for young people and trade relationships with the UK.

News.title: Tributes to 'inspirational' Olympian Ciara Mageean after death at 34
News.content:
Tributes have been paid to former European champion and two-time Olympic runner Ciara Mageean, who has died at the age of 34.

Mageean, from Portaferry in County Down, was diagnosed with stage four bowel cancer in May 2025.

She died on Sunday morning, surrounded by her loved ones, a statement posted on her social media accounts said.

"A beloved daughter, sister, wife, friend and inspiration to so many, she will be deeply missed," it said.

Mageean's death comes less than three weeks after her marriage to her long-term partner Thomas Moran.

The athlete represented Ireland at the 2016 and 2020 Olympics and won gold in the 1500m at the European Athletics Championships in Rome in 2024.

She also represented Northern Ireland at the Commonwealth Games, winning silver in Birmingham in 2022.

News.title: After a 28-year trek around the world, homebound Karl Bushby crosses the Humber Bridge
News.content:
British adventurer Karl Bushby crossed the Humber Bridge through thick mist on the final leg of his 31,000-mile (49,890 km), 28-year trek from South America to Hull.

Bushby left Chile in 1998 to head home to the UK without breaking two self-imposed rules: not to return to the UK until he had completed his journey, and not to use transport to advance.

The adventurer said he was "absolutely overwhelmed" by the crowds who lined the bridge.

Bushby, a former paratrooper, is due to complete the challenge on Monday and will be met by his mother, his son and granddaughter when he arrives in Hull.

News.title: Peaceful protests in Germany spiral into violence and looting
News.content:
Rioters looted shops in central Frankfurt late on Saturday as clashes erupted in German cities over the cost of living.

The rallies were organised by the campaign group Gen Z regelt - meaning "Gen Z takes charge". Thousands had taken part in the largely peaceful demonstrations across Germany before violence broke out.

At least 54 people were arrested in Frankfurt and over 100 police officers left injured, according to German authorities.

Besides Frankfurt - Germany's financial hub - there were outbreaks of violence in Berlin, Cologne and Hamburg.

This comes as protests have been taking place across Europe over the rising cost of living, poor public services, and a lack of affordable housing.

The BBC's world correspondent Joe Inwood reports.

News.title: Reeves says UK's future should be inside the EU
News.content:
Former Chancellor Rachel Reeves has argued the UK's future should be inside the EU, and that Brexit has made the country "poorer, weaker and less secure".

In her first major intervention since leaving the Treasury, Reeves said she welcomed debate around the UK's relationship with Europe.

At the last election, Labour's manifesto said a Labour government would stay outside the EU and make Brexit work.

But Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said there needs to be an honest discussion about what the future relationship looks like.

The Conservatives have said there is no desire to rerun the Brexit debate and Reform UK's Nigel Farage has said there is no mandate to pursue closer EU ties.

Labour's 2024 election manifesto ruled out a return of free movement, single market membership or a customs union.

Burnham has said that any changes would require a mandate at a general election, which is next due by 2029.

In the Sunday Times, external, Reeves wrote: "No-one in the Treasury ever doubted where my instincts were. I do believe Britain's future lies in the European Union."

She said supporters of rejoining the EU had to "make the argument, demonstrate tangible benefits and to get the next steps right".

Reeves added that at the forthcoming UK-EU summit, she hoped for confirmation of the youth mobility scheme she has been pushing for since she was in office.

She also said she was hoping for "progress towards entry" into the Security Action for Europe (SAFE) scheme.

Announced last March, SAFE is part of an EU-wide effort to rearm after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

A defence pact agreed with the EU last May paved the way for UK-based defence companies to be part of projects funded by SAFE.

In her piece for the Sunday Times, Reeves also sought to defend her record in office.

She wrote about the need for governments to be "braver" in building big infrastructure projects and "clear eyed" about the risks and benefits AI would drive in advanced economies.

Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch said she "can't even believe we are reopening" the Brexit debate.

She told BBC One's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg: "This is not something that is needed in order to cut welfare, in order to spend money on defence.

"We are having yet another Westminster bubble argument about the EU when it is time for us to actually start using the opportunities, fix mistakes that have been made and go into the future."

Badenoch added: "I do not want to indulge Andy Burnham's fantasies about redoing the referendum because he doesn't have a plan for what to do today."

Burnham told Badenoch during the most recent session of Prime Minister's Questions that he was focused on "getting a better deal for Britain, that is my responsibility".

The next UK-EU summit will take place in Brussels on 20 November.

News.title: More than 300 arrests at Palestine Action support protest outside US embassy
News.content:
More than 300 people have been arrested during a protest supporting the banned Palestine Action group outside the US embassy, police have said.

Hundreds of people gathered at Nine Elms in London on Saturday, with many holding signs reading phrases such as: "I oppose genocide, I support Palestine Action."

The Metropolitan Police said on Sunday that 325 arrests were made. The force added on social media that 320 of them were for "expressing support for a proscribed organisation under the Terrorism Act".

At least 4,000 arrests have been made in relation to the group, which was proscribed in July 2025.

The UK Supreme Court is due to review Palestine Action's ban under terrorism legislation, after the group's co-founder was granted permission to appeal it.

The Home Office has said that it will robustly defend against the appeal.

Officers on Saturday made arrests into the evening, taking people to police vans for transfer, to the applause of many protesters, some of whom chanted: "Free, free Palestine."

In some instances, officers had to carry demonstrators who refused to walk.

Retired lawyer Charles Allison - who was taken by police in the afternoon - had travelled from Cumbria to participate. He said he feared for people's civil liberties, which he said were "being devalued and watered down".

"I hope the Supreme Court justices - they won't necessarily be influenced by it [the protest] - but I hope that they will take a long-term view of what is happening in this country and decide that the proscription was unlawful, as I believe it was," the 75-year-old said.

David Bolden, another protester awaiting arrest called the ban an "absurd law".

Defend Our Juries, which has been co-ordinating a series of protests over the ban, said the number of people detained this weekend took the total over 4,000 arrests since the group was proscribed, calling it "truly dystopian".

According to Home Office figures seen by the BBC, 3,630 arrests were made in the year ending June 2026. Along with the 134 people arrested outside Westminster Magistrates Court earlier this year and those on Saturday brings the total up to 4,089.

The BBC has contacted the Met to confirm any figures it might hold.

Amnesty International UK has criticised the arrests and called for the government to drop the proscription of Palestine Action.

Defend Our Juries called the arrests "unjust" and an assault on free speech.

News.title: Healey risks breaking minimum wage promise for younger workers
News.content:
The Chancellor, John Healey, has suggested that younger workers might not receive the same minimum wage as others before the next election, potentially breaking a Labour manifesto promise.

In 2024, Labour said it would remove "discriminatory age bands", vowing to end the gap between the adult minimum wage and pay for 18 to 20-year-olds.

But in last week's Budget, Healey said that younger workers would see the same increase as older workers, leaving a gap between the two rates this year.

Pay for 18 to 20-year-olds in 2026 will rise to Â£11.27, while over-20s will be paid a minimum of Â£13.21 an hour.

In a BBC interview broadcast on Sunday, Healey was asked if younger workers would be paid the same as older workers, when it comes to the minimum wage, by the time of the next election?

"We'll take one step at a time," he said, suggesting that Labour might abandon its plan to close the gap before the next election.

It is a change that is likely to anger the unions and some on the left of the party.

Healey added that Labour was still committed to the ambition, but hinted the plan to equalise wages might be delayed, partly to encourage businesses to employ younger workers.

"There is no question about whether or if, it's a question of when - it's a question of how fast," he said.

"I want to make sure we can look hard at those trade-offs that are there between jobs and wages."

"I want to take business, I want to take trade unions with me, and with the government, because together we have to get into what at the moment is a moral shame on this nation. A million youngsters - written off without any prospect of being helped into work and making contributions to this country for the future."

News.title: Seven arrested after city centre firework disorder
News.content:
Seven people have been arrested after disorder, involving fireworks being set off, in a city centre.

Footage posted on social media showed crowds gathered on Corporation Street in Birmingham, with fireworks being set off close to police officers and vehicles.

West Midlands Police had warned firm action would be taken against anyone involved in fireworks-related disorder, following serious incidents in the city during Bonfire Night last year.

Those arrested, aged between 15 and 26, were held on suspicion of offences including assault, possession of fireworks and possession of an offensive weapon.

They all remain in custody for questioning, the force said.

Officers used Section 60 stop-and-search powers, which allow searches without the need to have reasonable grounds to do so.

The arrests were made in and around Stephenson Street and Corporation Street, after officers responded to "pockets of disorder," involving fireworks being set off in a dangerous manner, said the force.

Ch Supt Tom Boyce said: "Misusing fireworks is not only dangerous: it's illegal and can lead to fines, arrest and criminal charges."

The force said extra officers had been deployed at key locations to prevent a repeat of last year's violence.

On 6 November 2025, 21 people were arrested after officers were attacked with fireworks on Dale End and Staniforth Street.

News.title: Police probe video of officer hitting youth with handcuffs
News.content:
A police force has said it is reviewing a video which shows one of its officers punching a boy.

The footage circulated on social media shows a Merseyside Police officer punching what appears to be teenage boy three times while holding a pair of metal handcuffs in the hand he is striking him with.

The force said officers had been responding on Friday to reports of about 20 youths in the Alder Wood Avenue area of Speke, Liverpool, blocking roads with wheelie bins and "aiming fireworks at anyone who tried to remove them".

"We would like to stress that a short clip doesn't always show the full context," a Merseyside Police spokesman said.

The footage being circulated on social media - which has been viewed more than 40,000 times - begins moments before the officer strikes the boy.

It does not show anything that happened in the run-up to the incident.

Merseyside Police said youths had reportedly "smashed windows of nearby flats, tried to start fires and threatened members of the public".

News.title: Hospital admits full responsibility for 24 failures that led to toddler's death
News.content:
A hospital trust has taken full responsibility for 24 failures that led to the death of a 21-month-old.

Eleanor Hazel Aldred-Owen died at Liverpool's Alder Hey Hospital on 2 October 2023 - a coroner concluded she died as a result of misadventure, contributed to by neglect.

She had routine surgery for craniosynostosis, external, a birth defect affecting the skull, but an abnormal chest X-ray was not flagged.

Eleanor suffered a cardiac arrest and an unsurvivable brain injury, and died in her parents' arms.

Her family, from Mold, Flintshire, said they had lived with "unbearable" guilt and trauma ever since.

Alder Hey Children's Hospital NHS Foundation Trust said her "tragic" death "should not have happened".

Eleanor's dad Chaz said: "Not knowing how or why Eleanor died was the key factors and what kept us going was justice for her.

"The real victory is making sure what happened to Eleanor doesn't happen to anyone else. No other family or child will have to go through what we have."

He added both he and his wife Rachel were "fairly certain it was neglectful" but did not realise the extent of it, and were "at the mercy of what Alder Hey were telling us".

"They said it was breach of duty and not gross neglect and it took a long time for the trust to admit that."

He said the trust "being compelled to admit gross neglect" was the hardest thing.

News.title: Green Party at 'crossroads' after Zionism vote, says former co-leader
News.content:
Ramsay also said he has made it clear he is "deeply uncomfortable" with the motion adopted and suggested there is an "opportunity to take some action in relation to the motion in the run-up" to the party's spring conference next year.

He said the question now is how Polanski and the party as a whole responds to the motion.

Ramsay said: "I think there's a real crossroads point for the party at the moment.

"One option is to sort of dig in more down this approach, not only in relation to this motion, but I think that there's a risk it brings with it - a quite divisive, a quite internally focused approach to politics."

Ramsay said this is "perhaps seen from small groups of people on the hard left of politics who go around different parties try to influence how those parties are run".

He added: "What I want to see is the party really focus back in on our core aims as a party and our core values."

Ramsay said this includes ensuring the party is "consensus-building in how we approach our politics" and that "we engage the grassroots of our membership".

He added the party needs to be "very externally focused, because we're only going to be able to bring the environmental changes that we need to have to safeguard our society for now and for the future if the majority of the British public come behind that".

Ramsay served as co-leader of the Greens from 2021 to 2025 alongside Carla Denyer, who is also now an MP.

He unsuccessfully stood on a joint ticket with fellow MP Ellie Chowns in 2025, with the pair losing to Polanski in the leadership contest.

Polanski, who missed the conference vote to unsuccessfully campaign for election in a Westminster by-election, previously said he wants to see the "imperfect" motion amended in future.

However, he said the "substantial part of the motion", that "the displacement and genocide of the Palestinian people is clearly underpinned by a racist ideology" was "obvious". Israel has repeatedly denied its actions in Gaza amount to genocide.

Under Green Party rules, motions supported by members become official party policy, but will not necessarily be included in the party's manifesto at the next general election.

News.title: Northern Lights dance across UK sky on Halloween night
News.content:
Stargazers around the UK were treated to the vivid colours of the aurora borealis on Saturday night.

As cloud and rain on the weather front cleared southwards, parts of Scotland and Northern Ireland were perfectly placed to catch the display.

The eerie glow provided a fitting finale to spookiest night of the year, delighting skywatchers and photographers alike.

Aurora activity may continue into Sunday night, especially in northern skies, but the display is likely to be less intense than the one seen on Halloween night.

News.title: F1 LIVE: Lewis Hamilton shoved out of lead by Ferrari teammate Leclerc in dramatic start
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Charles Leclerc leads the Mexican Grand Prix early on ( Getty )

Formula 1 returns to Mexico City this weekend for the Mexican Grand Prix - with Kimi Antonelli set to seal the world championship.

The 20-year-old Italian holds a 123-point lead over Mercedes teammate George Russell and a 124-point advantage over Lewis Hamilton after his victory in Austin last time out. If Antonelli finishes ninth or higher in Mexico, he will be crowned world champion and, even if he doesn’t, Russell or Hamilton need to win the grand prix to extend the title race to Brazil.

Antonelli cruised to victory from pole in Texas, with Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc in second and Red Bull’s Max Verstappen in third. Hamilton missed out on a podium, while an early penalty resulted in Russell finishing a lowly eighth.

Lando Norris won last year’s race at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez, on his way to his maiden world title. After missing out last year, Sergio Perez returns to his home race off the back of signing a new contract with Cadillac this week.

Follow live coverage of the Mexican Grand Prix with The Independent.

News.title: SNL skewers ‘future press secretary’ Nicki Minaj as Trump character admits ‘I might be gay’
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Saturday Night Live has taken on Donald Trump’s newfound fascination with men’s body parts in a sketch that also took aim at his alliance with Nicki Minaj.

After Tom Hanks surprised the audience in SNL’s latest cold open by returning as beloved character David S. Pumpkins, James Austin Johnson entered as Trump and went on to mock the president’s recent comments praising other men’s butts.

“A great ass on Hanks — something that I’ve enjoyed lately admiring,” Johnson said as Trump. “Not that there’s anything wrong with that. Just that I might be gay.”

With a lot of ground to cover since the late-night sketch series last aired with Shane Gillis’ October 10 episode, the cold open then took on speculation that Trump will hire Minaj as his next press secretary after Katie Zacharia’s short-lived stint.

Johnson as Trump brought out SNL’s new cast member Saidah Belo-Osagie as the controversial rapper, introducing her as a potential next pick for the coveted job.

open image in gallery Saidah Belo-Osagie played Nicki Minaj during the 'Saturday Night Live' cold open ( SNL )

open image in gallery Donald Trump and Nicki Minaj’s alliance has raised speculation that the rapper is being considered as the potential new White House secretary ( Getty )

“Trump’s out here killing it — and by it, I mean my career,” Belo-Osagie, as Minaj said. Trump then remarked on Minaj’s famously curvy bottom, adding: “Perhaps if it was on a man, I could admire it.”

To close the segment, Trump then brought out Zacharia — played by Belo-Osagie’s fellow newcomer Veronika Slowikowska — to deliver the show’s signature line, “Live from New York, it’s Saturday night.”However, Slowikowska flubbed the attempt in character, and Hanks ended up delivering the line.

Later in the episode, Colin Jost poked more fun at Trump’s fixation on his colleagues’ bodies during his “Weekend Update” segment, saying: “Your party is about to lose the midterms. Stop playing ‘smash or pass’ with each other.”

The Halloween episode of SNL was hosted by Obsession star Inde Navarrette, with musical guest Gracie Abrams.

During her monologue, Navarrette made a subtle dig at SNL’s Shane Gillis controversy while speaking about her upcoming role as Rogue in X-Men.

While speaking about preparing for the role with physical training, Navarrette joked: “I know it’s really important for Marvel that you get really fit, so I've been working out a lot. So every morning I put on my little w**** outfit, and I hit the gym.”

The comment, which received a hearty round of applause, appeared to call out Gillis’ divisive opening monologue from earlier in the month, during which he delivered a bizarre commentary on women’s gym wear. His comments prompted backlash criticizing Gillis’s sexualization of women. The comedian has not responded to the backlash.

News.title: Photos show Buddhist stupas taking shape in Bhutan’s planned Mindfulness City
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Buddhist masters gathered in Gelephu, Bhutan, as volunteers built stupas symbolizing Buddha’s enlightenment in a procession-like row along the Mao Chhu River. Visitors prayed and chanted. The monuments are part of Gelephu Mindfulness City, envisioned by Bhutan’s king to boost the economy while embracing Buddhist values. The city is being developed in phases over several decades.

This is a photo gallery curated by AP photo editors.

News.title: Who left Strictly Come Dancing 2026? Fifth celebrity voted off after Halloween Week twist
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The latest couple to leave Strictly Come Dancing’s 2026 season has been announced, following a lively episode for Halloween Week and a terrifying twist for this week’s results show.

Ahead of Saturday night’s (31 October) episode, it was revealed that three couples, instead of two, would find themselves in Sunday’s dance-off.

Lawrence Robb and Jowita Przystal, Bethany Antonia and Nancy Xu, and Jaime Winstone and Carlos Gu then found themselves in the bottom three, and performed their routines again.

Antonia and Xu did their Jive to “I’m in Love with a Monster” by Fifth Harmony, while Winstone and Gu re-did their Salsa to “Filthy/Gorgeous” by the Scissor Sisters.

Ultimately, Robb and Przystal became the fifth couple to be voted off after dancing their Tango to the “Ghostbusters” theme by Ray Parker Jr, in a unanimous decision by the judges.

Judge Motsi Mobusi, who had this week’s deciding vote, said she would also have voted for Robb and Przystal to leave the competition.

The couple will join Ellie Taylor on Strictly: It Takes Two on Monday at 6.30pm on BBC Two and BBC iPlayer to discuss their time on this year’s show.

Lawrence Robb and his professional partner Jowita Przysta were voted off after a dance-off with two other couples ( BBC )

Elsewhere in Halloween Week, the results show continued the spooky vibe when the Professionals performed a group routine to “Dracula”, the hit track by Tame Impala featuring a voice cameo from Sir Ian McKellen, reading from Bram Stoker’s gothic novel.

Becky Hill also performed, accompanied by a routine from Strictly pros Aleksandra Isaeva and Cristian Priori.

In Saturday’s episode, John Nellis and Katya Jones performed a passionate Tango, earning the YouTuber his highest score yet. Delta Goodrem and Kai Widdrington also impressed with a Viennese Waltz that was labelled “sensational” by the judges.

Lacey Turner and her pro partner Vito Coppola ended up top of the leaderboard after closing the show with a lift-packed Charleston.

The surviving 10 couples will take the dancefloor next Saturday when Strictly Come Dancing returns at 6.30pm on Saturday 7 November.

News.title: Notre Dame beats Villanova 74-72 in men's college basketball season opener in Rome
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Brady Koehler scored key baskets down the stretch and Notre Dame made a late comeback after trailing for most of the second half to beat Villanova 74-72 in the college basketball season opener in Rome on Sunday.

Villanova standout Tyler Perkins fouled out with 16.3 seconds to go. He led the Wildcats with 18 points.

The event — a doubleheader dubbed the Eternal City Tip-Off — included an audience with Villanova alumnus Pope Leo XIV for both teams and their fans on Saturday.

Both teams are unranked in the preseason AP Top 25.

Koehler and Braeden Smith led Notre Dame, which has 10 new players, with 16 points each.

Koehler’s dunk cut Villanova’s lead to one point with 1:36 remaining and Logan Duncomb hit a 3-pointer with 1:08 to go to give Notre Dame its first lead of the second half, 70-68.

Koehler sank two free throws to put the Fighting Irish up 74-70 with 4 seconds remaining and essentially seal it.

Villanova is looking for a revival after four years without winning a game at the NCAA Tournament: A three-year absence followed the sudden retirement of Hall of Fame coach Jay Wright and then the Wildcats had a first-round loss to Utah State last season.

Luigi Suigo, the 7-foot-3 Italian making his Villanova debut on home soil, had two dunks and showed his range with a 3-pointer to finish with seven points.

When he scored, the arena announcer yelled, “Su-su-su Suigo.”

The nonconference game between the two Catholic universities was played at the 11,000-seat Palazzo dello Sport, which is located about a half-hour drive from the Vatican.

Villanova had many more fans in attendance.

In the second game, Hannah Hidalgo had 32 points, eight assists, seven rebounds and three steals as the No. 13 Fighting Irish women beat Villanova 99-75.

Up next

Notre Dame faces another Catholic school in its home opener against Mercyhurst on Thursday.

Villanova faces two more Catholic schools in its next two games: The Wildcats play Holy Cross in their home opener on Friday and then meet La Salle four days later.

News.title: The ‘crazy’ stats that defined Arsenal’s statement win at Anfield
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

There was a time when Mikel Arteta resorted to gimmicks in his bid to win at Anfield. He has tried blasting out You’ll Never Walk Alone at Arsenal’s training ground. That didn’t work.

Assembling this redoubtable, forceful side did. Five days after the worst result of Arteta’s reign came one of the best. “The defeat against Fleetwood looks the end of the world,” said Arteta. In contrast, this made him feel on top of the world.

Anfield may not quite be the final frontier for the Spaniard – perhaps winning at the Etihad Stadium is or, more importantly, winning the Champions League is – but another ambition has been realised.

open image in gallery Mikel Arteta masterminded the end of Arsenal’s 14-year winless streak at Anfield ( Getty )

For the first time in 14 years, Arsenal return from Anfield with three points. Captain then, Arteta is manager now. A victory that was hard-fought and hard-earned had his imprint on it. Arsenal were defensively brilliant. For the first time since numbers were compiled in 2003, Liverpool failed to have a shot on target in a Premier League game at Anfield. “I didn’t know about that stat but that is incredible,” said Arteta.

In a tale of two goalkeepers, Alisson made a mistake for Kai Havertz’s decider while, remarkably, David Raya did not have save to make. It was testament to the way his teammates showed a willingness to block shots, crosses and anything else in their path. “That togetherness is undefeated, nothing I have ever seen before,” said Declan Rice.

That Havertz got the goal was instructive in its own way. Without playing particularly well, he ended his drought. His first goal in 10 outings was a reminder he remains a big-game scorer. That Arsenal did not add an elite attacker in the summer can leave their forward line with a prosaic look.

open image in gallery Kai Havertz slotted home the only goal of the game ( Getty )

open image in gallery And celebrated ending his scoring drought ( Reuters )

But this was an illustration of why Arteta committed much of his budget to the battle-hardened pair of Ezri Konsa and Bruno Guimaraes; for days like this. Almost three months into Arsenal’s season, William Saliba has not featured yet and Konsa has ensured it barely matters. Where Liverpool had a rookie in midfield, with Trey Nyoni preferred to a fit-again Dominik Szoboszlai and the unused Ryan Gravenberch, Arsenal had a £75m sidekick to Rice.

And Rice was the best player on the pitch in one of the biggest games of the season. “Ninety per cent of the goal belongs to Declan Rice,” said Havertz. The Englishman was the provider of the only goal in one respect, sliding a low cross to the far post for the German to finish, but there was an inadvertent assist from Alisson. Not for the first time this season, his distribution was strangely poor to gift Arsenal possession in the final third.

open image in gallery Declan Rice was the best player on the pitch ( PA Wire )

“We are to the blame, especially from the beginning of the game,” admitted Iraola. But, in different ways, it was a demonstration of Arsenal’s power. A second trip to the north-west in a few days brought a very different outcome. Embarrassed at Fleetwood, there were ecstatic at Anfield. It was an emphatic response

It could also have consequences. The gap between them now stands at nine points. Even at this early stage, that looks insurmountable for Liverpool. If so, their title race may be run when the starting gun has barely been fired.

Arsenal did become champions last season despite failing to score against Liverpool. In one respect, anyway, there will not be a repeat. Beaten 1-0 at Anfield last season, they got the opposite scoreline.

open image in gallery Arsenal made a statement in the title race to distance Liverpool ( Getty )

It was not purely about defence. Arsenal committed plenty of players forward in the first half. They could have scored another. Guimaraes angled a shot wide. Jurrien Timber could not turn the ball in from close range. Alisson made amends in part with a terrific save to keep out Christos Tzolis’ low curler.

Not that Arsenal came to Anfield to make friends. Iraola thought Liverpool were wronged when Alexander Isak’s shirt was grabbed by Jurrien Timber in the box. “It is a clear penalty,” he said. Isak, he felt, was “too honest” to go to ground. Meanwhile, some of the times Arsenal flung themselves to the turf were unedifying, while Raya ended up with a caution for time-wasting.

Liverpool ended up frustrated. They showed their energy in the first half, a high-octane affair as they launched an assault on Arsenal. But clear-cut chances were rarities, the best when Alexis Mac Allister, a few yards out, met Milos Kerkez’s cross but headed over.

open image in gallery Manager Andoni Iraola believes Liverpool deserved a goal ( PA )

The only time Raya was beaten was when Florian Wirtz curled a free kick from an acute angle on to the bar. “We definitely deserved a goal,” said Iraola.

But Liverpool’s 17 shots were all off target and Arsenal weathered the storm. “We knew we have to navigate through periods where we have to suffer,” said Arteta. They have suffered at Anfield since 2012. “Fourteen years, that’s a crazy stat,” said Havertz. But not as crazy, arguably, as limiting Liverpool to no shots on target.

News.title: Villanova had the the pope's support. Notre Dame swept the wins in college hoops openers in Rome
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Villanova had the pope’s support and many more traveling fans. Notre Dame prevailed on the court.

The Fighting Irish produced a late comeback for a 74-72 victory in the men’s game that opened the college basketball season in Rome on Sunday. Then Hannah Hidalgo starred as the No. 13 Notre Dame women won to complete a sweep of Pope Leo's alma mater, beating Villanova 99-75.

The doubleheader between the two Catholic universities, dubbed the Eternal City Tip-Off, was created to honor the first American pope, who was not in attendance for the games.

But Chicago-born Pope Leo XIV did receive all four teams in an audience at the Vatican on Saturday.

“I’ve been a part of some really cool things and this is right at the top of the list of experiences,” Notre Dame men's coach Micah Shrewsberry said. “We played two road games in the (preseason) and it came in handy because the Villanova fans were loud.”

At the Vatican a day earlier, Leo told the teams from alma mater Villanova and fellow Catholic university Notre Dame that in matters of sport, the pontiff was neutral.

Then the pope, who was born Robert Prevost, said his former self might disagree.

“Prevost has another opinion, but we won’t do that now,” he said to laughs during a whooping, cheering audience of 7,000 people from both schools — players, coaches, fans and their families — in the Vatican audience hall.

Inside the basketball arena, many Villanova fans wore Wildcats jerseys featuring the name of “Pope Leo” and a “XIV” for his number.

Leo graduated in 1977 with a Bachelor of Science in mathematics from Villanova, the Augustinian school near Philadelphia. He was born in Chicago — not all that far from Notre Dame, which is located in South Bend, Indiana.

Villanova fans also held aloft a banner featuring Pope Leo depicted wearing a Villanova jersey reaching out to the university's president, the Rev. Peter M. Donohue, in a playful scene reminiscent of Michelangelo’s fresco in the Sistine Chapel.

“We just had a (tough) loss, but this has been a phenomenal experience, a once-in-a-lifetime experience,” Villanova men's coach Kevin Willard said.

“To see (the pope's) love for Villanova. To see what he’s done for the Catholic Church and really for people all over, it was, I don’t have the words to be perfectly honest with you, that’s how special it was. And we’re just blessed that it happened,” Willard added.

The games were played at the 11,000-seat Palazzo dello Sport, which is located about a half-hour drive from the Vatican. Cardinal Peter Turkson of Ghana, who was considered a candidate for pope until Leo was elected last year, was at the arena. So was Sister Raffaella Petrini, president of the Vatican City state.

The schools also brought their team chaplains to Rome.

The games were played on All Saints’ Day — a major Catholic holiday.

Before tipoff, there was a moment of prayer and the U.S. and Italian national anthems were sung.
