News.title: Alexis Mac Allister labelled ‘embarrassing’ after trying to get Arsenal man sent off
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Alexis Mac Allister was labelled as “embarrassing” after trying to get Noni Madueke sent off during Arsenal’s win over Liverpool.

Mikel Arteta’s side went to the top of the Premier League after beating Liverpool 1-0 courtesy of Kai Havertz’s early strike, marking their first triumph at Anfield since 2012.

Liverpool threw everything at Arsenal in an attempt to find an equaliser, and frustration boiled over late on when a scuffle broke out between Reds midfielder Mac Allister and a number of Gunners players.

After Mac Allister appeared to shout at a downed Arsenal captain Martin Odegaard before slapping the back of his head, he was confronted by Jurrien Timber as other players from both sides began surrounding.

Mac Allister then went down dramatically following contact between his head and Madueke’s, something which sparked red card appeals from the Liverpool players.

Replays showed that there was no thrust or intent indicative of a head-butt from Madueke, who was already on a yellow card, and co-commentator Gary Neville lambasted Mac Allister for his reaction.

"I don't think Mac Allister needs to go down like that but there's a little nudge with the head. A little inch forward can cost you a lot,” he said on Sky Sports.

"Mac Allister's reaction is a bit over the top, I can tell you that. Get up. Embarrassing.

"It's Mac Allister's fault because he slaps Odegaard when he's down which is unnecessary.

"It's the little movement forward of Madueke's head they're looking at. I hope they don't go for a red card for it."

open image in gallery Alexis Mac Allister was labelled ‘embarrassing’ by Gary Neville ( Getty )

VAR examined the incident closely but decided against recommending a red card for Madueke, taking the review no further.

"Well done to VAR because they're recognised that Mac Allister going down is embarrassing,” he said. "He [VAR Stuart Attwell] said that [to Madley], but in a posher way.”

Mac Allister, meanwhile, was shown a yellow card, as was Timber for his part in the confrontation.

Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola said he felt the incident did not warrant a red card for Madueke.

"I've just seen one replay,” he said. “I think a red card has to be more clear movement. It didn't look like a clear red card, no.”

After the match, former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher echoed Neville’s sentiment on the outcome of the incident.

"I want Liverpool to win the game, but I'm delighted he [Madueke] didn't get sent off,” he said. “We have really got to be calling people out and saying 'this is embarrassing'.

"It's ridiculous and it's got to stop. I can't stand it. If someone puts their head back and butts, then red card. But if it's head-to-head and they touch, the other one goes down and the player gets sent off, as a game, call your own people out on it.

open image in gallery Mac Allister and Jurrien Timber were booked ( Reuters )

"It's a joke from Mac Allister and it's got to stop. People are trying to gain an advantage because they can and red cards are being given for it. Whether it's Howard Webb, the Premier League, the managers getting together, this has got to stop."

Daniel Sturridge, another former Reds player turned pundit, also weighed in on Mac Allister’s reaction, saying: "He doesn't headbutt him with any force. It's a coming together and they're both into it.

"He's trying to bait him and that is league wide - that's not just Mac Allister. Every player in world football - that's the game.

"He knew exactly what he was doing and ultimately it didn't work out for him. You tried to bait a man into something and he didn't bite."

Ian Wright added: "The first thing with Mac Allister is the way he goes over. He's actually slapped Odegaard on the back of the head.

"The laws have to do something about this because that [Mac Allister going down] is trying to get someone sent off.

"Common sense prevailed because he [Madueke] didn't push his head into him, he just confronted him and Mac Allister tried to take that advantage to go down."

News.title: Arsenal produce defensive masterclass to end Anfield hoodoo
News.content:
It is clear and obvious that Arsenal will be the team to beat in this season’s Premier League title race, especially given we do not know the fate of faltering Manchester City.

But a statement victory to Liverpool, their first in the league at Anfield since 2012, took Arsenal back to the top. And who would bet against them staying there and retaining their title?

A win would have thrust Liverpool into that race. Instead, under Andoni Iraola, they are already nine points behind after just nine games.

It is also clear and obvious that they should have been prevented that victory with Liverpool somehow denied a first-half penalty after Alexander Isak’s shirt was pulled by Jurrien Timber as the striker tried to head home a cross. Okay, referee Andy Madley may have missed it but what was the excuse of VAR Stuart Attwell? It was a stunning decision.

What is also clear and obvious is that, once again, Arsenal’s resilience, defensive determination and appetite for toughing it out will be their greatest weapons. They are certainly, under Mikel Arteta, not here to win friends.

More to follow...

News.title: Lewis Hamilton becomes oldest driver to claim pole position in 44 years
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for qualifying for the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix from the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez in Mexico City, obviously. The big story this weekend is that Jimi Antonelli is almost certain to become the youngest world champion in Formula One history. To guarantee it he needs just two points, but if George Russell or Lewis Hamilton fail to win here then the title is his whatever he does. It has been a superb, strong and consistent season from the man who began the year as a teenager. He has not quite been faultless, but he has not been far away.

There are other stories floating around the paddock, too. Notably, Esteban Ocon has been dropped by Haas today for final practice, qualifying and the race, to be replaced by reserve driver Ryo Hirakawa for the weekend. Whether Ocon will continue in any other races has yet to be confirmed but you have to say that it seems extremely unlikely. More on that later.

Another line is the ongoing tension between Liam Lawson and Max Verstappen after their crash in FP2 yesterday. It was certainly a strange one in which neither driver backed down, which resulted in contact, debris being strewn across the track and a red flag. Both drivers seemed unrepentant, though admitted it was clumsy. Lawson and Verstappen each receive a one-place grid penalty for the incident, which feels about right given how silly and unnecessary it all was.

But what about the competitive order on track? Since the summer break, and a little before in fairness, things have been unpredictable at the top. Mercedes have still, on average, been the best team but Ferrari, Red Bull and McLaren have all had their moments.

What happened in final practice? It was Lando Norris who topped the timesheets by just 0.001sec ahead of Mercedes’ Antonelli. Charles Leclerc was a further tenth or so back for Ferrari followed by Oscar Piastri in the other McLaren, who was 0.195sec off his team-mate’s pace. Then came Verstappen, Hamilton, Russell, Isack Hadjar, Lawson and Arvid Lindblad. All drivers were within 0.6sec off Norris, which promises a close qualifying session. Let’s hope we get it.

News.title: Suzuki howler costs Aston Villa crucial points
News.content:
Tonight sees a battle between two Spaniards at Villa Park as Aston Villa host Fulham. Both sides are looking to bounce back from disappointing midweeks having been knocked out of the League Cup; Aston Villa lost 3-0 at Bournemouth, while Fulham fell to a 1-0 defeat at home against Crystal Palace.

After a slow start to the season in the league, Aston Villa’s form has picked up, which includes handing Manchester City their first defeat of the season a week ago. After this evening, Aston Villa have games against Barcelona and Manchester United before the international break but Unai Emery has insisted his full focus is on this game.

“If we are thinking after the match against Fulham, then we are making a mistake and we are completely wrong,” Emery said. “We are prioritising the Premier League, and this is the message. To keep our consistency and demands means that each match is a test.”

Having failed to win any of their first six league games, Fulham have now won back-to-back Premier League games, with consecutive 1-0 wins over Hull and Coventry, which has lifted them out of the relegation zone.

“It [managing in England] is a very tough challenge but I am so happy to be here,” Alvaro Arbeloa said. “I am where I want to be and I am really enjoying my days. I want to win games and I think we are performing well but we need to improve.

“They [Aston Villa] are very compact, they defend so well and even with the ball they know what they have to do. And they have top players, and when you have a top coach with top players, normally you have a top team. I think right now he [Unai Emery] is one of the best coaches in the world. He is very, very good, he improves everything every year. It does not matter where he is coaching, he is doing an amazing job, and for me also it is a very good challenge to face him.”

In the two league meetings between these sides last season, it was one win apiece; Aston Villa won this fixture 3-1 just over a year ago before Fulham won 1-0 at Craven Cottage back in April. Team news from Villa Park to follow shortly.

News.title: Alex Mitchell injury blow for England but Northampton dig deep to win
News.content:
England were dealt a fresh blow ahead of their Nations Championship opener with Australia after scrum-half Alex Mitchell was forced off early in Northampton’s victory over Gloucester.

Mitchell left the field gingerly 20 minutes into the action after picking up a suspected hamstring injury following an innocuous coming-together with Gloucester winger Will Joseph.

The Saints scrum-half has suffered a series of hamstring issues this year – this would be a fourth time he has picked up a problem – and he looked visibly disappointed as he limped off.

He suffered a left leg hamstring tear during England’s Six Nations defeat to Ireland which left him sidelined for two months and, in a cruel twist of fate, sustained another on his right leg during an England three-day training camp in Bagshot last May. He suffered the injury for a third time in England’s 73-8 rout of Fiji in July.

With Mitchell’s club-mate, Archie McParland, nursing an unspecified knock that forced him to miss Saints’ high-stakes clash with Gloucester, Jack van Poortvliet is likely to start at nine against the Wallabies next Sunday. McParland was the third-choice scrum-half in England’s Nations Championship squad, but Steve Borthwick may be forced to look elsewhere if Mitchell’s prognosis is serious.

News.title: Spurs win three in row for first time in 616 days to pile pressure on Sage
News.content:
Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League encounter between Tottenham and Crystal Palace.

Last weekend, Spurs enjoyed a historic result, beating Chelsea 2-0 at Stamford Bridge for only the second time in the league for 36 years thanks to Mike Penders’ own goal and Mathys Tel’s stunning solo strike. This result, coupled with the 3-1 victory over Coventry City in their previous home outing, means that Tottenham have won back-to-back league games and are beginning to gather some momentum under Roberto De Zerbi.

In his pre-match press conference, when asked if he’s felt a change in atmosphere after the triumph at Stamford Bridge, De Zerbi replied: “We have not achieved our goal. We want our fans to be happy, not now, at the end of the season. Now we have to push, we have to stay focused, we have to increase the spirit, the appetite to win games in a row. To do that, we have to show if we are good enough. If we are good enough on the pitch, for sure we are ready. In the head, in the mentality, we have to show, because the step of this club is to win games in a row and to be angry day by day, game by game, win by win. One time or two times are not enough.”

Palace have endured a tricky and inconsistent start to the season under their summer appointment Pierre Sage, accumulating just seven points from their opening seven league matches while shipping 17 goals. The 1-0 League Cup victory over Fulham in midweek has momentarily eased the pressure on the Frenchman, but given their newfound success in recent campaigns, fan expectations have risen, with recent performances prompting some cause for concern.

Tottenham remain without the suspended Rodrigo Bentancur, while Xavi Simons, Wilson Odobert, Lucas Bergvall, Savio, Tosin Adarabioyo and Mykhaylo Mudryk are out injured. James Maddison was substituted early in the second half at Chelsea with an apparent groin strain, but De Zerbi insists he’s available for this one. Destiny Udogie could also be involved after recovering from a knee issue.

News.title: Brighton underline title credentials with impressive win over Man City
News.content:
This Brighton and Hove Albion title challenge – as it must now be classed – flies in the face of the saying that money always talks in football. Manchester City have been found guilty of breaching financial rules and also fielded the most expensive midfield in Premier League history here, yet the match-winners cost a fraction in comparison.

Looking at Brighton’s winning goal, it was created by a cross that flashed across the City goal from Diego Gómez, an £11m signing who was playing in Major League Soccer in the United States not so long ago. Maxim de Cuyper, a £17.5m arrival from Club Brugge, was credited with the assist after Yasin Ayari tapped in.

Ayari cost £3.5m from Swedish club AIK and scored in the 5-0 wins over Coventry and Palace, and now has this winner to add to his collection. The 23-year-old is another example of Brighton polishing these gems and putting them together in a team that can win against any opponent in the Premier League.

News.title: Man Utd the masters of self-destruction as pressure piles on Carrick
News.content:
The strange thing is this could and probably should have been a day when they at least stopped the rot for a few days. But more non-existent defending and brainlessness from Martinez, who was sent off for planting an elbow in Wesley Fofana’s face, put paid to that in a second half in which Carrick admitted United “unravelled”.

Chelsea were cut open on at least five occasions in a see-saw first half and Matheus Cunha also had a goal disallowed for a narrow offside. Xabi Alonso’s side had opportunities of their own – you will always get them against this United team – but they were second best and lucky not to be behind. Everyone talks about United being there for the taking, but the truth is Chelsea, coming off the back of a miserable defeat to Spurs and Carabao Cup exit to Liverpool, were here.

The problem is Carrick’s team could not hit a barn door at the moment. They have scored just three goals in their last six league games and that lack of cutting edge was evident in the way Bruno Fernandes, back in the team as captain, and Amad Diallo (dangerous but with no end product) wasted excellent chances. That wastefulness would put pressure on any back line, let alone one with all the fortitude of wet cardboard. Chelsea were spared and exploited it with the help of the second and most corrosive acts of United’s self-mutilation.

We will come to Martinez’s sending off in a moment, but there had already been a cowardly act of a different kind from the Argentine defender before then in the lead-up to Chelsea’s opening goal soon after the restart.

Take nothing away from Morgan Rogers – his 40yd dash from the edge of the centre circle in United’s half to the six-yard box and the finish that followed were top notch. But where was the challenge? How could not a single player in red have stood in his path? “Come on Morgan, run through us buddy” seemed to be the message.

News.title: Red Roses cruise to dominant victory over United States in final WXV game
News.content:
English rugby chiefs have been on a charm offensive in the United States this week, but the players on the pitch opted for more of a brute-force approach.

The Red Roses were in the unfamiliar position of coming off the back of successive defeats and Meg Jones had called on her team to respond. They certainly did that, looking far more like world champions than they have over the past fortnight with a convincing nine-try win – four of them scored by Claudia Moloney-MacDonald – albeit there is still room for them to “grow”, as Jones put it after the game.

That is what the Rugby Football Union (RFU) have been trying to do off the field. Bill Sweeney, the RFU chief executive, and his colleagues used this fixture in New Jersey as an opportunity to tap into the US market by “creating connections” with business leaders and potential investors.

It is little wonder English rugby is trying to get a piece of the American pie. There are an ever-growing number of US owners in British football and with the US hosting the men’s and women’s Rugby World Cups in 2031 and 2033 interest in the oval-ball game is sure to grow too, although the sparse crowd in New Jersey would suggest there is work to do on that front.

Sports.title: Three points from Arsenal’s win at Liverpool, including Saliba’s Konsa issue, Rice’s remedy and tactical dilemma
Sports.content:
Next

ARSENAL secured a huge win against Liverpool on the road to leap to the top of the Premier League table.

Mikel Arteta‘s men took the lead through Kai Havertz in the early stages of the match before weathering a barrage of Reds pressure to protect their three points.



A number of Gunners stars stood out in the thrilling clash at Anfield, but that is not to say there were not signs to learn and improve upon as the season rumbles on.

SunSport’s Simon Collings singled out three things we learned from Arsenal‘s triumph on Merseyside…



KONSA-QUENCES

The defence was at the heart of Arsenal‘s performance as they stole all three points at Anfield for the first time in 14 years.

Ezri Konsa put in a stunning performance alongside Gabriel at the base of the back four as he continues to build on his impressive catalogue of showings since joining from Aston Villa in the summer.

William Saliba is potentially set to make his return to contention in the coming weeks, and could be available for selection as early as after the November international break.

But the Frenchman faces a fight if he wants to reclaim his spot in the starting line-up.

Konsa has built up his relationship with his defensive partner this season, and deciding whether to split them up may prove a real dilemma for Arteta in the near future.

THINK RICE

Declan Rice continued to impress in midfield as he put the ball on a plate for Havertz at the back post to give the Gunners an early lead.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

That made it five assists for the season so far for Rice, who is adding a creative spark to his repertoire of skills this campaign.

But the impactful showing comes on the back of him receiving a rest in the midweek.

The quality of his performance at Anfield is proof that Arteta will have to carefully manage his minutes going forward this season so he can make the difference in the biggest clashes.

RACE FOR PACE

But while the back line and the midfield shone, there was a glaring issue at the other end of the pitch.



Liverpool had the visitors pinned back for large spells in the second half, but Arsenal lacked the pace up front to provide a danger on the counter attack.

The absence was especially stark watching the likes of Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak bombing down the channels for the hosts when they regained possession.

Arsenal were unable to exploit the space behind Liverpool’s back line when they cranked up the pressure in the defensive third, but a pace injection in the January window could make them a real danger on the counter.

Sports.title: Arsenal player ratings: Christos Tzolis shrugs off rusty start on injury return as Declan Rice leads charge vs Liverpool
Sports.content:
Next

ARSENAL beat Liverpool to claim their first win at Anfield in the Premier League for 14 YEARS.

Kai Havertz scored the only goal of the game after tapping home a cross from Declan Rice in the 16th minute.



Liverpool battled back well, with Florian Wirtz hitting the crossbar and Alexander Isak having a penalty shout waved away.

The Gunners held on for the win, though, to move top of the Premier League and three points clear of Manchester City.



Here’s how SunSport’s Simon Collings rated the Arsenal players:

David Raya – 7



Under pressure in the first half as Liverpool put countless crosses into the box.

Looked solid and his distribution was largely effective, too. Saved by the crossbar after Florian Wirtz’s wicked free-kick beat him.

Jurrien Timber – 7

Got the nod over Ben White as he started just his second Premier League game this season.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

A bit off the pace early on and was lucky not to give away a penalty after pulling Isak’s shirt in the box. Much better in the second half and made a few vital blocks.

Ezri Konsa – 9

Made an error early on that gifted Liverpool a chance, but he bounced back so well.

Continues to be an utter rock at the back in the absence of William Saliba. Helped Arsenal weather the Anfield storm. A monster showing.



Gabriel – 8

So often the Brazilian is tormented by Isak, but he dealt with him well on this occasion.

Led the defence impressively when the Gunners were rocking towards the end of the first half.



Riccardo Calafiori – 7

Fit to start after struggling with hip pain last week. Could not get forward as much as he usually would because Arsenal were penned in at times.

Nearly created a second goal for Havertz with a great run and cross, though.



Declan Rice – 8

Arsenal needed their big players to step up – and the England star delivered.



Covered so much ground and created Havertz’s goal to move on to five assists for the season. A beast in the heart of midfield.

Bruno Guimaraes – 6

Had a slow start to the game, but came alive during the first half with a crunching tackle that he celebrated in front of the away fans.

Went close with a deflected strike, too, but was hooked with about 30 minutes to go.



Noni Madueke – 6

Shook off an ankle knock to start and helped create Havertz’s goal by combining with Rice down the right flank.

Almost got Arsenal a second by getting onto Tzolis’ cross. Struggled a bit out of possession with Milos Kerkez bombing forward from left-back.

Martin Odegaard – 7

Was at the heart of Arsenal’s good start and his pressing helped win the ball for the move that led to Havertz scoring.



Faded towards the end of the first half, but better after the break as the Gunners got some control back.

Christos Tzolis – 6

Straight into the team after missing Arsenal’s previous six games due to injury.



Looked understandably a little rusty in the early stages. However, he got better as the game wore on and was denied a goal by a brilliant save from Alisson.

Kai Havertz – 7

Bounced back from a woeful performance at Fleetwood by opening the scoring.

Had a tough afternoon up against Jeremy Jacquet and Virgil van Dijk, and the German largely fed off scraps. Arsenal’s hero, nonetheless.

Subs

Myles Lewis-Skelly (Guimaraes 62’) – 6



Unlucky not to start given his performances this season. Tried to give Arsenal some control and slowed the game down with some smart fouls.

Piero Hincapie (Tzolis 84’) – N/A

Viktor Gyokeres (Havertz 84’) – N/A

Sports.title: I just don’t understand how VAR cleared that, says ex-Prem ref after major blunder in Arsenal’s win over Liverpool
Sports.content:
Next

WHAT a pulsating first half we saw as Liverpool locked horns with Arsenal at Anfield.

And what an advert it was for the Premier League as the Gunners went on to notch a narrow 1-0 win.



But the first half was incident-packed – and you can argue that Liverpool midfielder Trey Nyoni’s challenges on Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz could have resulted in two yellow cards.

I think it’s subjective. The first one is definitely a yellow card for a reckless challenge on Arsenal skipper Odegaard.



Would Nyoni have committed the second challenge had he already been cautioned? That’s hard to judge.

Then, obviously, Liverpool had a couple of penalty shouts in the first half.



I think the first one – Christos Tzolis on Cody Gakpo – wasn’t enough for a spot-kick.

But the one we saw with Jurrien Timber, when he clearly pulled the shirt of Alexander Isak, is a clear penalty for me.

And I just don’t understand how VAR cleared that and didn’t recommend a review to referee Andy Madley.

If Timber doesn’t pull Isak’s shirt, the Liverpool striker is getting to the ball.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

I was just amazed that VAR never got involved in that incident.

Arsenal ended up profiting from the situation as they went on to bag all three points and move clear at the top of the Premier League.

Havertz grabbed the only goal of the clash during the action-packed first half.

There was also a flashpoint in the final stages as Alexis Mac Allister sparked a huge bust-up.

Sports.title: Liverpool 0 Arsenal 1: Kai Havertz fires champions top of Premier League table and finally ends 14-YEAR Anfield hoodoo
Sports.content:
Next

MIKEL ARTETA featured in the heart of the midfield the last time Arsenal won at Anfield.

But 14 years later, Arteta celebrated a far more important victory with the reigning champions asserting their authority back at the top of the Premier League.



Arsenal’s fans were able to drive down the M6, reflecting on a win that will have major repercussions for the rest of the season.

It was hard-fought and slightly lucky. It was also proof it will now take a monumental effort from another club to knock the champions off their perch.



It would not even be a surprise if Arsenal, after this defensive masterclass, keep their spot at the top for the rest of the season.

Kai Havertz struck the winner in a breathless chaotic game which saw Liverpool denied a penalty when VAR failed to intervene after Alexander Isak was clearly fouled by Jurrien Timber.



But ultimately, even though Liverpool played really well, they failed to seriously test Arsenal keeper David Raya.

At a time when Manchester City have started to wobble, Arsenal have sorted themselves out after their blip away to Brighton.

Maybe Brighton can deliver a proper challenge. With City likely to suffer a points deduction, Liverpool are surely the only other team who can stop Arsenal but they fell short.

Ultimately, Isak knows he should have thrown himself to the floor in the first half after being fouled by Timber but he remained on his feet, simply because he was trying to do the right thing and reach the ball.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Had Liverpool levelled for 1-1, maybe it would have been different. In the end, the Reds were desperate and Alexis Mac Allister embarrassed himself by trying to get Noni Madueke sent off for a headbutt.

At least VAR got this one right as there was no force in the movement of Madueke’s head.

With City’s future uncertain, Chelsea still a work in progress and Manchester United doing their best to get relegated, it does look as though Liverpool-Arsenal will be the main Premier League rivalry over the next couple of years.

This was a compelling, physical contest which underlined that Liverpool are a much better team under Andoni Iraola while it also proved that Arsenal’s defence – even without the injured William Saliba – is even better.

Teenager Trey Nyoni made his mark 50 seconds into his full Premier League derby by raking the studs down the ankle of Martin Odegaard.



He was not only extremely lucky to avoid a caution on that occasion but also 10 minutes later when he left his foot on Havertz.

The Arsenal striker then fell to the floor holding his face after a meaty challenge from Virgil van Dijk yet the German was able to land the first, proper blow of the game by scoring the opening goal.

Martin Odegaard pressed high to win possession after a loose pass out from the back by Alisson. Bruno Guimaraes and Noni Madueke combined to shift the ball out to the overlapping Rice on the right and he delivered a sensational, precise, daisy cutter which whizzed across the area and fell perfectly to Havertz at the far post who was never going to miss.



After enjoying complete control, Arsenal were forced to buckle down and sustain all sorts of pressure. Crucially, they also enjoyed that bit of good fortune any team needs in a big game with that controversial first half decision.

Isak, with good reason, complained that he was having his shirt pulled by Jurrien Timber as he moved to reach a cross from Rio Ngumoha. It was still remarkable that VAR did not intervene.

The lucky Timber, making only his second Premier League start of the season, then stopped a certain goal at the other end by accidentally getting in the way when Madueke attempted to hook the ball back to Havertz to score.



Yet that was a rare Arsenal attack and Arteta’s team were thankful to hear Andy Madley’s half-time whistle.

Liverpool’s 28 touches in the opposition box were the most on record – so since 2008-09 – by any side in the first half of a Premier League game against Arsenal

Florian Wirtz hammered a free-kick against the crossbar while Alexis Mac Allister was left in a state of disbelief when he somehow headed Milos Kerkez’s cross into the Anfield Road End.



Unfortunately for Reds boss Iraola, his team could not match the intensity of the first half as they attacked the Kop although Arsenal’s back four were excellent.

Christos Tzolis, playing his first game in a month, forced a cracking save from Alisson in a rare Arsenal attack with the Gunners not showing too much menace in the final third.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Viktor Gyokeres replaced Havertz but he continues to look for his first Premier League goal.

While Arsenal fans are still worrying about their lack of firepower, it will be the defence that could help the club retain the title, as they proved at Anfield.

Sports.title: Mac Allister sparks huge bust-up as he falls to ground after SCREAMING in Odegaard’s face during Liverpool vs Arsenal
Sports.content:
Next

ALEXIS MAC ALLISTER kicked off a fiery sequence against Arsenal after he screamed down at a floored Martin Odegaard.

The Argentina midfielder was featuring for Liverpool as they looked to claw back a leveller at Anfield.



But the occasion seemed to get the better of him when he fouled the Arsenal captain, before leaning down over the injured star and screaming at him.

He then gently tapped the back of his opponent’s head before moving away.



Gunners defender Jurrien Timber took issue with the questionable antics and followed Mac Allister to give him a piece of his mind, prompting a number of players on both sides to rush to the site of the confrontation.

One such star was winger Noni Madueke, who carved his way through the brawl to get face to face with Liverpool’s No10.

Perhaps a bit too literally, however, as he pushed his head forward until it made contact with Mac Allister’s head.

The contact looked to be negligible, but the 27-year-old apparently felt differently as he theatrically tumbled to the floor holding his face.

Madueke could only awkwardly grin at the bizarre scene, while Declan Rice took the opportunity to lean down and give Mac Allister some harsh words as he had previously done to Odegaard.

VAR dutifully took a look at the incident, but decided that it did not meet the harsh threshold for violent conduct when it comes to head-to-head contact.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

The scuffle eventually calmed down, with Mac Allister and Timber both shown yellow cards for their respective roles in the chaos.

Madueke was already on a caution at the time of the confrontation, but his conduct was not deemed worthy of a second yellow by referee Andy Madley.

The entire scenario wasted precious minutes for Liverpool as they attempted to rescue an important point at home.



But the defending Prem champions proved too rigid to break down, and walked away with all three points to send them to the top of the table.

Sports.title: Fans left stunned as Premier League legend, 40, spotted running in New York Marathon just months after retiring
Sports.content:
Next

PREMIER LEAGUE fans were shocked to see an icon of the English game running in the New York Marathon.

The iconic race tested the skills of around 60,000 people this year, from elite long-distance runners to everyday runners looking to get involved for good causes.

And among them during the race on Sunday was former Liverpool and Manchester City star James Milner.



The Prem veteran hung up the boots at the end of last season after breaking the league’s appearance record.



But he wasted no time getting into training for a new challenge as he took on the marathon aged 40.

The 26-mile course took Milner around New York’s five boroughs, finishing in Central Park, Manhattan.

A number of surprised fans noticed the star running the race, wearing a neon yellow vest as he whizzed round the course.

According to the New York Road Runners tracking app, Milner averaged 7:13min/mile on his way to a total finish time of three hours, nine minutes and four seconds.

The athlete revealed ahead of the run that he has been in training using an AI model, claiming he bounced ideas off of the computer while taking part in three or four runs a week.

But when asked if he had a target time in mind, the ex-Brighton star said he was happy to take the race as it comes.

CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS



He told LetsRun.com: “A few years ago, I feel like I could have definitely done sub-3:00. My career went on longer and longer.

“Two years ago, I had a knee operation, and when I woke up from the knee operation, I couldn’t lift my foot. And I had a second operation that day to check, and then I couldn’t lift my foot for six months. I had nerve damage.

“So I feel to go from not being able to walk properly and maybe never being able to walk to coming back, playing football in the Premier League, and hopefully potentially finishing a marathon, I don’t want to get too much caught up on the time.

“Obviously, I’m a competitive guy and I want to do well, but I feel like after going through that and the miles I’ve got on the clock playing football for a very long time



“So [my goal is] to just enjoy it and finish it, because New York’s such a special place to do my first marathon here, and 50th anniversary [of the five-borough marathon] as well. That’s pretty special on this course.”

Sports.title: Erik ten Hag says Man Utd could be RELEGATED and warns Michael Carrick about ‘vicious circle’
Sports.content:
Next

ERIK TEN HAG has warned Manchester United could be relegated after slipping to 17th in the table.

Chelsea’s 2-0 win over Michael Carrick‘s side on Saturday saw them slip to a ninth game without a win, and left them teetering perilously over the relegation zone.



Relegation is not something that would usually be in the thoughts of Man Utd chiefs and fans, but Ten Hag, who won the Carabao Cup and FA Cup with the club, has warned it is a very real possibility.

He also warned the club about a “vicious circle” they can be caught in, and based on the evidence of this season they have already fallen foul of it.



Speaking to ESPN NL’s Goedemorgen Eredivisie, the Dutchman said: “In the Premier League it’s certainly possible, because all the teams are simply strong.

“They’re all strong squads, all good managers.



“And if you end up on the wrong side once and you really get into that vicious circle — yes, then it can become very, very difficult.”

United could have dropped into the bottom three over the weekend, but Crystal Palace, Nottingham Forest and Sunderland all failed to win to go ahead of the Red Devils.

Carrick has reportedly been given until at least the international break to turn results around, but the dismal defeat in London wasn’t the best start to repaying that blind faith.

United have failed to win any of their first seven away games in all competitions for the first time since 1973-74, a season they were relegated.

Regardless, Ten Hag reflects on his time at Old Trafford with positivity.

He said: “I think we performed pretty well with United. I think we had performed more than pretty well. We couldn’t have done it better.

Sports.title: Title winner, 34, training ‘five times a week’ to become an MMA fighter just months after retiring from football
Sports.content:

DIEGO DEMME has made the shock decision to switch sports – just months after hanging up his boots.

The former defensive midfielder, 34, got his hands on the Serie A title during a four-year spell with Napoli.



But Demme has made the stunning move into MMA following his retirement from football at the end of last season.

And the ex-Germany international is already seeing the benefits after training up to five times a week at the Berlin-based Choke Athletics.



Demme told Bild: “At the beginning, I really got my butt kicked because it’s a completely different kind of strain.

“I couldn’t get out of my opponents’ holds and my arms were sore from all the gripping.

“Recently, I had my first class where no one tapped me. That was awesome.

“I’m slowly getting ready to join the evening class, where the intermediate to advanced students practice grappling.”

But Demme – who counts the likes of Paderborn, RB Leipzig and Hertha Berlin among his former clubs – does not plan to become a professional cage fighter.

The Coppa Italia winner added: “That’s not my goal with this course. It’s a reassuring feeling to know that you would be able to help others or yourself even better in an emergency situation.”



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Demme’s sensational improvement in the cage has stunned personal trainer Saman Darvish.

The head coach of the MMA gym, 41, said: “Diego has been with me for four to five weeks.

“He’s doing exceptionally well, learning rapidly, and is very physically resilient.

“Even during warm-ups, you can tell that a professional is at work. His willpower and tenacity are remarkable.



“This is likely related to his great ambition and his professional background in sports. Likewise, his enormous stamina.

Sports.title: Sale secures Grand Final title and Brown crowned Road to Mallorca No 1
Sports.content:
Julien Sale produced a dominant final round to secure victory at the HotelPlanner Tour’s Grand Final, while Hamish Brown topped the Road to Mallorca rankings.

Frenchman Sale, who was guaranteed promotion to the DP World Tour before the season finale in Mallorca, posted his second 65 of the week to reach 22 under par, four strokes clear of the Brown, who narrowly held onto solo second to capture the season-long title.

Sale ends the year second in the rankings and will now step up to golf's DP World Tour for the first time in his career.

He becomes the fifth player from France to win the Grand Final after Clément Sordet (2017), Benjamin Hebert (2014), Mike Lorenzo-Vera (2007) and Nicolas Joakimides (1997).

Image: Hamish Brown (left) and Julien Sale (right) celebrate successes at the HotelPlanner Tour Grand Final

The 29-year-old started the day with a one-stroke advantage and fired four front-nine birdies to take control at Club de Golf Alcanada.

A gain on the par-five 12th further extended his advantage before he dropped his only shot of the day on the next.

He responded well, however, with three birdies in his final six holes helping him to his second HotelPlanner Tour triumph of 2026, after his win on home soil at the Le Vaudreuil Golf Challenge earlier this year.

He said: "Coming this week, I didn't have much stress because I knew I was inside the top 15 and the goal was to win the tournament and obviously try to finish number one on the ranking.

"I was going to have fun already tonight but now I'm going to enjoy it even more with my family here."

Sports.title: Arsenal win at Anfield for first time in 14 years to move top
Sports.content:
Arsenal won at Anfield for the first time in 14 years after Kai Havertz's strike sealed a gritty 1-0 victory - but Liverpool were denied what looked to be a clear penalty.

The result opens up a three-point gap on Manchester City at the top of the Premier League - and means Mikel Arteta's side are nine clear of Liverpool.

In a battle of attrition, the only discernible difference was at the top end. Liverpool's various waves of pressure almost always led to an effort on David Raya's goal - 17 in total - but none actually forced the goalkeeper into a save.

Florian Wirtz hit the crossbar with a free-kick and Alexis Mac Allister ballooned a header over the bar unmarked, but Andoni Iraola's side failed to land a single shot on target at home for the first time on record. "It's been a defensive masterclass from Arsenal," said Gary Neville.

Liverpool have scored just four league goals in five Anfield outings this term.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Declan Rice sends a low cross across the box to the far post, where Kai Havertz delivers the finish to put Arsenal ahead against Liverpool.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Liverpool come close to getting on the scoresheet as a free-kick sees Florian Wirtz smash the ball into the crossbar.

The blunted hosts might have had an opportunity from the penalty spot to change that, but Jurrien Timber's less-than-subtle tug on Alexander Isak's shirt in the first half was not spotted by the officials, prompting Jamie Carragher to tell VAR to "do its job".

For the remainder of the game, Arsenal did theirs. Havertz's decider meant he became the division's top-scoring German with 46 goals in total, overtaking former Man City midfielder Ilkay Gundogan, and made sure his side collected another statement win in defence of their title.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jamie Carragher, Daniel Sturridge and Ian Wright discuss Liverpool's penalty shout as Jurrien Timber pulled Alexander Isak's shirt as the striker attempted to head the ball.

Arsenal in driving seat

Sky Sports' Gary Neville at Anfield:

"It was a defensive masterclass. Iraola will be upset, he'll feel like his team have given everything, but the champions have turned up in a season of uncertainty, sabotaged by the Man City saga.

"They can only do the job they continue to do and that puts them right in the driving seat. What a tough place this is to play football and they've come and conquered it."

Arteta: Winning at Anfield 'better' as a manger

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta:

"It feels better as a manager [to win at Anfield], because it's been such a long time. We really needed it. We're extremely proud, especially because of the conditions we arrive in the game after defeat to Fleetwood. We had to pick ourselves up.

"This is the mission, which we hadn't completed for 14 years. We knew we needed to nail absolutely everything and navigate through periods where we suffer. They create chaos moments. It was very impressive and I'm very happy."

On changing the Anfield record: "I had the feeling, now is the moment, we had to dig deep and have an element of luck at times. We had quality in key moments and we've done it."

Sports.title: Why Man Utd fans continue to stick by Carrick
Sports.content:
The last time Manchester United won a league game, schools were closed for the summer and the transfer window was still open.

When things get this bad, managers can be forgiven for heading straight down the tunnel after another defeat - especially if their side have made their worst start to a season in 40 years.

Michael Carrick did not have to think twice before heading towards the United supporters after the final whistle at Stamford Bridge following Saturday's 2-0 defeat.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from Chelsea’s match against Manchester United in the Premier League

Those fans had not seen their team win for almost two months, but they showed warmth, appreciation and respect for the manager who has overseen a run of nine league games without a win.

No matter how much worse things get, it is difficult to imagine hardcore United fans turning on their manager.

No team has won fewer Premier League games than United this season. Only goal difference is keeping Carrick's side out of the relegation zone.

Make no mistake, on their current trajectory of 0.77 points per game, United are heading for relegation for the first time since 1974. They would end the season with fewer than 30 points, which would almost certainly mean Championship football next season.

Things have got so bad some United fans think relegation would be a blessing in disguise if it forces their owners to sell the club.

So, despite all the doom and gloom, and the damning statistics, why have United fans not turned on their manager?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Gary Neville has his say on the current situation at Manchester United and admits he is finding the poor run of form 'really worrying '

Carrick is one of their own

Carrick is a class act and he still embodies the values United are meant to represent as a club.

Carrick played under Sir Alex Ferguson and is an old-school manager in the sense that he wants to keep everything inside the dressing room. Some fans may want him to rant and rave and show more emotion in public but you are never going to get that from Carrick.

When it comes to the media, United are like Real Madrid and Barcelona. Everything that happens at the club is headline news - especially in the social media age. United fans feel like they are under siege.

Carrick is on their side. He gives very little away when he speaks in public. He wears his club suit with pride and always says what is in the best interests of the club. He never makes it about himself. The clue is in the name: United.

Problems lie beyond the dugout

Changing the manager is not going to fix the long-term problems at the club. United fans know that and that is why they are not going to hound Carrick out and watch him being replaced by another manager who has to operate in the same structure.

United have had seven permanent managers since Ferguson retired in 2013 and, despite varying levels of relative success in cup competitions, none of them has been able to mount a genuine title challenge.

A long list of former United players have now joined fans in arguing that things are not going to get better at United until the club has new owners.

The media are sometimes criticised for not highlighting issues with United's ownership structure but anyone who has time on their hands can go and check old newspapers from 2005.

The vast majority of football reporters and commentators who covered the Glazer family's takeover warned that leveraged buyouts - the acquisition of a company using a high proportion of borrowed money (debt) - should not be allowed in football. Leveraged buyouts of the kind the Glazers used to buy United are no longer allowed in English football. That is no consolation for United fans.

United fans don't traditionally turn on their managers

It seems almost inevitable that Carrick will lose his job and his body language sometimes resembles a man who is resigned to his fate.

If Carrick does go this month, he can walk out of Old Trafford with his head held high - and come back whenever he wants.

United fans are proud of the fact that they have historically not turned on their managers. Fans have become disaffected and disillusioned with the managers who have followed in Ferguson's footsteps but there have been no mutinies.

United supporters of a certain age still remember the lone fan who turned up to Old Trafford with a banner in December 1989 declaring that Ferguson should leave after "three years of excuses".

Ferguson did not say goodbye and the rest is history - including 13 league titles and two European Cups.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Clinton Morrison and Darren Ambrose feel the Manchester United fans kept Michael Carrick in the job as they turned on the players after the Bournemouth loss

Fans don't trust chiefs to make the right calls

When Jim Ratcliffe bought a minority stake in United in 2024, the Glazers agreed to let him take control of football operations.

Erik ten Hag was the manager at the time and despite initial misgivings he was given a contract extension after winning the 2024 FA Cup final. He was sacked and replaced by Ruben Amorim just five months later. Amorim lasted 14 months before he was sacked after he criticised the way the club was being run in a press conference.

Carrick took over in an interim capacity in January and he was given the full-time job in the summer after he led United back into the Champions League with a third-place finish in the Premier League.

The key decision makers below Ratcliffe are chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox, who both used to work at Manchester City.

Highly-respected sporting director Dan Ashworth left in December 2024 after just five months - after spending five months on gardening leave at Newcastle United.

No great clamour for Howe or Nagelsmann

Image: Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann are potential replacements

United's top targets to replace Carrick are former Newcastle and Bournemouth manager Eddie Howe and former Germany and Bayern Munich manager Julian Nagelsmann.

Both of them are strong candidates but United fans do not seem to be that excited by the prospect of either of them taking over.

A clean slate and a fresh start may mean they would be able to get more out of this group of players than Carrick but there are no guarantees in football.

If Unai Emery was available, he would be the favourite to take over but he is doing a great job at Aston Villa and is under contract until 2029.

In any case, swapping Villa for United at this stage of his career would mean dropping down 19 places in the Champions League table and eight places in the Premier League.

Clubs in the Premier League are also duty-bound to act in utmost good faith towards each other, which makes any move for Emery fraught with complications.

Sports.title: Neville: Man Utd stuck in a rut - and it's really worrying
Sports.content:
Gary Neville says Manchester United are stuck in a rut and that a difficult run of fixtures ahead makes for “really worrying” times at Old Trafford.

Saturday's 2-0 defeat at Chelsea extended United's winless run to nine games in all competitions - their longest since 1984 - and puts them at risk of falling into the relegation zone before the next international break.

Head coach Michael Carrick said after the loss at Chelsea that he expects to remain in charge for Tuesday night's Champions League visit of Roma.

Describing United's current predicament, Neville said: "It's very difficult. It feels like the club is stuck in a rut. It's stuck in a rut in terms of results, it's now nine without a win, which is obviously a really horrible run to be in at any point.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sunday Supplement looks at the crisis at Manchester United and whether or not they are realistically in danger of relegation this season, and who is the right man to help them avoid that.

"People will talk about the first half (against Chelsea) and say that there were some good things, and there were. But when things aren't going your way, you've got to be able to dig in.

"You've got to keep your discipline and you've got be able to get through points in a game when your opponents are doing quite well - and Manchester United can't do that right now.

"As soon as they go a goal down they fall to pieces.

"I don't think it's at that stage (where Manchester United are in a relegation battle). I don't think they will end up there, but it's a worry. It's a real depression of results, a depression of performances.

"And they've got difficult games coming up.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Danyal Khan brings the latest update on Michael Carrick's future at Manchester United as they prepare for a vey tough test in the Champions League against Roma.

"Any team that is organised, that's got a combination or two about them, will cause Manchester United problems.

"Roma could do that on Tuesday, Aston Villa next weekend are very organised, [they] know how to play. After that, they come to Anfield.

"There are a lot of big games in front for Manchester United in these next few weeks, but it's really worrying."

Nev: If I played like Martinez, I'd be curled up in a ball

Image: Lisandro Martinez was sent off by referee Peter Bankes after picking up two yellow cards

Neville explained he is distinctly unimpressed by Lisandro Martinez's performances. Martinez was sent off in the loss at Stamford Bridge on just his second start since his extraordinary criticism of the club's hierarchy.

"Lisandro Martinez? That's what I expect from him, to be honest with you," Neville said.

"I said the other week - and you've got to respect hat he is a World Cup winner - but every time I watch him for Manchester United he is at fault for a goal.

"He was at fault for two yesterday. The first goal is solely on him.

"We all give goals away as defenders, but the quantity of goals he gives away is remarkable. And that defence is nowhere near good enough and it falls apart every time it is put under big pressure."

Sports.title: 'This is on Martin' - Sutton blames O'Neill for Celtic struggles
Sports.content:
"It's a lottery waiting for the Celtic team. Who knows what team Martin is going to pick?"

Sky Sports' Chris Sutton did not hold back after his former club fell to a shock 2-0 defeat at Falkirk, insisting he is watching a "team in regression."

Ethan Ross' early goal was added to by Scott Tanser's excellent finish, as Celtic's defensive frailties were exposed once again.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Scott Tanser scored Falkirk's second against Celtic

The defeat leaves Celtic with a record of three wins from their past 10 outings as they failed to extend their four-point lead at the top of the table, with Besiktas next in the Europa League, where they have lost three of three.

"The club and the team are in regression. They're just not a good functioning team at this moment in time," the former Hoops striker said.

"Martin will say they're top of the league but in Europe, they're ahead of a team from an outpost in Azerbaijan or Armenia, but that's it. They've been woeful in Europe.

"Celtic fans, quite rightly, expect more.

Image: stats

"Celtic have had issues all season. It's not a great surprise that Celtic have come to Falkirk and been rolled over.

"They weren't great in the week and I still don't think Martin O'Neill knows his best XI.

"There's not an area of the team or the club that is functioning as it should this season and that's a problem.

"There's this big debate about Shaun Maloney and Mark Fotheringham and their coaching, or is it on Martin?

"This is all on Martin because he employs the coaches and he will ask them to play and train in a certain way.

"It's hard to see how Celtic are actually set up. It's a bit off the cuff - get the ball to Hassan and hope he can do something.

"That's the way it has been essentially all season."

'We're still top of the league'

Image: Martin O'Neill led Celtic to the title after returning last season

The defeat was Celtic's second in the Premiership this season, and followed their 2-2 draw at home to Dundee United.

But for the manager, there is no reason to panic.

"We're still top of the league," O'Neill told Sky Sports at full-time.

"We came from a mile behind last year to win the league. A mile behind on two or three occasions as well too.

"We're still in a decent position at this minute. We've played a lot of football as well.

"I keep out the noise at the end of it all.

"I've managed this team now for about a year, give or take a month or two, and I've managed before.

"Celtic are used to winning, as you can tell by the number of trophies they've won in the last 25 years."

'Where are Celtic going?'

After returning to the club twice last season following the departures of Brendan Rodgers then Wilfried Nancy, Martin O'Neill agreed to take permanent charge in the summer after securing a league and cup double.

Sky Sports' Kris Boyd believes the current run casts doubt over his Parkhead future.

"Celtic have got a team that if they're all functioning - as we saw against Hearts - they can still cause problems to any team in the league.

"But they're not functioning properly.

"There are other managers under severe pressure. There have to be serious questions asked about Martin [O'Neill] now.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Celtic came from behind to draw with Dundee United in midweek

"Last season is over now... and right now, for Celtic to have lost six in the last ten in all competitions still isn't good enough. They're miles off it.

"Overall if you look at Celtic right now, where are they going?

"If you're operating as a top football club, you should already have a list of who your next managers are.

"Celtic haven't a clue what they're doing... the hierarchy will say 'we're still successful, we're still winning', but eventually it catches up with you if you don't have a plan in place."

Sports.title: Borthwick: England must quickly adjust from Prem to Test rugby for Nations Championship
Sports.content:
Steve Borthwick admits England need to bridge the gap between the Prem and Test rugby quickly if they’re to have a successful autumn campaign.

Australia's visit to Allianz Stadium, Twickenham on Sunday marks the start of the second phase of the inaugural Nations Championship. Borthwick knows England will need to raise their standards at the breakdown and in defence if they are to compete successfully.

While the Prem's focus on attack has created some thrilling spectacles, it is inadequate preparation for the battles to come against the Wallabies, Japan and New Zealand.

The only round of Champions Cup action so far this season exposed English clubs to a different level of competition in defence and at the breakdown, as they managed just one win from eight matches.

Referee Christophe Ridley provided assistance in training at last week's camp and also gave presentations to the squad in a bid to accelerate their readiness to take on Australia.

"The contact area in the Prem is different to Test rugby," Borthwick said. "That was exemplified in Europe where the English clubs lost more ball and won back less ball at the breakdown than any other nation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player James Cole, speaks with Borthwick ahead of the Autumn internationals starting with Australia

"The other area is the emphasis and importance placed upon defence. We need to ensure that we make it very, very difficult for the opposition to score.

"One of the challenges is that we are refereed domestically by English referees when internationally, quite clearly, we will never have the English referees, so you need to get used to other interpretations.

"Having that European round pleased me because clearly players needed to be able to adjust. The best players are smart and the best players adjust.

"And I think it's pretty obvious that over the last six to eight months, we haven't adjusted and dealt with moments in the way we want to."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Borthwick reacts to the scuffle between Northampton Saints and Leicester Tigers players which featured England players Henry Pollock and Ollie Chessum

England have amassed 15 yellow cards in their eight Tests so far this year, including four in their most recent outing against Argentina in July. Borthwick believes going on the attack provides the solution to the indiscipline.

"Frankly, we spend too much time defending," he said. "The way the interpretations are right now, as soon as you spend time defending there is likely to be a decision that goes against you.

"There has been an exponential increase in cards given - and not just by us. The vast majority of them are given when defending in your own 22."

England are facing mounting problems at half-back ahead of Monday's squad announcement after Alex Mitchell followed Fin Smith and Archie McParland into the treatment room.

Image: Northampton Saints scrum-half Alex Mitchell is an England injury worry ahead of the Nations Championship after departing early on Saturday

Mitchell has joined his Northampton team-mates in becoming a doubt against Australia after sustaining a hamstring injury in Saturday's 28-14 victory over Gloucester.

Sports.title: Alcaraz waltzes past De Minaur to win Vienna title for first time
Sports.content:
Carlos Alcaraz won his fourth title of an injury-disrupted season as he defeated Alex de Minaur in the Erste Bank Open final in Vienna.

The Spaniard, who missed five months of the year with a wrist issue, powered to a 6-1 6-4 win against world No 10 Minaur in the indoor hard-court event.

World No 3 Alcaraz delivered a high-quality, 97-minute display to overwhelm De Minaur and secure the title without dropping a set across his five matches.

The 23-year-old arrived in Vienna following titles in Doha and Tokyo ‌and completed a perfect 16-0 record at ATP 500 events in ​2026 with another dominant week.

"My team and I know pretty well Alex de Minaur's level," Alcaraz said. "His style is really dangerous. Really flat balls that slip a lot through the court really low. It's really difficult to increase the power that I want to in every shot and every ball.

"He's really fast, so you have to earn every point. You might hit a winner against everybody, except him. I had to be really focused on that, so we knew I had to start the match really focused, increasing my speed, my pace in every shot.

"I tried to be aggressive and show him that if he wants to win, he has to play better [than me], more aggressive, more solid, and be smarter than me.

"I'm just really happy that at the end I found my way, played great, and obviously it has been a really emotional and amazing week for me.

"I learned a lot, to keep going forward, step by step, playing on indoor courts, and trying to gain more confidence playing on this surface."

Alcaraz seized control from the ​opening stages, breaking De Minaur's serve ⁠in the first game and ⁠quickly establishing a double-break advantage as the Australian struggled to deal with his intensity.

The seven-time Grand Slam champion raced through the opening, repeatedly punishing short balls ‌and forcing errors from De Minaur.

Although De Minaur put up greater resistance in the second set and kept pace for long spells, Alcaraz closed out victory and secured his seventh ​consecutive win over his opponent.

Alcaraz, who has already qualified for the season-ending ATP Finals in Turin, will head ​to next week's Paris Masters brimming with confidence.

He takes on Jiri Lehecka or Alex Michelsen in his first match.

De Minaur, meanwhile, will turn ​his attention to Paris as he continues his ​push to qualify for the ATP Finals for a third consecutive year.

Vacherot rallies to beat Lehecka to win Swiss Indoors and clinch a second career title

Valentin Vacherot clinched his second career title after beating Jiri Lehecka 2-6 6-3 6-3 in the Swiss Indoors final on Sunday.

Sports.title: Arsenal hold on for vital win at Liverpool after Kai Havertz’s close-range finish
Sports.content:
It was a game when Arsenal showed their ruthless side and all of the champion knowhow that they accumulated over the course of last season. As they headed back to London, they did so having made a statement. Irrespective of what happens to Manchester City over their financial rule breaches, Arsenal remain the Premier League’s team to beat.

Mikel Arteta was in the Arsenal midfield when the club previously won a league fixture at Anfield; it was back in September 2012, although his memories are a little hazy owing to the concussion that he sustained in a collision with Jordan Henderson.

Arteta has a clear-eyed focus on retaining the league title and this was an occasion to see his hopes surge. Kai Havertz’s first goal in ten appearances proved the difference but, really, the victory was rooted in Arsenal’s capacity to control and frustrate.

When the full-time whistle went, the Liverpool captain, Virgil van Dijk, was booked for sarcastically applauding the referee, Andy Madley. Everybody connected to the club raged at what they perceived as Arsenal’s dark arts. The truth was that Arteta’s team held them at arm’s length with relative comfort.

Liverpool ran out of ideas as their five-match winning streak in all competitions came to a shuddering halt. They provided high energy enjoyment in the first half but fizzled out badly, the invention drying up. Arsenal’s previous trip to the north-west had ended badly on Tuesday night with the Carabao Cup humiliation at Fleetwood. This was much more like it.

Liverpool were in the mood to take no prisoners at the outset, with Trey Nyoni – on his full league debut – snapping into challenges. The 19-year-old’s first action was to leave something on Martin Ødegaard and not long after that, he did the same to Havertz. Nyoni was fortunate to emerge without a yellow card. The Kop teemed with intensity; indignation, too, when they felt that Arsenal’s players were too quick to tumble to ground. And stay down. It was a theme of the day.

The Arsenal breakthrough was a self-inflicted wound from a Liverpool point of view, Alisson trying to be too cute with a short pass out from his area for Jérémy Jacquet. He got the weight and direction of it wrong, Ødegaard pouncing to intercept and from that point, it was just a stunning piece of interplay. Arsenal worked it over and up the right and Declan Rice fizzed over the final ball; low and across the corridor of six-yard box uncertainly. Havertz, a player who needed an easy tap-in, got one.

Liverpool responded with more fire and they might have scored before the interval, Alexis Mac Allister blowing the big chance – a free header from Milos Kerkez’s cross in the 43th minute. Moments earlier, Florian Wirtz had whipped a free-kick from the left-hand side against the crossbar.

Liverpool howled in vain for a penalty on more than one occasion in the first half, most loudly when Jurriën Timber grabbed a fistful of Alexander Isak’s shirt in the 21st minute as the striker tried to reach a Bradley Barcola cross. Timber got away with that one. Barcola was also denied by Rice after a loose Ezri Konsa touch.

View image in fullscreen Alexis Mac Allister clashes with Jurriën Timber as tempers flare. Photograph: Michael Steele/Getty Images

Arsenal flickered on the break. There were a few times in the first half when they flooded men forward and there were possibilities. Havertz narrowly failed to get a touch to a Bruno Guimarães cross-cum-shot while Timber could not react in front of goal when Noni Madueke volleyed a Christos Tzolis cross back from an acute angle.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

At 1-0 up, Arsenal had the game where they wanted it. They backed themselves to keep Liverpool at bay; to frustrate Andoni Iraola and his players; to withstand the hostilities of Anfield. It was about their game management. They have become masters at drawing the sting.

Iraola introduced the fit-again Dominik Szoboszlai for Nyoni on 59 minutes; the youngster was given a tremendous ovation as he departed. Liverpool had to do more in attacking terms and the longer the second half went on, the more assured Arsenal looked. They stifled Liverpool and there remained the feeling that they could land something on the counter.

When Jacquet slipped in the 68th minute, Arsenal went left to Tzolis and he almost teed up Ødegaard – with Alisson out of position. Jacquet got back to make an important intervention. Tzolis also forced an excellent save out of Alisson with a first-time shot for the far corner.

Liverpool struggled to keep a lid on their frustrations. As did the home crowd. There was uproar every time that Arsenal won a free-kick, Mac Allister raging after Ødegaard bought a cheap one towards the end. In the ensuing melee, Mac Allister felt Madueke initiate a touch of foreheads. Which was risky by Madueke given he was on a booking for a foul on Barcola.

Down went Mac Allister, undermining Liverpool’s claim to the moral high ground. Madueke survived. It would have been an awfully soft dismissal. Liverpool huffed and puffed. They never looked like landing a decisive blow.

Sports.title: Hemp strikes back as Manchester City edge out London City Lionesses in thriller
Sports.content:
Goals from Khadija Shaw and Lauren Hemp helped Manchester City to escape from Bromley with three points after a thrilling encounter with London City Lionesses. It was a statement performance from the home team, despite the defeat delivering a blow to any title ambitions they may have been quietly holding on to before kick-off.

The gap between the hosts and the champions is now six points, after Hemp restored City’s lead following Jana Fernández’s equaliser. But that London City had even played their way into conversations about this season’s title contenders in their second season has been impressive.

Andrée Jeglertz, the Manchester City manager, praised the ability of his team to win in different ways as needed, after three games in eight days. “We said afterwards, the players should be so proud of what they put into this game,” he said.

“We’ve learned we’re a great team who can keep the ball for 75% of the game and win that way, or we can win like this. That quality to win in different ways is good to have, but the players also have to adapt to that and feel it’s OK to not have the ball all the time, take pride in defending and only having three or four chances but finishing off those chances.”

Before kick-off, cameras showed London City’s superstar summer signing Alexia Putellas opening the boot of her car and taking out a heavy leather-clad square item, her third Ballon d’Or safely encased inside. The Spain midfielder did not present her trophy to fans in the stands before kick-off, instead choosing to put it on display so supporters could queue to have their photo taken with it.

The only nod to the player’s stunning individual year, in which she won the quadruple with Barcelona before joining London City, was on her feet, the geometric gold on her custom Ballon d’Or-themed boots glinting on their first outing.

There have been jokes aplenty about the unlikelihood of the world’s premier individual award heading to its new Bromley home. To reach the stadium from Hayes Lane, you pass a field of horses on your left. London City Lionesses are not Barcelona, and they have become the home of the Ballon d’Or winner by default rather than being the key component of that individual success.

Except, based on the season London City are having and the ruthless ambitions of the owner, Michelle Kang, the idea that the club could produce a season that delivers them collective success and individual success off the back of it feels less distant than it did just a few short months ago.

Against the champions, London City more than held their own, the opportunity to move level on points with their opponents and league leaders Chelsea an inviting incentive. Their threat was evident within 30 seconds, when the Manchester City defender Rebecca Knaak was forced to turn Lucía Corrales’s cross wide of the far post just ahead of a waiting Isobel Goodwin.

Neither team has impressed defensively this season, each only managing to keep one clean sheet in the Women’s Super League, and it made for a thrilling encounter, the high lines and aggressiveness of both attacks delivering a showstopper.

Making her first WSL start for the home team, with Elene Lete hitherto preferred, Mary Earps made a huge statement with an impressive double save from a Knaak header to keep the game goalless going into the break.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Mary Earps dives at the feet of Manchester City’s Khadija Shaw. Photograph: Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty Images

City broke the deadlock despite London City dominating and it was their most influential player who delivered. Hemp flicked the ball into the run of Shaw and with her first touch, she took it past Earps before she switched the ball on to her right foot and fired in to become just the third player to score in eight consecutive WSL starts.

A deserved equaliser arrived in the 72nd minute, when Fernández was at the near post to meet a corner and her assured header sent the ball looping in at the back post.

The celebrations were emphatic but they were short-lived. This is a new, more resilient Manchester City, one that survived various scares last term to secure a second WSL title, and they re-established their lead two minutes later, when Hemp stretched out a leg to poke in Mary Fowler’s cross from the right to secure the win.

That London City could feel aggrieved at having not taken something from the game was a testament to their performance and how quickly progress is being made. The home team had 23 shots to City’s seven and 52 touches in the opposition box to City’s 13, but critically the visiting team were clinical when it mattered. Converting two of their three efforts on target and showing the edge needed to battle at the top.

Sports.title: European football: Mbappé penalty helps Real Madrid stroll to sixth straight win
Sports.content:
Kylian Mbappé moved on from a tumultuous week by scoring a penalty to help Real Madrid win 3-0 at Racing Santander on Sunday.

The French forward narrowly lost out on the Ballon d’Or to Bayern Munich’s Harry Kane on Monday and then had to apologise after a social media storm following a video in which he joked about the former Chinese leader Mao Zedong.

Real Madrid’s match, along with other Spanish fixtures this weekend, was not broadcast by Chinese state television because of the fallout.

Jude Bellingham and Yan Diomandé were also on target to keep third-placed Madrid within three points of the La Liga leaders, Barcelona, who thrashed Alavés 6-1 on Saturday.

José Mourinho’s side have won six straight games across all competitions and are a point behind Atlético Madrid, who beat Levante 2-0.

Gennaro Gattuso’s Lazio consolidated their position at the top of Serie A with a 2-1 victory over Cagliari, nudging ahead of Inter Milan after the two clubs had started the weekend level on points.

Lazio made a poor start as Cagliari took the lead through M’Bala Nzola in the 20th minute before goals in either half from Gustav Isaksen and Andrea Pinamonti gave them a sixth straight Serie A win.

Como moved back into the top four as they eked out a 1-0 victory at home over bottom side Venezia on Sunday for a fifth consecutive victory across all competitions.

The hosts dominated, but needed a penalty to find the back of the net. The Como captain, Lucas Da Cunha, converted in the 43rd minute for the French international’s first goal of the season. “This is the type of match we found hard to win last season,” Da Cunha told DAZN.
