Later on Sunday in Italy, Juventus host Napoli in a game between two sides in danger of getting left behind, eighth v seventh at the start of the day. In the Basque derby, Real Sociedad need to win in Bilbao against Athletic Club if they are to keep in touch with the top four. In France, Paris FC host Monaco in a game both need to win to keep in touch with Paris Saint-Germain, who won 5-1 at Le Havre on Friday.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick to stay in charge of Manchester United for Roma game
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick is poised to remain in charge of Manchester United for the Champions League game against Roma at Old Trafford on Tuesday despite the 2-0 defeat at Chelsea on Saturday.

United have not won in nine games and have made their poorest start to a season since 1988, but Carrick’s position is expected to be reviewed again during the international break after the next round of Premier League matches, in which United host Aston Villa next Sunday.

The 45-year-old head coach came close to losing his job last Monday when Jason Wilcox and Omar ­Berrada met at the training ground to discuss his future. The director of football and the chief executive decided ­Carrick should be given a chance to turn form and results around.

Carrick’s side are in 17th with seven points, above the relegation zone only on goal difference.

There remains a view within the hierarchy that Carrick can still transform fortunes, with United’s travelling support still backing him at the end of the defeat at Stamford Bridge on Saturday. After the game the head coach indicated that he expected to still be in position for the Roma match. He said: “We’ve got to move forward and win matches, it’s as simple as that.”

View image in fullscreen Bruno Fernandes, Manchester United’s captain, looks dejected after the 2-0 defeat at Chelsea. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

Eddie Howe is Wilcox’s preferred candidate should Carrick be sacked, with contact between the parties understood to have been made. The former Newcastle manager is open to taking up the position, subject to negotiations. He would cost about £3m in compensation to Newcastle.

Julian Nagelsmann, the ­former Germany and Bayern Munich head coach, is highly regarded by ­Christopher ­Vivell, United’s director of ­recruitment, who is believed to have sounded out his fellow ­German. The pair previously worked together at RB Leipzig.

Sports.title: Boy hands himself into police after Bradley Lowery taunt in Sunderland match
Sports.content:
A 14-year-old boy has “handed himself in” to West Midlands police after a video posted on social media appeared to show a Coventry fan taunting Sunderland with a photo of Bradley Lowery during the Premier League match on Saturday.

Sunderland fan Bradley captured the hearts of the football world when he was diagnosed with neuroblastoma, a rare form of childhood cancer. He died aged six in 2017.

Coventry said on Sunday that they were investigating the video footage and Bradley’s mother, Gemma, issued an emotional statement through the Bradley Lowery Foundation, which raises funds and awareness to help and support children.

West Midlands police said: “We are aware of a video circulating on social media showing an incident at Coventry City’s Premier League match with Sunderland [on Saturday] afternoon.

“A thorough investigation has been launched, and a 14-year-old boy has since handed himself in and will be spoken with in due course. We understand the upset and outrage this video has caused in the community and to the victim’s family and our officers are keeping them up to date with the progress of our investigation and working closely alongside both football clubs.”

Coventry said in their earlier statement: “Coventry City FC is aware of footage circulating on social media in connection with an incident during our Premier League fixture against Sunderland. The club does not tolerate offensive behaviour and will liaise with the relevant authorities to determine the appropriate course of action.”

Gemma Lowery said her “beautiful boy deserves to be remembered with love, not hate” in her statement. She posted on Instagram: “Yesterday, a Coventry fan used a photograph of Bradley to taunt Sunderland supporters. As Bradley’s mam, this is heartbreaking, especially as it’s one of my favourite photographs of him. Just look at that smile.

“I remember that day like it was yesterday. He was so happy, having so much fun. Those moments were precious because they were few and far between.

“So much of Bradley’s short life was spent battling cancer and enduring treatments no child should ever face. To see such a beautiful memory used in such a cruel way really does make my heart hurt.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Sport in Focus Our picture editors select their favourite sporting images from the past week, from the spectacular to the powerful, and with a little bit of fun thrown in Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“We are a football-loving family who follow Sunderland home and away. I’m all for football banter, but surely mocking a child who died from cancer is not banter?”

Lowery added: “I hope the club takes appropriate action and the young lad’s family help him understand how hurtful his actions were. I don’t want hatred directed towards him, so please please don’t, just for him to learn from this.

“Behind that photograph is a little boy who was loved beyond measure and a family who miss him every day. Thank you to everyone who has defended Bradley and shown us so much love. It means more than you know.”

Sports.title: Scottish roundup: Falkirk shock Celtic; Hibernian beat Hearts in semi-final
Sports.content:
Celtic slumped to a 2-0 defeat at Falkirk on Sunday to ramp up the scrutiny on manager Martin O’Neill after a run of three wins in 10 games. The Scottish champions had the chance to extend their lead at the top of the table to seven points, but never recovered from conceding a third-minute opener to Ethan Ross.

Scott Tanser scored a second before half-time and the Bairns even had a third goal ruled out by a VAR review for handball against Jacob Murrell. The majority of Celtic’s struggles this season have come in European competition as they crashed out of the Champions League qualifiers and have lost all three Europa League group matches.

But sloppy defensive errors and a lack of a clear tactical plan is beginning to cost them domestically as well. Rangers could now close to within one point of their Old Firm rivals should they win a game in hand.

Quick Guide Scottish Premiership roundup: Saints dedicate draw to dismissed Steward Show Simo Valakari dedicated St Johnstone’s battling 2-2 draw at Kilmarnock to the goalkeeper Toby Steward, who was dismissed in the 14th minute (pictured) after misjudging a long ball and handling outside his penalty area. Saints then twice fell behind to Cathal McCarthy and Djenairo Daniels, but equalised both times with goals from Danny Schmidt and Joel Cotterill to capture an unlikely point. The substitute goalkeeper Ross Sinclair, who came on at the expense of Taylor Steven, also made multiple second-half saves to help Saints move up to seventh. Valakari, the St Johnstone manager, said: “Toby has held his hands up and said: ‘I am sorry, boys, for what I did.’ But our team did it for Toby, the boys did it for Taylor, who I needed to take out straight away. “We are all here playing for each other. We have got each other’s backs when things happen. That tells me my players are ready to accept any responsibility. Early red card, with Toby that’s my tactical choice. I ask my keeper to play very high, like a sweeper-keeper for those long balls. In those moments, for a year, Toby has been fantastic in clearing the ball, reading the ball. It’s a thin line, a little outside the box, that can happen.” Alfred Johansson admitted he was left to sweat as Motherwell broke a seven-game winless run with a 1-0 win over St Mirren. Lukas Fadinger rattled home a penalty eight minutes from time to relieve some pressure on the Swede as the Fir Park side climbed into eighth. Johansson was adamant his team were well worthy of a result, which brought welcome relief to both him and his players. He said: “Even more than relief, I felt good, happy, joy, determination. This group has done really well lately and I think it’s very well deserved to get the victory and have at least four points from these last two games. It’s important to build on it, the most important thing today is that we didn’t give away easy goals or big chances at all." Press Association Photograph: Andy Buchanan/Shutterstock Editorial Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

“We’re still in a decent position at this minute,” said a defiant O’Neill. “I keep out the noise at the end of it all. A tough one to take because I know we conceded two goals but we could have scored six or seven dead easily.”

Falkirk had not beaten Celtic since March 2007, but were well worthy of a fourth consecutive victory to move up to fourth in the table. O’Neill recalled Cameron Carter-Vickers to the heart of his defence, but that decision backfired when the American international presented the ball to Ross to slam home the opening goal.

The former Celtic goalkeeper Scott Bain was inspired in the Falkirk goal to deny Haissem Hassan and Camilo Durán, while the Colombian forward also struck a post as the visitors pressed for an equaliser. But Celtic’s leaky defence was exposed once more on 38 minutes when Tanser raced forward from left-back and drilled low into the corner.

O’Neill, 74, twice rode to Celtic’s rescue last season to take interim charge, 20 years after his first spell at the club ended. The Northern Irishman then signed a one-year deal in June.

Yet murmurs of discontent among the club’s fanbase have increased in recent weeks with many now calling for a change. “I’ve managed this team now for about a year, give or take a month or two, and I’ve managed before,” added O’Neill. “We’re still top of the league. We came from a mile behind last year to win the league. A mile behind on two or three occasions as well too.”

Marink Reedijk secured his first win as Hibernian boss in a memorable 2-1 Premier Sports Cup semi-final win over Hearts at Hampden Park.

View image in fullscreen Jamie McGrath wheels away after scoring Hibernian’s second goal. Photograph: Andrew Milligan/PA

A frenetic Edinburhg derby got up and running in the fourth minute when the Hearts attacker Claudio Braga headed in from a corner, only for Martin Boyle to deservedly level in the 19th minute with a poacher’s goal.

A compelling encounter continued and the midfielder Jamie McGrath put the on-top Hibernian ahead three minutes before the interval.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Although Hearts retained a threat in the second half, a stout defensive display by the Leith side means they will meet Rangers in the final at Scotland’s national stadium on Sunday 13 December. Hearts had won the four previous meetings between the teams at Hampden, in 2006, 2012, 2020 and 2022, but this was Hibs’ day.

On Saturday, Ryan Naderi’s dramatic late strike broke down Aberdeen’s stubborn resistance to earn Rangers a place in the final.

View image in fullscreen Ryan Naderi of Rangers celebrates after the semi-final victory over Aberdeen. Photograph: Jamie Johnston/Focus Images Ltd/Shutterstock

Aberdeen restricted Rangers to one shot on target in a low quality first half, but Derek McInnes’s side picked up the pace after the break. Aberdeen survived relentless pressure at times but in the 83rd minute Naderi redirected a strike from James Penrice into the net for his eighth goal of the season to seal a 1-0 win at Hampden Park.

The 23-year-old Naderi later tried to share the glory, saying: “It feels amazing. I’m happy, of course, happy to be the one who scores the goals, but happy for the team. I think we deserved it. We believed we could score right up until the very end and we did, and I think it’s a deserved win.”

It was another close-range strike from Naderi and he joked about this proficiency from distance. The Germany-born Czechia international said: “I’ve tried to shoot twice today from outside of the box and it didn’t go well. So I went back inside the box. Maybe I should just stick to the easy ones! As I said, I’m just happy how it is right now and I’m going to try to stick to it.”

Sports.title: WSL roundup: Russo salvages draw, James suffers hamstring injury
Sports.content:
One shot, on target and in the back of the net, was all it took for Aston Villa to reopen the wound that Arsenal had been carefully trying to stitch back up.

Despite almost 65% possession, 28 shots to one, and 56 touches in the opposition box to four, Alessia Russo’s 85th-minute goal meant Arsenal were only able to salvage a point against Villa after back-to-back wins in the league and Champions League had appeared to have kickstarted their season.

The worst possible scenario for a team that has struggled against low blocks arrived in the 25th minute, when Lynn Wilms found Chasity Grant, who fired low into the bottom corner. It was a hammer blow to the home team, with Villa knowing exactly what to do next: stick 11 players behind the ball and frustrate the Gunners.

Russo’s late goal spared Arsenal’s blushes a little, the forward flicking a header in at the far post from a Stina Blackstenius cross, but the reprieve delivered by Arsenal’s victories over Tottenham and Benfica has been rolled back.

The Gunners have an incredibly tricky run of fixtures coming up, with Liverpool away followed by Barcelona, London City and then Lyonnes. And, despite the back-to-back wins, they haven’t been able to resolve the problems in the final third that have plagued every performance.

The pressure will be back on head coach Renée Slegers and there are questions to be asked about some decision making. However, with similar problems present under Joe Montemurro and Jonas Eidevall before her, maybe it’s time to look beyond the head coach.

Elsewhere Lauren James was forced off with an injury in the first half of Chelsea’s 6-0 win at Charlton. The England forward was replaced by Erin Cuthbert in the 35th minute with the away team 4-0 up. There were five different goalscorers with Melvine Malard getting two. The coach, Sonia Bompastor, said: “It is too soon [to know] about Lauren’s injury. I spoke to her at half-time and it seems to be her hamstring so we will have to have a proper assessment tomorrow.”

Tottenham climbed to fourth in the table after a comprehensive 4-1 win at Birmingham City. The Spurs midfielder Drew Spence set a new all-time WSL appearance record with 2017 to move one above the former Chelsea defender Millie Bright. West Ham were also 4-1 winners, over Liverpool, in their third league win of the season, leapfrogging their opponents in the table to move up to 10th.

Annabel Blanchard gave Crystal Palace the lead at Brighton with a glorious long-range effort but the visitors could not hold on and strikes from Caitlin Hayes and Sophie Peskett completed the turnaround for Arturo Ruiz’s side. “I think that these three wins in a row will be key for the rest of the season and we are in a very good moment,” Ruiz told the club website. “And I think that we are showing what we want to do in terms of our energy. The first half was very good even though we conceded a goal.”

Sports.title: Should Premier League strugglers stick or twist as pressure on managers mounts?  | Andrew Beasley
Sports.content:
No Premier League manager has yet lost his job this season. In only three of the past 10 campaigns was November reached without a club making a managerial change.

The 2026-27 season commencing with 11 managers who were appointed at some point in 2026 has probably contributed to the early season stability. They have to be given a chance to fashion their side as they see fit. But with roughly a quarter of the season played and only one more round of fixtures before an international break, the first sacking may not be far away.

Michael Carrick remains the favourite to be the next manager to leave his post. He is unsurprisingly followed by the managers of the clubs who occupy the relegation zone: Pierre Sage of Crystal Palace, Sunderland’s Régis Le Bris and Oliver Glasner at Nottingham Forest. It seems almost inevitable that Carrick will leave soon so the more interesting analysis lies among the bottom three.

Sunderland sit 20th and are predicted by Opta to finish there. However, they have had a testing start to the season. Le Bris’s side have faced five of the current top seven clubs, the joint-most along with Liverpool. The manager also has enormous reserves of goodwill after taking the club back to the Premier League and then into Europe.

Despite their tough schedule, Sunderland came into the weekend within one expected point of Chelsea, Manchester United and Tottenham before losing 3-1 at Coventry with the xG count 1.8 to 0.7 in their favour. It was a familiar outcome for a side that has scored 6.2 goals fewer than expected this season.

With Sunderland’s next five league opponents being Chelsea, Aston Villa, Tottenham, Liverpool and Newcastle, the challenge of staying up will not immediately get easier. At least their chance‑converting woes are not as bad as those of Nottingham Forest.

Their shots have been worth 14.7 expected goals, the fourth most in the division after the matches on Saturday. But not once in a game this season have the goals they scored at least equalled their xG, let alone surpassed it. It is a finishing issue, not a question of opposition goalkeepers having super-human performances against them.

The analytical step above standard expected goals is xG on target (xGOT). It measures the likelihood of an on-target shot becoming a goal based on chance quality and shot placement. Forest’s xGOT this season is 7.4, little more than half of their expected goal tally.

This inability to test goalkeepers severely enough explains why Glasner’s men have scored just six times. They are squandering almost one goal per game on average according to their expected goals, a significant shortfall. None of the 96 teams in Europe’s big five leagues were worse than 0.5 goals per match below xG last season, which suggests Forest’s luck should turn for the better.

Is Evangelos Marinakis patient enough for that to happen? Forest’s expected goal data is much stronger for Glasner than it was under any of the four managers their owner fired last season. Whether he pays attention to such numbers is a different issue.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Glasner hinted at a physical deficiency in the squad after defeat at Brentford. “We are outrun by the opposition in every single game. We have to change it,” he said. Distance covered data from Fotmob suggests that is not quite the case, albeit Forest have been outrun in their past five league games. Both the underlying xG data and physical statistics are worse at Glasner’s former club Crystal Palace though.

As expected goals have a far greater bearing on future performance or results than running stats, those numbers are the greater concern. Equally, Palace’s average of 96.9 sprints per match is the fewest in the Premier League (after Saturday’s matches).

The club have been through similar teething troubles with new managers before. Palace’s previous two appointments that occurred between seasons were Frank de Boer and Patrick Vieira. The former was sacked after only five matches in all competitions in 2017, the latter won just one of his first nine league games four years later before recovering to finish 12th.

While Palace are a little wasteful in attack, they have not been as bad as Forest or Sunderland. Their defence is a much bigger problem, which is unusual as Sage’s Lens conceded the fourth fewest expected goals in Ligue 1 last season. Palace are second worst for that metric in the Premier League in 2026‑27, rock bottom if penalties are excluded. Some of that may be down to starting seven combinations of players in the back three because of injuries and Axel Disasi’s three‑match ban, but it is imperative that a manager overcomes such inevitable difficulties.

Palace host Liverpool next weekend. They return after the international break with potentially winnable games against Coventry and Hull. Will those fixtures represent a good opportunity for Sage to kickstart his reign or an excellent chance for his replacement to hit the ground running? Only the chair, Steve Parish, will know the answer but Palace are the strugglers who look most in need of managerial change.

Sports.title: Anfield victory was vindication for Mikel Arteta after Fleetwood humbling. His Arsenal look the finished article - Liverpool were authors of their own downfall, writes OLIVER HOLT
Sports.content:
Five nights ago, 40 miles to the north of Anfield at a remote outpost of English football, Arsenal fell to one of the most humiliating reverses of their long and august history. In the teeth of a gale that blew in off the Irish Sea, they were knocked out of the League Cup by Fleetwood Town, a team 18th in League Two.

They left with their tails between their legs, their teenage prodigy Max Dowman sent off in a melee, their heart questioned, their quality debated, their discipline an issue. Mikel Arteta and his side knew that just a few days later, at the other end of the Fylde Coast and across the Ribble Estuary, they would have to swap running the gauntlet of the Cod Army for the challenge of facing down the roar of the Kop.

They did not shirk it. If Tuesday night was a humbling, their gritty 1-0 victory in an Anfield that was a cauldron once more felt like a significant triumph. It was a defensive masterclass from the champions, an exercise in indomitability. It was their first victory here since 2012 and it took them above Manchester City so that they sit, once more, at the top of the table. Liverpool could not summon a single shot on target.

‘It felt like the end of the world when we were knocked out at Fleetwood,’ Arteta said after this win. ‘You look so silly. I was thinking “How can I lift these players up?” You have to dig deep. This was a mission to win here and it is something that we have not done for 14 years for a variety of reasons. We knew we would have to navigate some difficult moments.’

If Arteta left Fleetwood answering questions about his management of Dowman, he finished this game by striding on to the pitch after the final whistle, pumping his fists in front of the Arsenal fans celebrating in the Anfield Road end, and beating his hand on his chest. This was a vindication for him and his team. Five nights is a long time in football.

He had talked about the harsh realities of this sport after Tuesday’s loss. He had reminded everyone that playing at this level was not like ‘Disneyland’. And this victory was not like Disneyland, either. It was less a theme park and more an assault course. It was rough and it was unforgiving and Arsenal were equal to it.

Liverpool, improving under the management of Andoni Iraola, had been talked up as title contenders ahead of this match on a dank evening on Merseyside where the streets around the ground were decorated with the toothless grimaces of rotting pumpkins on doorsteps. The home team showed exhilarating signs of their re-emergence as an attacking force.

They dominated much of the game, too, but they looked like an emerging team, a team that is still evolving. Arsenal, marshalled imperiously by Declan Rice, looked like the finished article. They created one outstanding chance and Kai Havertz converted it. That was all they needed.

Their defence stayed rock-solid, although there was some puzzlement that Liverpool were not awarded a penalty for Jurrien Timber’s blatant shirt-pull on Alexander Isak. After the interval, Liverpool rarely looked like drawing level.

Kai Havertz gave the Gunners a lead to defend after finishing off a well worked move early on

The German slotted home after Declan Rice fizzed a dangerous ball across the six-yard box

Winning at Anfield was vindication for Mikel Arteta after Arsenal's defeat by Fleetwood Town

The opening had been predictably frenetic. Neither team forged a chance but Trey Nyoni, who has forced his way into the first team with a series of excellent performances in midfield, could have been booked twice inside the first quarter of an hour.

The initial infringement was a nasty tackle on Martin Odegaard inside the first minute where he planted his studs in Odegaard’s ankle. The second was a spiteful tackle on Kai Havertz. Neither received a yellow card, which gave yet more pause for thought about the red card shown to Dowman at Fleetwood, and its aftermath.

Let’s get one thing straight – the criticism of Arteta for his ‘treatment’ of Dowman was absurd. It has come to something when a manager giving a player a hard stare is interpreted by some as a disproportionate response.

Nobody is necessarily hankering after a return to the days of Sir Alex Ferguson’s hairdrier or Joe Kinnear’s rants that broke records for expletives but if a boss is attracting censure because he looked at a player a bit funny, we are in big trouble.

Arteta is not there to indulge Dowman. He is there to coach him and to teach him and to help him grow up in the context of a Premier League football club. His actions in Fleetwood on Tuesday fulfilled his obligations in all of those criteria.

Arsenal survived the initial frenzy here and took the lead after 16 minutes. Liverpool were the authors of their own downfall. They gave the ball away from a goal kick, it was worked to Noni Madueke on the right, and when Madueke fed it to Declan Rice on the overlap, Rice crossed beautifully for Havertz, who touched it home at the back post.

Arsenal nearly returned the favour a minute later when they played themselves into trouble at the back. Bradley Barcola found himself through on David Raya but his first touch let him down and Rice moved across to clear the danger.

Alexis Mac Allister was left with his head in his hands after missing a glorious chance to score

Liverpool's 19-year-old talent Trey Nyoni started the match but was replaced in the second half

Liverpool recovered and began to dominate the game. Barcola’s pace began to cause Arsenal all sorts of problems down their right flank and Liverpool came close to an equaliser when Virgil van Dijk flicked on a corner and Alexander Isak was denied by the brave intervention of Raya.

Arsenal were still threatening on the counter. Christos Tzolis chipped a ball to the back post and, as Liverpool scrambled to clear it, Madueke turned it back across goal. The ball was intended for Havertz, who was unmarked in the middle, but Timber could not get out of the way of it and it bounced off him into touch.

The atmosphere was febrile. Liverpool had three appeals for penalties, first for Timber’s shirt pull on Isak, then for challenges on Alexis Mac Allister and Cody Gakpo, turned down in quick succession. Tempers began to flare on the benches.

The breathlessness of the match was relentless. Florian Wirtz drove a free kick against the face of the crossbar with Raya beaten and then, three minutes before the interval, Mac Allister ran on to a cross from Milos Kerkez and, with the goal at his mercy, directed his free header too high.

Liverpool laid siege to the Arsenal goal after the break but the openings just would not come. Isak blazed high over the bar from an angle, Wirtz had a shot on the turn blocked and then, just before the hour, Dominik Szoboszlai replaced Nyoni and, to more acclaim, Rio Ngumoha came on for Gakpo.

Still Liverpool could not prise Arsenal open. Arsenal began to grow in confidence and threat. The home team The home team were grateful to Jeremy Jacquet for a clearance that prevented Odegaard turning Tzolis’s cross into an open goal, for Van Dijk’s brilliant interception to deny Havertz and, most of all, for a quite magnificent one-handed save from Alisson that diverted a Tzolis shot round the post. It will stand the test of time as one of the saves of the season.

Arsenal put in another excellent defensive display to frustrate and keep Liverpool at bay

Liverpool’s frustration boiled over. Mac Allister was booked for his part in an ugly fracas with Odegaard and Madueke. The stands became a mass of pointing fingers and shouts of protest and anger. Time-wasting and play-acting peppered the match. Liverpool felt the game slipping away in the angst.

Liverpool threw everything at it in the final minutes. Lewis Koumas flung himself at a bouncing ball but could not get enough power on his header, Ngumoha had a shot charged down, Barcola desperately searched for pockets of space but could not find them. There were six minutes of time added on but there was no way through. Arsenal’s defence would not yield.

Sports.title: Erik ten Hag launches latest attack on Cristiano Ronaldo: Former Man United boss claims Portugal star's career was OVER by time he joined Juventus
Sports.content:
Erik ten Hag launches latest attack on Cristiano Ronaldo: Former Man United boss claims Portugal star's career was OVER by time he joined Juventus

Former Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag has taken another swipe at Cristiano Ronaldo, claiming the Portugal icon's career was already over by the time he joined Juventus and eventually returned to Old Trafford.

The legendary forward's second spell at United ended acrimoniously after he launched a public attack on the club and Ten Hag, accusing the manager of 'betraying' him in a bombshell interview.

Ronaldo, whose United contract was terminated following his explosive criticism of the club, joined Al-Nassr in January 2023, while Ten Hag was eventually sacked in October 2024 after a disappointing run of results.

Last month, Ten Hag gave a wide-ranging interview to The Athletic in which he criticised Ronaldo for 'letting the team down' and accused the club's hierarchy of contributing to a 'toxic culture'.

The Dutchman has now doubled down on his criticism of the 41-year-old veteran once again, claiming Ronaldo could not 'make way' for the team.

'Every top team must embrace the top player, but the top player must also make way for the team. That was simply the problem with Ronaldo,' Ten Hag said in an interview on ESPN.

Erik ten Hag has claimed Cristiano Ronaldo's career was over by the time he returned to United

Ten Hag conducted a wide-ranging interview with The Athletic last week in which he hit out at the club's hierarchy for contributing to a 'toxic culture' - and lashed out at Ronaldo

'Let there be no misunderstanding on my part, he is of course a great player. He belongs among the greats of the world.

'But the reality is also that he hasn't been able to deliver for the last seven or eight years. From Juventus onwards, it was simply over.'

Ten Hag also praised Real Madrid, where Ronaldo statistically enjoyed the most prolific years of his career, for selling the superstar at what he believed was the perfect time.

'That is also Real Madrid's great gift,' he added. 'They see when a player is declining in level. Then they part ways at a moment when, to the outside world, they are still at their peak, but actually can no longer deliver.'

In Ten Hag's tell-all interview last month, he accused Manchester United's owners of 'breaking promises' over recruitment and blasted them for showing a lack of ambition in the transfer market.

His criticism of Manchester United came amid a turbulent spell for the club, with Lisandro Martinez and Bruno Fernandes both publicly criticising the board and manager Michael Carrick respectively in recent weeks.

Carrick was given a chance to put things right after United's chiefs met for crunch talks earlier this week in the wake of his side losing 4-1 to Como in the Champions League and 3-0 to Bournemouth in the Premier League.

According to Ten Hag, Ronaldo was not prepared to stand aside for the good of the team

Ronaldo, who now plays for Al-Nassr, is within touching distance of scoring 1,000 career goals

On Saturday, United met a similar fate as they were thumped 3-0 by Chelsea at Stamford Bridge, piling even more pressure on Carrick.

Red Devils legend Peter Schmeichel expressed his anger at Ten Hag speaking out against the club during this difficult period last week.

Speaking on The Overlap Daily, former United goalkeeper Schmeichel said: 'What really annoys me in everything that has happened in the past two weeks is Ten Hag coming out and saying that he wanted Declan Rice and Harry Kane, like he was a god.

'It's so ridiculous. He brought (Lisandro) Martinez in, (Matthijs) de Ligt. I mean he brought players in that are still there, how dare he go out and say that.

'Everybody knew we should sign Harry Kane. Everyone knows we should have signed Declan Rice, that's no secret. I don't know why we didn't do that.

'But you have now people stirring the pot where they should just keep calm and not talk and maybe talk about what they did for this football club themselves, or what they didn't do.

'He wasn't a success at Manchester United. Why does he feel the need to come out and say that?

'What he's saying is "I was let down by the club" and there might be an element of truth in that but he wasn't good enough. And then he went to Bayer Leverkusen, a team who had just won the Bundesliga, and then he got sacked within, what, three games?

Ten Hag also hit out at Manchester United's hierarchy amid a turbulent time for the club

Michael Carrick has been given a chance to turn things around after chiefs held crunch talks

'Maybe just take a step back and don't put yourself in that because then you will end up with someone like me criticising him, and there's no need for that. We don't need it in the narrative.'

Ten Hag was sacked by United in October 2024 after a string of poor results left the team 14th in the Premier League.

His future had been in doubt after he led United to a disappointing eighth-placed finish in the top flight a couple of months earlier, but victory in the FA Cup final over rivals Manchester City contributed to the club's decision to give him a contract extension in the summer after crunch talks in Ibiza.

He went on to replace Xabi Alonso at Bundesliga side Bayer Leverkusen the following season, but was sacked after just three games in charge, and he criticised the club's board for this 'unprecedented' decision.

Sports.title: Liverpool 0-1 Arsenal PLAYER RATINGS: Whose touch let him down? Who produced another promising display after facing scrutiny? And how did youngster Trey Nyoni settle in?
Sports.content:
Liverpool 0-1 Arsenal PLAYER RATINGS: Whose touch let him down? Who produced another promising display after facing scrutiny? And how did youngster Trey Nyoni settle in?

Arsenal's miserly defence thwarted Liverpool at Anfield to send the Premier League champions top.

Kai Havertz tapped in what proved to be the winner from a fine Arsenal move 16 minutes in, with Alexis Mac Allister spurning the best chance before the break.

Wave after wave of attack from the home side came and went in the second period, although Andoni Iraola's men were unable to conjure many clear-cut chances.

Ultimately the Reds could not force their way through the wall in front of them and Arteta won away against Liverpool for the first time in the top flight.

The Gunners took advantage of Man City's defeat by Brighton on Saturday and are now three points clear.

Daily Mail Sport's LEWIS STEELE and ISAAN KHAN were in position at Anfield to run the rule over both sides...

Ezri Konsa (left) and Gabriel Magalhaes (right) were at the heart of Arsenal's resilient win

LIVERPOOL (4-2-3-1):

Alisson - 6

A loose pass cost Liverpool and led directly to Arsenal’s goal but made a phenomenal save on 73 minutes to deny Tzolis.

Ronald Araujo - 5

Could he have done better to keep track of Havertz for the opener? Maybe harsh but the German ghosted in at Araujo’s back post.

Jeremy Jacquet - 6

A few heavy touches early doors but settled and made some important tackles.

Virgil van Dijk - 6

Made a last-ditch intervention on 71 minutes to prevent what looked certain to be Havertz’s second goal.

Milos Kerkez - 6 (Booked)

Threatened more than usual going forward and nearly had an assist but for a bad Mac Allister header.

Trey Nyoni - 6

Two fouls were lucky to go unpunished in the opening stages but Nyoni, on his first league start, soon settled and started to dictate from deep.

Trey Nyoni made a shaky start for the Reds but quickly found his composure

Alexis Mac Allister - 7 (Booked)

Had Liverpool’s best chance when unmarked in the box and the Argentine usually gobbles up those chances. Was Liverpool’s sharpest player.

Cody Gakpo - 5

Did an important defensive shift on the wildcard left back Riccardo Calafiori, who is everywhere, but Gakpo did not offer enough threat the other way.

Florian Wirtz - 5

Another big game where fans would have wanted more. Some nice moments but made the wrong decision too often.

Bradley Barcola - 7 (Booked)

Had a big opening just after Arsenal’s goal to make it 1-1 but a heavy touch let him down. Was Liverpool’s most dangerous asset in the first half, looked tired late on.

Bradley Barcola was the most dangerous Liverpool attacker but fatigue set in

Alexander Isak - 5

His honesty came back to bite him when he did not throw himself to ground in a first-half penalty shout. Did not impact proceedings enough otherwise.

His attackers got into dangerous positions but could not finish their dinner.

Looked a penalty for a tug on Isak. Inconsistent usage of his yellow card.

ARSENAL (4-2-3-1):

David Raya: 7

Accurate, fast distribution when under pressure from the Liverpool frontline. Consistently set Arsenal away on counter-attacks.

Jurrien Timber: 6

Looked overwhelmed at times and didn’t get forward as much as he’d have liked. Still, played his part in keeping the cleansheet.

Ezri Konsa: 8

Bailed out by Declan Rice for his errant pass on 18 minutes. After that, he barely put a foot wrong. Found himself in the right place at the right time defensively.

Konsa defended brilliantly, seen here shielding the ball from Alexander Isak

Gabriel: 7

Up for the fight in the bearpit atmosphere that is Anfield. Strong aerially and stayed switched on for darting runs of Alexander Isak.

Riccardo Calafiori: 8

A handful both in attack and defence. Made menacing runs into final third which the opposition found tricky to track.

Declan Rice: 9

A complete, domineering display typified by a desire to break into attacking areas and clean up in midfield. Excellent cross to assist Kai Havertz.

Declan Rice celebrates the first Arsenal win at Anfield in 14 years after full time

Aggressive in tackles and pressing. His wild scream towards the crowd after tackling Bradley Barcola set the tone. Yet the introduction of Myles Lewis-Skelly brought more control.

Has now strung together a few promising displays after facing scrutiny. Direct and kept looking to take on Milos Kerkez.

Led the press, which contributed in the build-up to Havertz’s strike. Tireless and his will didn’t peter, even when Liverpool enjoyed much possession.

Good effort by the Greek to accelerate his return to Arsenal’s squad after his injury woes. Curling effort on 73 minutes required a good save.

Christos Tzolis looked on in disbelief after Alisson saved brilliantly from his effort

Simple finish from Rice’s excellent cross. Did his best to hold play up when in possession. Put in a vigorous shift off the ball.

Arsenal win at Anfield for the first time in 14 years — and they keep a clean sheet. An excellent day’s work.

Sports.title: European 1500m champion and two-time Olympian, 34, who married her partner last month dies after cancer battle
Sports.content:
European 1500m champion and two-time Olympian Ciara Mageean has died aged 34 following a battle with bowel cancer.

The Northern Irish athlete, who represented Ireland at two Olympic Games and claimed European gold in 2024, died on Sunday morning surrounded by her loved ones.

Mageean, from Portaferry in County Down, was diagnosed with stage four bowel cancer in May 2025.

Her death comes just weeks after she married her long-term partner Thomas Moran in an intimate civil ceremony in Belfast.

A statement shared on her social media accounts confirmed the news on Sunday. It read: 'At 6.30am this morning, Ciara lost her battle with cancer surrounded by her loved ones.

'A beloved daughter, sister, wife, friend and inspiration to so many, she will be deeply missed. Ar dheis Dé go raibh a hanam [may her soul rest in peace].'

Tributes have poured in for the celebrated middle-distance runner, who became one of Ireland's most successful athletes after overcoming years of injuries and sporting setbacks.

Her death comes just weeks after she married her long-term partner Thomas Moran in an intimate civil ceremony in Belfast last month

European 1500m champion and two-time Olympian Ciara Mageean has died aged 34 following a battle with bowel cancer

Athletics Ireland said in a statement: 'We are heartbroken. An inspiration to so many, Ciara will be remembered for her courage, kindness and incredible spirit.

'Our deepest sympathies are with her family, friends and loved ones at this difficult time. Rest in peace, Ciara.'

Mageean's crowning achievement came at the European Athletics Championships in Rome in June 2024, when she stormed to victory in the women's 1500m final to claim the first major title of her career.

In a dramatic race, she found herself trapped behind British runners Georgia Bell and Jemma Reekie before finding a gap and surging down the home straight to take gold in four minutes 4.66 seconds.

The emotional victory followed years of near-misses on the international stage and cemented her reputation as one of Europe's finest middle-distance runners.

An ecstatic Mageean later admitted that 'words can't even come close' to describing her feelings after finally securing the coveted title.

But her hopes of adding an Olympic medal to her collection were cruelly dashed just weeks later when an Achilles injury forced her to withdraw from the Paris Games on the eve of her opening heat.

It was the latest in a series of injury setbacks that had repeatedly threatened to derail her career.

Mageean had previously represented Ireland at the Rio Olympics in 2016, where she reached the 1500m semi-finals, and the delayed Tokyo Games in 2021, where a calf injury hampered her preparations and she was eliminated in the heats.

Her sporting talent had been evident from childhood, when she played camogie for Portaferry GAC before turning her attention to athletics in pursuit of her Olympic ambitions.

She enjoyed a glittering junior career, winning silver medals over 1500m at the 2010 World Junior Championships and the 2011 European Junior Championships.

At just 18, she also reached the 1500m final at the 2010 Commonwealth Games.

The Northern Irish athlete, who represented Ireland at two Olympic Games and claimed European gold in 2024, passed away on Sunday morning surrounded by her loved ones

However, a serious ankle injury subsequently ended her hopes of competing at London 2012 and required surgery in 2013.

She fought her way back to win the Irish 1500m title in 2014 before claiming European bronze in Amsterdam two years later.

In 2017, she moved from Dublin to Manchester to join Steve Vernon's Team New Balance after parting ways with coach Jerry Kiernan.

Her career continued to flourish, with a European Indoor bronze medal in 2019 followed by a series of record-breaking performances.

In 2020, she shattered Sonia O'Sullivan's 27-year-old Irish 1,000m record at the Diamond League meeting in Monaco.

Two years later, under the guidance of former British Olympian Helen Clitheroe, Mageean won silver medals at both the European Championships and the Commonwealth Games in Birmingham, finishing behind Britain's Laura Muir.

She subsequently defeated Muir and a world-class field at the Brussels Diamond League meeting, breaking O'Sullivan's Irish 1500m record with a time of 3:56.63.

In 2023, she narrowly missed out on a World Championships medal after finishing fourth in Budapest, but broke the Irish mile record and was named BBC Northern Ireland Sports Personality of the Year.

Her long-awaited European triumph in Rome the following summer was the pinnacle of a career defined by extraordinary resilience.

Following her cancer diagnosis, Mageean spoke movingly about her gratitude for the life she had enjoyed and the opportunities athletics had given her.

Earlier this year, she said she was 'continuing to find the joy in everyday' as she thanked supporters for their messages.

Speaking to the BBC in June, she said she was 'grateful' for having a career 'that many others didn't get to have'.

In a poignant interview with The Irish Times in June, Mageean had spoken candidly about her terminal diagnosis and the prospect of leaving her partner behind.

She revealed that doctors had warned she might have just two or three years left to live, admitting she feared she would not reach her 40th birthday.

Despite the devastating prognosis, she remained determined to make the most of her remaining time, publishing a memoir, My Greatest Race, and going ahead with her wedding plans.

Just days before her death, Mageean and her husband celebrated their marriage with family and friends at Darver Castle in County Louth, following their earlier civil ceremony in Belfast.

The couple's celebrations marked a final joyful chapter in the life of an athlete whose determination and achievements had inspired thousands across Ireland and beyond.

Taoiseach Micheal Martin said he was deeply saddened by the news.

'My heartfelt sympathies go to her husband Thomas, all her family and friends,' he said in a statement on the social media network X.

Tanaiste Simon Harris described the news as heartbreaking.

He said on X: 'She was a European champion, two-time Olympian, a proud Irish athlete and an extraordinary person.'

Northern Ireland's First Minister Michelle O'Neill said Mageean demonstrated 'extraordinary talent, determination and dedication'.

'From representing Ireland at two Olympic Games to winning European Championship gold in Rome in 2024, Ciara demonstrated extraordinary talent, determination and dedication,' she said.

'However, beyond the medals, records and sporting accolades, Ciara will be remembered for her warmth, courage and tremendous strength of character.

'Throughout her illness, she showed a remarkable spirit and an incredible ability to find hope and joy in life, even in the most difficult circumstances. Her courage touched countless people and will leave a lasting legacy.

'For a community like Portaferry, this loss will be deeply felt. Ciara was one of our own, and the pride she brought to her community and beyond will never be forgotten.'

Sports.title: 'My beautiful boy deserves to be remembered with love, not hate': Bradley Lowery's mum issues heartbreaking statement to condemn 'cruel' Coventry fan who used her late son's photo to taunt Sunderland fans
Sports.content:
Bradley Lowery's mum has released a heartbreaking statement after a Coventry fan appeared to use his photograph to taunt Sunderland supporters. The deplorable behaviour came during the Premier League clash between the two sides on Saturday, which the Sky Blues won 3-1. A video on social media showed a supporter holding up a picture of Bradley - who tragically died from a rare form of childhood cancer at the age of six in 2017 - smiling in the direction of Sunderland fans, with the individual pointing at it and seen smirking at the same time. And, in a statement on Sunday morning after the behaviour of the Coventry fan went viral, Bradley's mum Gemma shared a heartbreaking message. 'My beautiful boy deserves to be remembered with love, not hate,' she wrote. 'Yesterday, a Coventry fan used a photograph of Bradley to taunt Sunderland supporters. As Bradley’s mam, this is heartbreaking, especially as it’s one of my favourite photographs of him. Just look at that smile. 'I remember that day like it was yesterday. He was so happy, having so much fun. Those moments were precious because they were few and far between. So much of Bradley’s short life was spent battling cancer and enduring treatments no child should ever face. To see such a beautiful memory used in such a cruel way really does make my heart hurt. A Coventry fan appeared to use a photograph of Bradley Lowery to taunt Sunderland fans A fan held up a photo of Bradley, the Sunderland fan who tragically passed away aged six from a rare form of childhood cancer, and was seen smirking and pointing 'We are a football-loving family who follow Sunderland home and away. I’m all for football banter, but surely mocking a child who died from cancer is not banter? I hope the club takes appropriate action and the young lad’s family help him understand how hurtful his actions were. 'I don’t want hatred directed towards him, so please please don't, just for him to learn from this. Behind that photograph is a little boy who was loved beyond measure and a family who miss him every day. Thank you to everyone who has defended Bradley and shown us so much love. It means more than you know.' Gemma continued: 'What some people don’t realise is that Bradley’s story didn’t end when his life did. Because of Bradley, children’s lives are being saved, hundreds of families have received vital support, and children facing unimaginable battles are being given hope. 'Through Super Brad’s Pad, families can escape hospital life, spend precious time together and make memories that last forever. That is Bradley’s legacy. The difference my little boy continues to make in this world. No amount of cruelty will ever take that away. 'So rather than let this photograph be remembered for hatred, I want it remembered for what it truly represents. My beautiful little boy, enjoying one of the happiest days of his life, with the biggest smile on his face. That is how I want the world to remember him. #CancerHasNoColours.' In response to the video Coventry released a statement, which read: 'Coventry City FC is aware of footage circulating on social media in connection with an incident during our Premier League fixture against Sunderland. 'The club does not tolerate offensive behaviour and will liaise with the relevant authorities to determine the appropriate course of action.' Bradley was previously used by a fan as a taunt back in 2023 when Sheffield Wednesday supporter Dale Houghton was seen holding up a picture of him at a match against Sunderland and laughing. Houghton was subsequently handed a 12-week suspended prison sentence and ordered to do 200 hours unpaid work. Bradley touched the hearts of football fans across the UK during his battle with neuroblastoma, and formed a touching relationship with then Sunderland striker Jermain Defoe Bradley pictured with his mum Gemma at his sixth birthday party back in May 2017 Bradley touched the hearts of football fans across the UK during his battle with neuroblastoma, a rare form of childhood cancer, before he tragically passed away aged just six in 2017. The Bradley Lowery Foundation was set up in his honour, with the charity aiming to help families who are fundraising for treatment or equipment that is not readily available or covered by the NHS, while it also supports research into various childhood cancers, including neuroblastoma. Bradley, who was diagnosed with neuroblastoma when he was just 18 months old, also built up a touching relationship with Jermain Defoe, who later called him his 'best mate'. Defoe played for Sunderland at the time, and speaking in 2023, he said: 'He will always be in my heart, for the rest of my life. There's not a day that goes past where I don't wake up and think about little Bradley, because his love is genuine.'

Sports.title: Falkirk 2-0 Celtic: Pressure is mounting on Martin O'Neill as Scottish giants suffer a sixth defeat in 10 matches - as hosts celebrate their first win over Bhoys since 2007
Sports.content:
Falkirk 2-0 Celtic: Pressure is mounting on Martin O'Neill as Scottish giants suffer a sixth defeat in 10 matches - as hosts celebrate their first win over Bhoys since 2007

Celtic paid the price for a sloppy start and a superb display from former goalkeeper Scott Bain as they fell to a 2-0 defeat at Falkirk.

Ethan Ross netted in the third minute after a mistake by Cameron Carter-Vickers and Scott Tanser put Falkirk two ahead in the 38th minute.

Bain made ten saves as Martin O’Neill’s side endured an afternoon of frustration and suffered a sixth defeat in ten matches.

The champions remain four points clear at the top of the William Hill Premiership but have now played a game more than second-placed Rangers.

Falkirk moved up to fourth in the table after their fourth consecutive victory and their first over Celtic since 2007.

Carter-Vickers returned to the starting line-up after injury, while Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain was handed his first start in two months. Winger Haissem Hassan was recalled.

Kasper Hogh might have fancied himself to end his barren run on Falkirk’s synthetic pitch given most of his career goals have come on artificial surfaces, but the former Bodo/Glimt striker was dropped as Camilo Duran led the line.

Martin O'Neill looks on in dismay as Celtic suffer in Falkirk

The Danish striker came on for the final 25 minutes but was barely involved as he went 14 games without a goal.

Falkirk got an early lift after the Celtic central defence failed to deal with a long ball.

The hosts worked the ball out to Ryan Strain, whose cross was knocked into the path of Ross by Carter-Vickers. The wide player lapped up the chance.

The goal came at a cost as Strain injured himself while crossing. Jack McMillan was a natural replacement at right-back.

Both sides made opportunities in the first half.

Celtic winger Haissem Hassan is in the thick of it during a scuffle at the Falkirk Stadium

Owen Eames hails goalscorer Scott Tanser after he scored Falkirk's second

On-loan Derby winger Owen Eames was a hive of creativity on Falkirk’s left wing and helped set up two half chances for Jacob Murrell, who could not make the most of them.

The 19-year-old wide player set up the second goal as left-back Tanser ran on to his infield pass before slotting past Sam Johnstone.

Duran hit a post after getting in behind and Celtic were kept out by a string of excellent first-half stops from Bain, who denied the Colombian three times and also foiled Hassan with a diving save.

Falkirk were almost out of sight early in the second half when Murrell bundled the ball over the line after Celtic failed to deal with a long throw, but the ball had hit the American’s hand when it bounced off a post before going in off the striker’s waist and the goal was disallowed by VAR.

O’Neill had brought on James Forrest for Callum Osmand at half-time and the winger forced Bain’s first save of the half before Callum McGregor, Kieran Tierney and Hassan missed the target from inside the box.

O’Neill turned to Hogh and Benjamin Nygren as Duran and Oxlade-Chamberlain made way.

Celtic captain Callum McGregor looks frustrated during their loss to Falkirk

But Bain quickly pulled off a brilliant double save from Forrest and Nygren to spark chants of ‘Scotland’s number one’.

The former Celtic goalkeeper soon denied Forrest again before Nygren was thwarted by a diving block from Finn Yeats.

It grew increasingly clear that Celtic were never going to score as Liam Scales headed over and Bain saved long-range efforts from Nygren and Mika Baur.

Sports.title: Doubts had been gathering about Roberto De Zerbi but not now, writes RIATH AL-SAMARRAI, as Crystal Palace's ludicrous acts of self-sabotage prove costly in 2-0 defeat
Sports.content:
For the first time in 616 days, Tottenham have won three games in succession. If that proves Roberto De Zerbi’s prowess over at least two of his predecessors, then he will presumably reserve some thanks to the assistance of Crystal Palace.

On a night when Palace crossed to the north of London, with their manager in grave danger of the sack, they contrived to commit an utterly ludicrous act of self-sabotage in two phases.

The first defined the match, with Jean-Philippe Mateta dismissed after only 13 minutes for a challenge that was as brainless as it was dangerous.

From there, Pierre Sage’s side quickly conceded from a set-piece with the sort of defending that explained why Palace have shipped more goals than any other team in the top flight. That no further damage was inflicted until Jan Paul van Hecke’s second-half header was less reflective of the game than the tally showing 34 Tottenham shots to Palace’s two.

Given Sage’s tenuous grip on his job, and the thunderous face in the crowd of his chairman, Steve Parish, that might prove to be the final straw. If it is, Mateta should at least have the decency to drive him to the airport.

Sage said: ‘I am responsible. I have to find solutions. They have to trust in me because I will give my life for it. If I have one hour or 10 years, I will try my best.’

Archie Gray opened the scoring for Tottenham after 25 minutes to settle the nerves

Jan Paul van Hecke slid in to make it 2-0 and all but wrap the game up for the home team

In the recent past, such doubts were gathering around De Zerbi, but not now, and especially with a favourable run of fixtures on the horizon. Having belatedly entered the top half of the table, his side are finally aligning results with performances, even if this fourth game in an unbeaten stretch was aided so much by the opposition.

There remains an issue with chance conversion – both Dominic Solanke and Omar Marmoush were underwhelming here, with the slight mitigation that Palace spent the better part of 75 minutes camped on the edge of their own area. Marmoush, who started at No 10 after earlier games on the left and up front, appears no closer to revealing his best position.

De Zerbi’s solution was to direct traffic to the wings and it worked a treat. Mathys Tel, riding the isolated high of his performance against Chelsea, was again sharp. So too Mohammed Kudus. But the real gains for Tottenham in this purple patch have come from the central pairing of Sandro Tonali and Matheus Fernandes.

They cost a fortune to acquire and have taken their sweet time to gel, but that partnership has developed to strong effect. On the ball, they are the tempo setters, and off it they have shaped the press that is key to De Zerbi’s system. They controlled this game.

‘Tonali was unbelievable,’ said De Zerbi. ‘We played with two players more - Tonali (counted) double.’

He added: ‘I am very happy with the performance. (But) if we want perfection we have to be more nasty. If I am No 9 or No 10 I want to score.’

The last sentence is very much the Tottenham riddle – an inability to finish what they start. But those frustrations are now coming from an upwardly mobile situation.

Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi is banishing the doubters as his team climb the table

Having belatedly entered the top half of the table, Spurs are finally aligning results with performances

For Sage, along with whatever consequences this result brings, the regret will come from knowing his side had looked decent out of the gate.

But the red card eradicated those traces of momentum. Initially, referee Michael Oliver felt a booking was sufficient for Mateta’s studs-up lunge into Micky van de Ven’s ankle, but the VAR suggested an upgrade. On review, Oliver agreed.

Sage’s reaction? He had a look of pure deflation. The tackle was bad enough but the need to make it was non-existent – Mateta was chasing a losing cause in Tottenham’s half against one of the quickest defenders in the league. Dismal.

Naturally, it shifted the game in Tottenham’s favour, if only to the effect of a one-goal lead by the break. As with Mateta’s dismissal, the Spurs breakthrough was avoidable for Palace, with Gray left unmarked at the far post before planting his head on Kudus’s high, looping corner.

The video analysis will do Sage no favours. Kudus’s delivery was excellent, that much is true, but five Tottenham men had gathered at the far post with only three markers – even factoring for the red card, the tracking of Gray was abysmal.

At half-time, De Zerbi substituted Gray, who was carrying a yellow card, and Spurs maintained momentum by creating openings for Tel, Matheus Fernandes, Jan Paul van Hecke and Solanke.

Palace were being pummelled but survived until Van Hecke’s finish for 2-0. As with the Chelsea win, Fernandes stood out in its creation with an excellent cross, from which Van Hecke powered a header at Dean Henderson.

The initial save was good, but the ball returned to Van Hecke, who was sat on his backside and able to steer his second header past Henderson. Sage could use similar inspiration from the floor.

Sports.title: Angry Oliver Glasner fumes at 's*** situation' in explosive rant: Nottingham Forest boss warns players they need to change or he'll be sacked and hits out at 'pattern' of problems
Sports.content:
Angry Oliver Glasner fumes at 's*** situation' in explosive rant: Nottingham Forest boss warns players they need to change or he'll be sacked and hits out at 'pattern' of problems

Nottingham Forest manager Oliver Glasner launched into an extraordinary rant after his team's 2-0 defeat at Brentford on Saturday left them second to bottom of the Premier League.

And Glasner made it clear that if things don't improve he will be sacked, or even walk away from the City Ground job.

Daily Mail Sport understands the under-fire Austrian is not happy with some of his players' attitudes and their response to his work since joining the club from Crystal Palace in the summer.

Glasner revealed that he had refused a request from one of his players to make his own way back to Nottingham from London after the game, banging the table at the press conference when revealing his dismay at the very idea.

'We have to accept it's not good enough,' he said. 'If we lose four of the last five games, it's not good enough. And that's why for me, it's now time that we change things, that I change things, and that's what I will do.

'Everywhere, and I feel I could see a few things from day number one. I feel now maybe I made too many compromises in some stuff, and it's always compromises.

Oliver Glasner made his feelings clear after the final whistle, with Forest in the bottom three

Striker Igor Thiago's goal secured the latest triumph for upwardly-mobile Brentford

'It's a clear way. I will tell [the players] what we want to do, what we have to do, and if the players buy in, I think we can have a turnaround, and if not, the sixth manager [since the start of last season] will come in.

‘I have no consequences. I think you see that. For me, I go home and have breakfast with my family. It's not the worst situation. Nobody needs to have pity with Oliver Glasner or with the manager. If I want, I could start in two weeks somewhere else. I won't do it.

'But, you know, the players, the staff, they remain in the same situation. And it's the same, sorry for the word, s*** situation that the club had last year.

'So you need to change and rebuild from the bottom to the top. And this is clear for me. And this is what I will do. And without any compromises. Zero. Zero. And if these things don't work, they will let me know [about my exit].'

The Bees had taken the lead after half an hour when Nikola Milenkovic steered the ball past his own goalkeeper. Igor Thiago continued his return to form as his second-half strike helped Brentford end their five-game wait for a win against the Midlands side.

For Glasner, it was all too much. 'I didn't come to Nottingham because I was bored at home,' he went on. 'No, I came to Nottingham to succeed. I came to Nottingham to get the visions of the owner and the fans and the club to reality. And therefore we need to have a bigger change than maybe I thought, to be honest.

'But again, when you're in a club, then you see what's going on. And I'm desperate to get this tournament around.

'But again, Oliver Glasner can't do anything alone. And I said this so often, and not just after a defeat. I always said the same after winning.

'It's not me, no, but we're all together and can do it. But I know where we have to go. And therefore, it's exactly this, being ruthless. And either you buy in or you leave. It's the only way.

'There is no compromise. Either you buy in where we want to go as a club. Because, and I mentioned it, if you're three times struggling, four or five Premier League seasons, struggling, being at the bottom of the league, there is a pattern.

'And I just know that Oliver Glasner is not here for five years. You see my mood, right? So, yes (I understand fans’ boos).

'And again, that's what should be expected. They say, hey, yes, we are nice. I paid the train ticket and the ticket here.

'And then, yeah, we're the same again. I think it's not, again, it's not a lack of effort, but there are a few things very obvious. And it's, let's say, we're talking about the realities.

'We are outrun by the opposition in every single game to change it. And if you can't change it, we need different personnel. And if the club doesn't want to change it, they need a different manager. I'm desperate to change it. Desperate.'

Sports.title: Michael Carrick future LIVE: Man Utd sack agreement as Eddie Howe 'responds to approach'
Sports.content:
After Manchester United were beaten by Chelsea in west London, Michael Carrick's position as manager appears to be under immense threat again

Michael Carrick is on the brink, yet again, after Manchester United imploded against Chelsea. Defeat to the Blues means that United are now without a win in nine matches and it looks a difficult position for Carrick to recover from.

The Red Devils would have gone into half-time with a 1-0 lead had Matheus Cunha not been fractionally offside in the opening 45 minutes. Then, in the second period, some weak defending allowed Morgan Rogers to waltz into the box and to dink the ball over Senne Lammens.

Lisandro Martinez went on to brainlessly push Wesley Fofana over, resulting in a penalty and a second yellow card being awarded. Cole Palmer squeezed his penalty through Lammens, and Chelsea eased their way to a 2-0 win.

Carrick may yet be afforded two more matches, against Roma and Aston Villa. But speculation over who could replace him will only ramp up with Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann among the names available.

Mirror Football will provide the latest news and updates regarding Carrick's future below.

Sports.title: Boy, 14, turns himself in to the police after vile Bradley Lowery taunt in Sunderland game
Sports.content:
Boy, 14, turns himself in to the police after vile Bradley Lowery taunt in Sunderland game

West Midlands Police have released a statement to confirm that a 14-year-old boy has turned himself in following a vile incident during Coventry's win over Sunderland

View 3 Images The fan appeared to hold up a photo of Bradley Lowery (Image: x.com/Roker Report)

A 14-year-old boy has turned himself in to the police after footage appeared to show a young Coventry supporter taunting Sunderland fans with a picture of Bradley Lowery.

‌



‌



Footage taken during Coventry's 3-1 Premier League win over Sunderland posted on social media went viral on Saturday. It appeared to show a young supporter showing the away fans a photograph of Lowery, a Sunderland fan who tragically died aged six in 2017 with cancer.

‌



The video sparked outrage, with Bradley's mum Gemma releasing a statement, and West Midlands Police have now given a significant update.

‌



A spokesperson said: “We are aware of a video circulating on social media showing an incident at Coventry City’s Premier League match with Sunderland yesterday afternoon. A thorough investigation has been launched, and a 14-year-old boy has since handed himself in and will be spoken with in due course.

“We understand the upset and outrage this video has caused in the community and to the victim’s family and our officers are keeping them up to date with the progress of our investigation and working closely alongside both football clubs.”

‌



Coventry City said in a statement: "Coventry City FC is aware of footage circulating on social media in connection with an incident during our Premier League fixture against Sunderland. The club does not tolerate offensive behaviour and will liaise with the relevant authorities to determine the appropriate course of action."

Bradley, who had neuroblastoma, touched the hearts of football fans with his bravery and his mum Gemma released an emotional statement on Sunday morning following the disgusting incident.

‌



View 3 Images Bradley Lowery was a passionate Sunderland fan (Image: PA)

She wrote: "My beautiful boy deserves to be remembered with love, not hate. Yesterday, a Coventry fan used a photograph of Bradley to taunt Sunderland supporters. As Bradley’s mam, this is heartbreaking, especially as it’s one of my favourite photographs of him. Just look at that smile.

‌



"I remember that day like it was yesterday. He was so happy, having so much fun. Those moments were precious because they were few and far between. So much of Bradley’s short life was spent battling cancer and enduring treatments no child should ever face. To see such a beautiful memory used in such a cruel way really does make my heart hurt."

She added: "We are a football-loving family who follow Sunderland home and away. I’m all for football banter, but surely mocking a child who died from cancer is not banter? I hope the club takes appropriate action and the young lad’s family help him understand how hurtful his actions were.

‌



View 3 Images Bradley Lowery died in 2017 (Image: PA)

“I don’t want hatred directed towards him, so please please don't, just for him to learn from this. Behind that photograph is a little boy who was loved beyond measure and a family who miss him every day. Thank you to everyone who has defended Bradley and shown us so much love. It means more than you know.

‌



"What some people don’t realise is that Bradley’s story didn’t end when his life did. Because of Bradley, children’s lives are being saved, hundreds of families have received vital support, and children facing unimaginable battles are being given hope.

"Through Super Brad’s Pad, families can escape hospital life, spend precious time together and make memories that last forever. That is Bradley’s legacy. The difference my little boy continues to make in this world. No amount of cruelty will ever take that away.

Article continues below

"So rather than let this photograph be remembered for hatred, I want it remembered for what it truly represents. My beautiful little boy, enjoying one of the happiest days of his life, with the biggest smile on his face. #CancerHasNoColours. That is how I want the world to remember him.”

Sports.title: Gary Neville singles out 'embarrassing' Arsenal star minutes into Liverpool clash
Sports.content:
Gary Neville singles out 'embarrassing' Arsenal star minutes into Liverpool clash

Gary Neville did not take long to dramatically call out one Arsenal player for their antics at the start of the north Londoners' away match against Liverpool

View 3 Images Gary Neville did not hold back on one Arsenal star (Image: 2026 James Gill - Danehouse)

Gary Neville slammed Arsenal defender Gabriel Magalhaes as "embarrassing" after an altercation with a Liverpool star.

‌



‌



It did not take long for the challenges to fly in between the Gunners and the Reds. In the early knockings, Gabriel and Alexander Isak clashed while battling for a loose ball.

‌



The Premier League's most expensive player made slight contact with Gabriel's head during their coming together. Once he sensed the contact, the Arsenal defender fell to the floor clutching his face.

Sports.title: Erling Haaland's true feelings on Man City future confirmed by dad after guilty verdict
Sports.content:
Erling Haaland's true feelings on Man City future confirmed by dad after guilty verdict

Manchester City are facing serious consequences for systematically breaking the Premier League's financial rules over a nine-year period, leaving players like Erling Haaland in an uncertain position

View 2 Images Alfie Haaland discussed his son's reaction to the guilty verdict (Image: Viaplay)

Erling Haaland is purely focused on playing for Manchester City and is not concerned by the possible punishment the club faces, according to his father Alfie.

‌



‌



City were found guilty of breaching the Premier League's financial rules over a nine-year period and are waiting the outcome of an appeal. An independent commission found the club guilty of 114 of the 115 charges, saying they had used "sham" contracts to disguise funding of more than £830million.

‌



The club have always maintained their innocence and are confident of clearing their name. But the bombshell verdict has cast a shadow of doubt over Enzo Maresca's side, who could be relegated as punishment for the club's past financial cheating.

‌



Haaland has reportedly been calming his teammates down about the potential consequences and his father has given an insight into the striker's mindset. "Erling thinks about playing as much football as he can and concentrates on that. I think it’s more those of us outside the pitch who think a bit more about it," Alfie told ViaPlay.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"Well, it has been circulating for quite a while, hasn’t it? So finally something came that was concrete, which it is possible to fight against for City as a club.

"Obviously, these are serious allegations, but now there is an appeal case pending to be heard, so I think we have to stay calm, keep our cool, and wait to see how it turns out."

‌



Haaland Snr was then asked whether he felt it would be unfair to punish the current players over financial irregularities which happened between 2009 and 2018. He replied: "Yes, in a way, one might feel that having to potentially take punishment for something done many years ago… yes, I would say so."

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



View 2 Images Erling Haaland could be relegated with Manchester City due to the guilty verdict (Image: Lewis Storey/Getty Images)

Asked if he knew anything more about the appeal, Alfie said: "Nothing more than what’s in the media. And there is an awful lot written there, and very one-sided, I would say, right? Because it's hard for Manchester City to come out right now – with an ongoing appeal – and defend themselves.

‌



"So we hope they get a fair hearing, and then we’ll see if they manage to prove that they are innocent, eventually. Now we just have to wait and see. I think they’ve done more than well to stand tall through this, because of course they have faced plenty of accusations. So I feel the player group has handled it very well.

"We also have to remember that these are things that allegedly happened quite a few years ago. The players today had nothing to do with it. So they’ve played well. They lost their last match, so it’s time to get back to winning ways."

Sports.title: Erik ten Hag reignites Cristiano Ronaldo feud with brutal message - 'It's over'
Sports.content:
Erik ten Hag reignites Cristiano Ronaldo feud with brutal message - 'It's over'

Erik ten Hag has been in the headlines after revealing why he fell out with Cristiano Ronaldo at Manchester United, and now he's taken another swipe at the 41-year-old

View 3 Images Erik ten Hag spoke candidly about Cristiano Ronaldo (Image: ESPN)

Erik ten Hag has once again hit out at Cristiano Ronaldo by claiming that the former Manchester United superstar hasn't been able to deliver for 'seven or eight years'. Ronaldo infamously fell out with Ten Hag during their five-month spell together at Old Trafford, leading to the forward's acrimonious exit.

‌



‌



The pair never saw eye-to-eye and Ten Hag lifted the lid on their relationship in a bombshell interview earlier this month. The ex-Red Devils boss accused Ronaldo of 'letting the team down' with his lack of effort in training while telling United's players to go against his instructions.

‌



On Sunday, Ten Hag appeared as a guest on Dutch programme Goedemorgen Eredivisie and fiercely criticised the five-time Ballon d'Or winner. "Every top team must embrace the top player, but the top player must work for the team," Ten Hag explained.

‌



"That was the problem with Ronaldo. The players wanted to work for him, because naturally they looked up to him. But for the last seven or eight years, he just hasn't been able to deliver. Since Juventus, it's simply over."

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe
