World.title: Arsenal go top after narrow win at Liverpool
World.content:
Arsenal record first win at Liverpool in 14 ttempts thanks to Kai Havertz goal

Share Arsenal win at Liverpool to go top of Premier League on social media

Arsenal went three points clear of Manchester City at the top of the English Premier League after a statement 1-0 win at Liverpool.

The Gunners had not won at Anfield since September 2012, when current coach Mikel Arteta captained the away side to a 2-0 victory, and had gone winless in their past 13 visits.

However, Kai Havertz turned home a low cross from Declan Rice after the home side were caught trying to play out from the back to silence the Kop on 16 minutes. The visitors withstood wave after wave of pressure from Andoni Iraola’s side thereafter.

Liverpool responded strongly with Florian Wirtz curling a free kick against the bar and Alexis Mac Allister heading a good chance over.

Arsenal weathered the storm, though, and defended superbly to keep Liverpool largely at arm’s length after the break, denying the home side a shot on target for the second meeting in succession.

Arteta’s side replaces Manchester City at the top with 24 points from nine games, with City on 21 after losing at home to Brighton and Hove Albion on Saturday.

Liverpool’s second league defeat of the season left them nine points behind Arsenal in fifth place.

World.title: How will the Iran war shape the outcome of the US midterm vote?
World.content:
The conflict has become a central issue ahead of Tuesday’s polls.

The war on Iran has emerged as a major campaign issue in the United States midterm elections.

Voters are preparing to cast their ballots on Tuesday, November 3, and for many, the effects of the Iran conflict at home are top of mind.

Fuel prices have skyrocketed, driving up the prices of other goods, too.

Polls suggest many Democrats – and Republicans – say this conflict was not worth the consequences.

So will the election shift the Senate and House of Representatives in Democrats’ favour? And what would that mean for the rest of President Donald Trump’s time in the White House?

Presenter: Mohammed Jamjoom

Guests:

Hassan Ahmadian – Associate professor at the University of Tehran and deputy director of the Middle East Scientific and Strategic Studies Center

Patrick Mara – Chairman of the Washington, DC Republican Party

James Butler – Democratic Party strategist

World.title: France opens ‘attempted murder’ probe into petrol bomb attacks on police
World.content:
No arrests made after several security officers were reportedly injured during incidents at Saturday’s protests.

Prosecutors in France have launched an investigation into attempted murder after petrol bombs were thrown at security forces during protests in Paris, as video of an officer in flames provoked outrage.

The probe announced on Sunday came after the Paris police prefecture said several hundred rioters had attacked security forces with projectiles, including a Molotov cocktail.

On Saturday, clashes erupted in Paris and other cities as hundreds of thousands of people staged a third weekend of protests against soaring living costs and deteriorating public services.

Video and images from the demonstrations showed a homemade incendiary device exploding at the feet of a security officer in protective gear, engulfing his lower body in flames.

Prosecutors said the investigation was opened for “attempted murder of persons vested with public authority”.

“Explosive devices were thrown at around 15 gendarmes as well as police officers,” the prosecutor’s office said, referring to military police officers who are part of the French armed forces.

While riots were less widespread than two weeks ago, when France experienced some of its worst unrest in years, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said on Saturday that the level of violence perpetrated by some was “extraordinary”.

An assessment of the injured was ongoing, prosecutors said, adding that the reported injuries included second-degree burns.

No suspects arrested yet

The gendarme struck said his unit was “under assault”, with glass bottles, paving stones, shards of glass and firebombs thrown at them.



“We were hit by several significant incendiary devices,” he told broadcaster RTL on condition of anonymity.

“The flammable substance was so greasy that I could feel it spreading across my skin,” he said. “I kept wondering when it would stop because I really felt as though I had been coated by the heat itself.”

The officer, who received minor injuries, said the leg and shin protections on his riot uniform melted.

The gendarmerie said 13 members of the officer’s unit were injured, according to RTL.

No suspects “have been arrested at this stage in connection with the incident”, the prosecutor’s office said, adding that investigators were working to identify those responsible.

More than 770 people were arrested across France, the interior ministry said.

A total of 159 members of law enforcement were injured during protests and Halloween celebrations, it added.

The protests come in a tense political climate, with presidential elections six months away and far-right frontrunner Marine Le Pen vowing to restore law and order if elected next year.

Le Pen, the leader of the far-right National Rally party, said on X that those responsible for the firebomb attack must be “punished with the utmost severity”.

World.title: Michigan Dem Haley Stevens endorses Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers
World.content:
Stevens lost the Democratic primary to Abdul El-Sayed, and she is now endorsing his Republican opponent in the Senate race.

In a blow to Democrat Abdul El-Sayed’s campaign for the United States Senate in Michigan, his former primary opponent, US Representative Haley Stevens, has endorsed Republican candidate Mike Rogers.

Stevens stunned party officials on Sunday by appearing with Rogers at a Detroit church service as tensions between her and El-Sayed boiled over two days before the election that will determine the balance of power on Capitol Hill.

“I am endorsing Mike Rogers for the US Senate. Today, I do not belong to Abdul’s campaign,” she said in a video posted on X.

Stevens’ surprising support for US President Donald Trump’s endorsed candidate in the tightly contested race comes after she was uninvited to a joint event on the same day with El-Sayed, who defeated her by a slim margin in the August primary.

“Who we are as Michiganders is not hate, and [that] is not what we are getting out of our Democratic nominee right now,” Stevens said.

World.title: Sullivan vows to honour Alaska race outcome, US judge dismisses DOJ lawsuit
World.content:
Senator Sullivan’s pledge contrasts with the Trump administration’s effort to challenge Alaska’s election certification, if he loses.

Republican Senator Dan S. Sullivan has vowed to accept the election outcome days after the United States Department of Justice filed a lawsuit seeking to decertify the results of the upcoming US Senate race there if the Republican incumbent loses.

“I’m going to accept the election results,” Sullivan, an ally of US President Donald Trump, told CNN on Sunday.

Sullivan’s promise comes just two days before the November 3 midterm election, which will determine control of the US Congress.

He said he was confident of winning, accusing his Democratic opponent Mary Peltola, who is attempting to unseat him, of cheating.

“My opponent and [Senate Minority Leader Chuck] Schumer and his aides are showing complete disrespect for Alaskans, complete disdain in recognising that they couldn’t run on their record, so they had to cheat. And now that that’s been exposed,” he said.

A New York Times report on Wednesday alleged that members of Peltola’s campaign helped recruit a retired teacher named Dan J Sullivan Jr to run for the Senate seat as a spoiler candidate in an attempt to draw votes away from Senator Sullivan.

The report seems to have prompted the Trump administration’s renewed legal push to bar Alaska from certifying its election results, should Senator Sullivan lose.

On Sunday, US District Court Judge Sharon Gleason dismissed the lawsuit, citing it as “infeasible” because many voters had already cast their ballots and the ballots have now been commingled to the point where the identity of each voter cannot be determined.



“More fundamentally, the United States provides no workable plan as to how it proposes to segregate ballots cast for Daniel J. Sullivan on Election Day and then conduct a court-ordered unspecified “investigation” of those ballots in a manner that would preserve voter secrecy,” she wrote.

The Justice Department said on Sunday that it plans to appeal Gleason’s ruling.

The second Sullivan is listed on the ballot as Daniel J Sullivan Jr, while the senator is listed as Dan S Sullivan and marked as a Republican incumbent.

Peltola has insisted she had nothing to do with recruiting the other Sullivan and has called attention to it a “distraction” from the main issues facing Alaskans — namely, high prices caused by US-Israel war on Iran. Her campaign has also denied involvement.

Before a rally on Friday, Peltola was asked whether someone on her campaign could have been involved in recruiting the other Sullivan. “I have no idea,” she told KTUU. “I honestly have no idea.”

Senator Sullivan doubted Peltola’s claims.

“There is no way this went on for a year that they weren’t informing her,” Sullivan told the CNN news programme State of the Union. “She got caught lying, and she’s still lying to the Alaskan people, the media, to all of us.”

Alaska’s Senate race is one of seven key toss-ups that will likely decide whether Republicans keep their majority in the US Congress’s upper chamber.

Both candidates have spent the final days campaigning through Alaska’s vast landscape.

On Saturday night, Senator Sullivan handed out candy at a “trunk-or-treat” event at a recreation centre north of Anchorage, where he quipped his costume was “the real Dan Sullivan”.

World.title: Israel’s first ambassador to Somaliland presents credentials in Hargeisa
World.content:
Israel expands ties with the breakaway territory as Somalia challenges its motives and war intensifies in Yemen.

Share Israel’s first ambassador to Somaliland presents credentials in Hargeisa on social media

Israel’s first ambassador to Somaliland has presented his credentials to the breakaway territory’s president, who formally accepted them at a ceremony in Hargeisa, where officials also laid the cornerstone for an Israeli embassy.

Israel’s Foreign Ministry announced the ceremonies on Sunday, saying they were held last week.

The move puts into practice an agreement reached on December 26, 2025, when Israel became the first United Nations member state to recognise Somaliland, It declared independence from Somalia in 1991 but remains claimed by Mogadishu.

Describing it as a “historical day,” President Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi, known as Cirro, said during the ceremony that it was the first time a Somaliland president had received the credentials of an ambassador from a UN member state recognising its independence.

Ambassador Michael Lotem said Israel’s recognition acknowledged what Somaliland had built over 35 years, rather than serving as a mere diplomatic formality.

Somaliland has governed itself for more than three decades, but remains without recognition from any other UN member state.

Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa’ar said in a statement on Sunday that the exchange of ambassadors fulfilled commitments made when relations were established.

Sa’ar visited Somaliland in January and the territory opened an embassy in West Jerusalem during Cirro’s visit to Israel in June.

At the ceremony in Hargeisa, Cirro stressed the broader importance of the relationship.

“Given our strategic position around the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden, our cooperation carries important regional and international significance. Let me reaffirm that Somaliland approaches this relationship with genuine strategic commitment and a long-term perspective,” he said.



Somaliland lies across the Gulf of Aden from Yemen, near the Bab al-Mandeb strait, the vital shipping passage between the Red Sea and Indian Ocean.

Fighting has intensified on the Yemeni side of the strait in recent weeks.

On October 9, United Nations envoy Hans Grundberg warned that Yemen had returned to full-scale war, with battles involving the Iran-aligned Houthi movement and forces of the internationally recognised government.

Israel has also acknowledged a security relationship that predates its diplomatic recognition.

During Cirro’s visit to Israel in June, Defence Minister Israel Katz said the two sides had cooperated on secret operations for years and wanted to expand their security ties.

Somalia’s President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud challenged Israel’s motives in an interview with Sky News this week, saying it was seeking access to the Red Sea rather than supporting Somaliland’s independence.

“Israel wants the Red Sea, that is the only reason,” he said.

Mohamud also alleged that Israel wants a naval base in the territory.

Somaliland officials have signalled openness to hosting an Israeli military base, but the territory’s president recently said no talks had been held.

Somalia condemned Israel’s recognition of Somaliland in December as a violation of its sovereignty.

Israel’s move has also been condemned by the Arab League, African Union and Organisation of Islamic Cooperation.

World.title: Hebron siege continues for 10th day as Israel threatens wider offensive
World.content:
Israeli forces are maintaining their siege on Hebron for the 10th consecutive day, threatening to expand their offensive and forcing more Palestinian families from their homes.

The lockdown in the occupied West Bank city was enforced after an attack on October 23 near Hebron in which two Israeli soldiers were killed.

More than 3,300 Palestinians have since been displaced or affected, with homes destroyed and businesses shut, according to the local municipality.

Mayor Yousef al-Jabari told Al Jazeera on Saturday that daily economic losses were estimated to exceed 12 million shekels ($3.8m), with more than $1.9m worth of damage to infrastructure, along with losses in the health and environmental sectors estimated at about $160,000.

He said Israeli forces have demolished 15 homes and other structures and forced 327 businesses to close. About 80,000 students have been unable to attend school for 10 days, he added.

The mayor said Hebron accounts for about 40 percent of the Palestinian economy and the siege amounts to “collective punishment”.

Palestinian families in and around the city fear the army could soon extend its attacks.

Raids and settler attacks

Israeli arrests of Palestinians in Hebron and other cities in the occupied West Bank continued on Sunday.

Israeli forces arrested 10 Palestinian teachers in Masafer Yatta, south of Hebron and seized their vehicle, reported the Palestinian news agency Wafa.

Video shared by Palestinian media and verified by Al Jazeera showed the Israeli military raiding a school run by the United Nations in the Shufat refugee camp in occupied East Jerusalem.



The United Nations humanitarian office, OCHA, said Israeli settlers carried out 397 attacks on Palestinians across the occupied West Bank in October, the highest monthly figure since monitoring began in 2006, Wafa said.

Between October 20 and 26, settler attacks targeted 49 Palestinian communities, mostly while Palestinians harvested olives on their land.

Nine children were among 57 Palestinians injured by settlers and Israeli forces: 34 by military gunfire and physical assaults and 23 in settler attacks.

Since the start of 2015, Israeli authorities have issued 9,518 demolition or stop-work notices against Palestinian property in the occupied West Bank, reported the Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission. The Palestinian government commission added that 344 of those notices were given in the first nine months of this year.

World.title: Al Jazeera marks 30 years of transforming news in Middle East and beyond
World.content:
Share Al Jazeera marks 30 years of transforming news in Arab world and beyond on social media

Al Jazeera marks 30 years of transforming news in Middle East and beyond

Doha, Qatar – As Al Jazeera marks its 30th anniversary with a special commemorative event, the media network’s history is a timeline of milestones and challenges – from risks, obstacles and attacks, to international awards and recognition from the communities whose stories it strives to tell.

Launched on November 1, 1996, the network broke new ground in Arab broadcasting, bringing previously marginalised political perspectives into the mainstream and creating space for debate on issues seldom openly discussed on regional television.

On Sunday, the network hosted an event to commemorate its enduring legacy at its headquarters in the Qatari capital, Doha, attended by the Emir of Qatar Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani and other delegates.

Since its launch, Al Jazeera was not “just a screen”, said Al Jazeera’s Director General Sheikh Nasser bin Faisal Al Thani at the anniversary event. “It was a promise that journalism can be free and responsible, and that ‘opinion and the other opinion’ is not just a slogan, but it’s a position you take.”

For three decades, Al Jazeera “has helped transform the way news is covered in the Arab world”, Director of News Raed Fakih said in a statement, hailing the network for making room for “voices, issues and perspectives that had not been given the space they deserved”.

“Today, as we mark Al Jazeera’s 30th anniversary, we are building on that editorial legacy to broaden the scope of our coverage and give greater prominence to a wider range of events and viewpoints,” he added.

The anniversary coincides with a significant restructuring of Al Jazeera Media Network’s Arabic-language news services, separating rolling breaking news coverage, live event broadcasting, and more in-depth reporting across three channels.



Risks, obstacles and attacks

Since Qatar’s late Father Emir Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani launched the independent channel – a first in the Arab world – the network has promised to provide “the opinion and the other opinion”.

It launched its first TV broadcast as an Arabic-language satellite news channel in 1996 from Doha and has since then grown into the Al Jazeera Media Network, with several outlets in multiple languages. A private corporation for public benefit, the network now includes television channels, websites and other digital platforms.

But as governments have banned it, and as its offices have been bombed in many parts of the world, the network has exacted a huge cost for staying on air.

Yet it has been instrumental in covering key events in the last three decades in the region and beyond.

In 2001, when the United States attacked Afghanistan, Al Jazeera was the only foreign broadcaster in Kabul, its updates and pictures travelling the world.

Then in 2011, millions followed the Arab Spring uprising live on Al Jazeera. Its coverage won a prestigious Peabody Award.

However, the network’s reporting has led to numerous threats over the years. Exclusive pictures have made Al Jazeera hard to ignore, but have also made the network a target.

In 2003, a US strike hit its Baghdad office, killing correspondent Tareq Ayyoub. Two dozen Al Jazeera journalists have been killed since.

In 2022, an Israeli soldier shot Palestinian correspondent Shireen Abu Akleh in Jenin, the 12th Al Jazeera journalist killed in 19 years. Another 12 were then killed in just 30 months, every one of them by Israel during its genocidal war in Gaza.

One of them was Anas al-Sharif, who for many viewers was the face of the war. In August 2025, an Israeli strike killed him and four colleagues as it hit a press tent outside al-Shifa Hospital.

“To the martyrs of Al Jazeera, to our colleagues who departed while carrying out their duties, we say to them today, you are part and parcel of Al Jazeera’s promise,” Al Jazeera’s Sheikh Nasser said at the event on Sunday.

Meanwhile, across the region, governments have closed the network’s bureaus and pulled the channel’s licences.

In 2024, Israel banned the network and raided its Ramallah office. Months later, the Palestinian Authority suspended it.

Overall, at least nine governments have tried to silence Al Jazeera.

A new technological era

Despite the challenges, Al Jazeera’s broadcast continues, with more than 3,000 staff working out of more than 70 bureaus across the globe.



Alongside its digital divisions, as well as its English channel that launched in 2006, Al Jazeera reaches more than 430 million homes.

The network on Sunday also launched The Core, an artificial intelligence (AI) initiative first announced in December 2025 in collaboration with Google Cloud. The initiative aims to integrate AI into newsroom operations, helping journalists manage information, coordinate coverage and make better use of the network’s reporting archives.

Meanwhile, Al Jazeera Balkans was also relaunched in a new digital-first format, opening a new chapter in its journalism in the region.

While the network’s shelves are packed with hundreds of awards, it continues its mission of serving as a voice of the voiceless.

World.title: French officials eye social media’s role in promoting unrest.
World.content:
Pinned

Hundreds of thousands of protesters took to the streets in cities across France again on Saturday, the latest expression of national grievance that has led to clashes between protesters and the police and kept the country on edge.

As dusk fell and official rallies wound down, unauthorized marches splintered off in Paris, stoking fresh fears of chaos as night approached.

Adding to those fears: Halloween, which falls on Saturday. The French authorities, citing calls on social media for people to revolt that encouraged them to wear masks and costumes, warned that the risk of a new outbreak of violence was high.

In Paris, tensions began flaring between protesters and the police in the late afternoon, as officers fired tear gas at people who refused to disperse. The Paris police estimated that 70,000 people marched in the demonstration, compared with 110,000 last Saturday. After the main demonstration ended, hundreds of protesters, many masked and clad in black, formed an unauthorized procession in eastern Paris.

The interior ministry estimated that nationwide, 320,000 people demonstrated, compared with 410,000 last week. Protesters and the police also clashed in Marseille, Lyon, Toulouse, and Rennes.

Corentin Schnell, a 19-year-old engineering student, took part in the unauthorized march in Paris because, he said, he was angered by accounts of the police using tear gas and stun grenades against protesters in past weeks. “I’ve come to demonstrate and to try to provide medical care — to limit the damage, regardless of which side it’s on,” he said.

Earlier in the week, France’s interior minister, Laurent Nuñez, promised to deploy 70,000 police officers, matching the numbers on Oct. 24. That operation helped keep a lid on outbreaks of arson and looting, although then, too, there were clashes as the police tried to disperse the crowds in the evening.

There was ample fuel for a repeat of those combustible scenes. Students, who are returning to school on Monday after a two-week break, were not mollified by the government’s initial response to their demands. The Education Ministry agreed to cap some class sizes, offer low-interest loans to rebuild school buildings and phase out an unpopular online college admissions platform.

The students vowed to go on protesting. Their two-month-old movement has grown to include university students, public workers and veterans of the “yellow vest” movement that convulsed France from 2018 to 2020.

The authorities have said they are most worried about trouble breaking out after nightfall.

“We are seeing numerous calls to gather coming from the far left, the radicalized extreme left, and from certain radicalized ‘yellow vests’ websites, which are urging people to attend rallies or public gatherings starting at 8 p.m. in many cities across France,” Mr. Nuñez said at a news conference.

Some of the messages were violent, Mr. Nuñez said, calling for “revolution” and “insurrection.” Those gatherings will be forbidden, and any attempt to gather despite the ban will lead to arrests, he said.

Demonstrators have been encouraged on social media to turn up wearing Halloween costumes. Mr. Nuñez warned that it was a criminal offense to conceal one’s face during a demonstration that disrupted public order.

Here’s what else to know.

Social media: French officials are increasingly concerned about social media’s role in attracting people and inciting violent behavior. Speculation that the government considered temporarily suspending several popular sites drew a denial from President Emmanuel Macron himself. Read more ›

Far-right activists: While the government has blamed far-left activists for much of the mayhem, officials confirmed that bands of young men with links to the far right have also infiltrated the demonstrations. They use the pretext of protecting shop owners but often clash with far-left groups.

Widening movement: The nationwide unrest in France began with a handful of student demonstrations at high schools in suburban Paris last month. Read more ›

Giulia Imbert contributed reporting.

Far-right activists: While the government has blamed far-left activists for much of the mayhem, officials confirmed that bands of young men with links to the far right have also infiltrated the demonstrations. They use the pretext of protecting shop owners but often clash with far-left groups.

Widening movement: The nationwide unrest in France began with a handful of student demonstrations at high schools in suburban Paris last month. Read more ›

Giulia Imbert contributed reporting.

World.title: Shops looted as German cost-of-living protests turn violent
World.content:
Rioters looted shops in central Frankfurt late on Saturday as clashes erupted in German cities over the cost of living.

Besides Frankfurt - Germany's financial hub - there were incidents of violence in Berlin, Cologne and Hamburg, with police saying they used water cannon to disperse protesters who were targeting emergency workers with fireworks, stones and bottles.

Thousands joined largely peaceful demonstrations earlier in the day. They were organised by the campaign group Gen Z regelt - meaning "Gen Z takes charge" - to protest against underfunding in schools, the high cost of living, public spending cuts and military service.

The unrest in Germany follows similar youth-led mass protests in France, where more than 320,000 people also demonstrated on Saturday.

On Sunday, Germany's Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt told Bild newspaper that overnight police had prevented "violence like that seen in Paris" in recent weeks and called for "harsh punishments" for rioters and looters.

Overnight, a large section of Frankfurt's main shopping street was closed off by police. A police spokesperson said many arrests were made in the city.

Authorities in Frankfurt, Munich and Berlin reported as many as 18,000 protesters, roughly half of what the organisers had estimated on their website. German media say tens of thousands protested in German cities on Saturday.

Gen Z regelt spokesperson Lina Friedrich said the demonstrations were "to fight for peace and freedom, rather than for war and coercion".

She said: "What matters most to us is better support for the health and education systems. We are against compulsory military service and we are in favour of a fairer distribution of the burden."

World.title: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill eight including child, hospitals say
World.content:
Israeli strikes in Gaza have killed at least eight people, including a child, according to hospitals, despite a year-old ceasefire.

In Gaza City to the north, hospital officials said a missile attack hit a group of civilians next to Cairo School in the Al-Rimal neighbourhood, killing three people, including a four-year-old boy.

In the southern city of Khan Younis, the Hamas-run ministry of interior said a drone attack targeted a group of police officers in the Al-Mawasi area, killing five, as they were carrying out their routine duties.

The Israeli military said it had carried out two attacks on what it described as military operatives but has not yet provided evidence or further information.

Outside Gaza City's Shifa Hospital, video showed a crowd of men gathered to pray next to two body bags and the tiny body of the child, which was wrapped in a white towel.

"My son and his child were martyred. They were sitting in their tent, bothering no one, and nothing else was happening in the area when suddenly, a missile struck them, and they were martyred," Ali Oweis told AFP news agency. "There is no ceasefire; the war is ongoing, don't you see?"

At Nasser hospital in Khan Younis, women despaired as body bags lay on the floor, video showed. The interior ministry named the five police officers killed, who were between the ages of 23 and 53, and called the attack a "horrific massacre".

A ceasefire came into force in Gaza in October last year, but Israeli air strikes have continued almost every day.

Since then, 1,580 people have been killed, according to Gaza's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN. Israel says it is targeting Hamas, but often civilians are also killed.

Meanwhile, a peace plan for Gaza, brokered by the Trump administration, has stalled.

The ceasefire saw thousands of Palestinians held by Israel released in return for all of the 48 remaining hostages held in Gaza, and an agreement to end the war.

The conflict was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed and 251 taken hostage.

Since the war began, 74,594 people have been killed in Gaza, according to the territory's health ministry.

Additional reporting by Jacob Phillips

World.title: University of Cambridge scientist among those who died in Spanish train crash
World.content:
An award-winning University of Cambridge researcher died in the Spanish train disaster while on her way to collect a prize for scientific excellence.

Dr Marta Shahbazi was travelling to an awards ceremony on Wednesday when the train she was on crashed into another near Urda, south of Madrid, killing 69 people.

The mother of two was an affiliate associate professor leading a group of researchers at MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology (LMB) in Cambridge and had earned several awards for work on human embryos and cell biology.

In a statement, the LMB paid tribute to the "inspiring, talented and passionate scientist" and described her death as a "profound shock and a huge loss".

The expert in cell biology ran the Shahbazi Laboratory at the LMB, based on the Cambridge Biomedical Campus.

She had been announced as the winner of a Spanish Society for Developmental Biology award for her contributions to the study of early human development and was due to collect the award at a conference in El Rompido in Andalusia.

The LMB said: "As a wife and mother of two young children, Marta wrote eloquently about balancing her family and career, serving as a much-admired role model for a 'mother scientist', a term she used to describe herself.

"Marta was an inspiring, talented and passionate scientist whose research shed light on the earliest steps in the development of human embryos and how errors occur that lead to failed pregnancies," the LMB said.

The institute said her death was "a profound shock and a huge loss for LMB".

Her work had been recognised with "many awards and prizes", the laboratory added.

World.title: Armed police start patrols in Sydney after Bondi Beach attack
World.content:
Heavily-armed police officers have started patrolling Sydney's streets, as part of heightened security measures following last year's deadly shooting at Bondi Beach.

The Armed Response Command (ARC) will see specially trained officers in busy tourist areas carrying long-arm rifles â an unfamiliar sight for most residents.

New South Wales police say the officers will also patrol major events like sports matches and places of worship "to prevent, deter and rapidly respond to serious threats, including active armed offender incidents".

Fifteen people - including a 10-year-old girl â were killed in December when two gunmen opened fire on an event marking the Jewish festival of Hanukkah at the popular beach.

The attack was Australia's worst mass shooting in almost three decades and prompted sweeping gun law reforms and a crackdown on hate speech.

One resident told ABC news that the sight of armed police was "unnerving".

"They are just everywhere. Those guns are huge."

But another woman told the broadcaster that seeing police with weapons made her feel safe.

ARC is specifically designed to be "highly visible across Sydney, driving specialist vehicles and carrying rifles," New South Wales police said in a statement.

Its role "is built on a simple principle - preserving life," Detective Superintendent Andrew Evans said.

The shooting on 14 December put huge pressure on Prime Minister Anthony Albanese's government, with calls for immediate action on antisemitism.

Jewish communities have welcomed the new police operation, which will eventually consist of 250 officers, but others have called for safeguards to protect human rights.

"No Australian wants to see officers with military weapons on our streets, but the sight of body bags is far worse," Alex Ryvchin, co-CEO of Executive Council of Australian Jewry, said.

But Amnesty International Australia said it was concerned about the "militarisation of policing", and asked for assurances from the state government that ARC will not be used to suppress peaceful protests.

"Any expansion of police powers and capabilities must be accompanied by clear, publicly accessible rules, robust independent oversight and accountability," said the organisation's Andrew Witheford.

The New South Wales administration defended the new measures.

"Our world changed forever. That's just the truth of it, right across this country. And I said it at the time, we will never be the same again," the state's Police Minister Yasmin Catley told the ABC.

One of the alleged gunmen, Naveed Akram, has been charged with 78 offences including 15 counts of murder, 40 counts of attempted murder, and one count of committing a terrorist act.

His father, Sajid Akram, 50 - who was also armed and shot at the crowd on Bondi Beach - was killed by police at the scene.

World.title: Democrat endorses Republican candidate in key Michigan Senate race as party spat escalates
World.content:
A Democrat in Michigan has endorsed the Republican candidate in the state's crucial US Senate contest, as a spat with her own party's candidate Abdul El-Sayed escalated just days before the vote.

Haley Stevens, a sitting congresswoman who lost out on the Democratic Senate nomination to El-Sayed, made a surprise appearance alongside the Republican candidate Mike Rogers at a church on Sunday.

"I don't belong in Abdul's campaign," she said in a video posted to X shortly after that appearance. "Who we are as Michiganders is not hate and is not what we are getting out from our Democratic nominee right now."

"That's why I am endorsing Mike Rogers," Stevens said.

Stevens also said El-Sayed had told her she was no longer welcome in his campaign.

"This is a very close election, we all know that, but Abdul made clear that I was not welcome in his campaign, that he didn't need me there, that he didn't want me there," Stevens told reporters after the Sunday church service.

The pair had been scheduled to appear together at a different event on Sunday, but El-Sayed reportedly asked her not to come.

They had clashed publicly over a campaign advert from an outside liberal group which blamed Israel for high food prices. El-Sayed criticised the advert and said he had nothing to do with its contents.

World.title: India's opposition holds mega rally seeking election chief's resignation
World.content:
Tens of thousands gathered in Delhi for a rally demanding the resignation of India's chief election commissioner over a controversial revision of voter lists.

Organised by the opposition INDIA bloc and led by Rahul Gandhi's Congress party, the protest drew many of the alliance's most prominent leaders in a show of strength against Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government.

Protesters waved flags and chanted "Save the vote, save the country" and "Vote thief, give up power".

It was the latest in a series of protests over electoral roll revision that the opposition says has removed eligible voters to benefit the Bharatiya Janata Party. The BJP and the Election Commission deny the allegations.

The crowds gathered at Ramlila Maidan, a sprawling ground in central Delhi known for hosting major political and cultural events. Some protesters sang and danced to patriotic Bollywood songs, while others waited beneath a large canopy in the colours of the Indian flag to hear opposition leaders speak.

Gandhi and several senior opposition leaders arrived at the venue in an open jeep, travelling through crowds of cheering supporters.

The event was also attended by Congress leaders Sonia Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge, alongside leaders of regional parties such as Mamata Banerjee, Akhilesh Yadav, Mehbooba Mufti, Supriya Sule and Tejashwi Yadav.

Addressing the crowds, Rahul Gandhi said those gathered had sent a message to Modi, Home Minister Amit Shah and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

"This is not the voice of a single political party or of politicians. It is the voice of India's youth, women, farmers and workers," he said.

"We will not allow democracy to be destroyed in India. We will not allow the constitution to be destroyed."

Other opposition leaders echoed Gandhi's criticism of the Election Commission. Congress president Kharge said the alliance would continue its campaign until Kumar resigned, while Banerjee pledged to keep fighting against what she described as threats to democracy.

Speaking to reporters in Delhi on Sunday, senior BJP leader and federal minister JP Nadda accused the opposition of trying to create unrest and destabilise the government under the guise of defending democracy.

He described the rally as a "calculated conspiracy to plunge the nation into anarchy - in the name of democracy".

World.title: Crypto firm Binance covers 90% of losses after $6.3bn hack
World.content:
Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, says it has covered 90% of the $6.3bn (Â£4.7bn) assets stolen in a hack on Thursday.

The remaining 10% may take longer to source in the required amounts, the company added.

Binance has consistently pledged to cover 100% of the losses from what is suspected to be crypto's biggest hack on record and said it has set aside more than $6.34bn in company funds to do so.

"Binance will absorb the financial impact of these stolen funds, not our users," the company said in a statement on Saturday.

In an update on Sunday, Binance said withdrawals had been restored on several of its networks, after they were suspended following the hack.

It previously said withdrawals would be resumed in phases.

The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) said on Saturday that North Korea was responsible for the attack.

The FBI said it had observed hackers converting stolen assets into a type of cryptocurrency called Ethereum and that it is expected that the assets will then be converted again using decentralised finance and instant swap services.

Two analytics firms previously told the BBC they had robust intelligence pointing to North Korean state-backed hacking unit the Lazarus Group, also known as TraderTraitor - which was specifically named by the FBI - as the likely culprits.

Speaking to reporters on Saturday night, US President Donald Trump said, external the US is still unsure who the culprits are.

"We're learning about it. We don't know if it's North Korea - but if it is, we'll talk to North Korea about it," he said.

Binance said it had replenished the stolen assets using various funds and its own corporate treasury.

All holdings of the cryptocurrencies bitcoin, Ethereum and Tether are covered, along with seven other widely-traded crypto assets, the company said.

The hack is believed to be the largest in history, eclipsing the record of a $1.5bn heist on the Bybit exchange in 2025 - for which the FBI also said North Korea was responsible.

North Korea has always denied involvement in these attacks.

World.title: Judge dismisses Trump's lawsuit against Wall Street Journal over Epstein birthday book
World.content:
A US judge has thrown out President Donald Trump's $10bn (Â£7.4bn) lawsuit against The Wall Street Journal, ruling the suit was "grasping at straws".

Trump had sued the media outlet's parent company Dow Jones and its leader Rupert Murdoch last year after it reported on a letter allegedly written by Trump to disgraced financier and sex offender Jeffrey Epstein as part of a birthday book in 2003, before Epstein was charged with sex crimes.

Trump has denied writing or signing the letter, which included suggestive language and a drawing of the outline of a woman's body.

Judge Darrin Gayles threw out the case, finding the suit runs counter to the First Amendment, which protects freedom of the press.

Gayles had already once dismissed the defamation lawsuit, which sought $20 billion in damages. Trump's team refiled the suit seeking $10 billion, and this time, the judge threw out the case "with prejudice," meaning the suit cannot be filed again.

The news outlet's story about Epstein's 50th birthday book, external - and the letter with Trump's name - came as the Trump administration battled intense bipartisan criticism over the summer for its handling of Epstein documents.

Trump had said the newspaper had slandered him and violated libel laws in publishing the article.

In his 20-page ruling, Gayles noted the paper's "thoughtful and detailed âinvestigation" that led to the story and said the lawsuit was "grasping at âstraws" to "manufacture flaws" in their work.

World.title: Okorocha chasing shadows, Uzodimma says, vows to appeal court judgement
World.content:
Imo State Governor Hope Uzodimma has vowed to appeal the Federal High Court judgement recognising his predecessor, Rochas Okorocha, as the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate for Imo West Senatorial District in the 2027 elections, describing the former governor as “chasing shadows”.

Mr Uzodimma’s Chief Press Secretary, Oguike Nwachuku, said the governor considered the judgement a “travesty of justice” and was confident it would be overturned by the Court of Appeal.

“Obviously, the Governor will appeal the judgement which is a travesty of justice,” Mr Nwachuku told PREMIUM TIMES on Friday in response to questions about Mr Okorocha’s allegations against the governor and his (Okorocha) account of the disputed APC senatorial primary.

The governor’s response followed Mr Okorocha’s appearance on Arise News’ Prime Time on Thursday, where he claimed that he remained the dominant political figure in the APC in Imo State and accused Mr Uzodimma of relying on documents containing irregularities to secure the party’s senatorial ticket.

Mr Okorocha had declared that “the structure of APC in Imo State is Rochas”, insisting that his political influence in the state remained intact despite opposition from the governor’s camp.

In a PREMIUM TIMES report the former governor also alleged that documents supporting Mr Uzodimma’s emergence as the party’s candidate contained inconsistencies, including discrepancies in the primary’s date, the description of the exercise as a consensus arrangement and result sheets allegedly completed by one person across 144 wards and 12 local government areas.

Mr Nwachuku, however, dismissed Mr Okorocha’s account and insisted that the governor won the primary by an overwhelming margin.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Uzodimma’s account of the primary

According to the governor’s spokesperson, there was a direct primary in Imo West because Mr Okorocha rejected the consensus arrangement adopted in the other two senatorial districts.

He said political stakeholders in Owerri Zone, which produces the Imo East senatorial seat, and Okigwe Zone, which produces Imo North, opted for consensus arrangements that produced Prince Alex Mbata and Senator Patrick Ndubueze, respectively.

Mr Nwachuku said Mr Okorocha insisted on contesting against Mr Uzodimma across the 12 local government areas in Imo West.

He insisted that the governor won the contest with 230,464 votes against Mr Okorocha’s 1,098 votes.

The spokesperson said officials of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) were present during the exercise, while the APC National Assembly Primary Election Committee, led by its chairman and returning officer, Williams Kayoda a retired rear admiral supervised the process across the local government areas.

He maintained that the outcome was legitimate and accused Mr Okorocha of attempting to undermine the APC by challenging the result.

“Rochas Okorocha is simply chasing shadows and intentionally working against the interest of the APC he claims to be a founding member and the re-election of President Bola Tinubu,” he said.

Dispute over APC leadership

Mr Nwachuku also rejected Mr Okorocha’s claim to control the APC structure in Imo State, arguing that the party’s rules recognise sitting governors as leaders of the party in their respective states.

He said President Bola Tinubu remained the national leader of the APC, while Mr Uzodimma controlled the party’s structure in Imo State.

“By the APC rules, the governors are the leaders of the party in their states while the president is the leader in the country. I’m not aware that rule has changed,” he said.

He accused Mr Okorocha of attempting to personalise a party structure that belonged collectively to its members, adding that the former governor was unwilling to submit to the party’s leadership.

Mr Nwachuku also criticised Mr Okorocha’s eight-year administration in Imo State, describing it as a family system of government and blaming his performance in office for his alleged loss of political relevance.

He dismissed the former governor’s public celebration of the court judgement, arguing that the ruling would not survive an appeal.

“No responsible leader anywhere in the world will appear on television the way Okorocha did to celebrate a judgement he knows will be thrown out at the appeal for lacking in facts and for being against the rules of the party,” he said.

He also dismissed Mr Okorocha’s claims of continued popularity among voters in Imo West and the state.

Mr Nwachuku concluded his response with the expression caveat emptor, meaning buyer beware, urging the public to scrutinise the former governor’s claims.

Background to the court dispute

The Federal High Court in Abuja, presided over by Justice Obiora Egwuatu, had ruled in favour of Mr Okorocha in the dispute over the APC’s Imo West senatorial primary.

The court declared him the validly nominated candidate of the party and directed INEC to recognise him for the 2027 senatorial election.

The judgement followed a suit filed by Mr Okorocha challenging INEC’s recognition of Mr Uzodimma as the winner of the party’s 18 May primary.

During his interview, Mr Okorocha said he obtained certified copies of documents relating to the primary from INEC on 26 July 2026, while documents supporting Mr Uzodimma’s emergence were presented to the commission on 22 August.

He alleged that the later documents contained inconsistencies, including a discrepancy in the date of the election and the description of Mr Uzodimma’s emergence as a consensus candidate despite the existence of competing aspirants.

He further claimed that result sheets covering more than 300 polling units across 144 wards and 12 local government areas were completed by one person.

Mr Okorocha also questioned the circumstances surrounding a letter allegedly submitted to the APC national chairman by the Imo resident electoral commissioner, arguing that the document supporting his own claim was certified by INEC, while the one supporting Mr Uzodimma was certified by the APC.

He alleged that these discrepancies were part of the evidence that persuaded the court to recognise him as the winner.

However, Mr Okorocha’s allegations of document irregularities and forgery remain disputed by the governor’s camp. Mr Nwachuku insisted that the primary was properly conducted under the supervision of INEC officials and the APC’s national election committee.

The APC had also indicated that it would study the judgement and pursue available legal remedies.

The dispute is the latest chapter in the political rivalry between the two men. Mr Okorocha governed Imo State from 2011 to 2019 and subsequently represented Imo West in the Senate from 2019 to 2023.

World.title: South-East governors urge Ndigbo to shun deception and vote for Tinubu in 2027
World.content:
Governors Peter Mbah of Enugu State, Charles Soludo of Anambra State, Francis Nwifuru of Ebonyi State, and Hope Uzodimma of Imo State have called on the people of South-East region to vote massively for President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election and ignore every form of deceipt and political distractions.

The governors made the call during the All Progressives Congress (APC) Women Mega Rally and Empowerment Programme for the South-East flagged off by the First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu at Okpara Square, Enugu, on Saturday.

Speaking, the host governor, Dr. Peter Mbah, urged the people of the region to support Tinubu’s re-election bid to enable him to consolidate the gains of his administration’s economic reforms.

He attributed ongoing development projects, including the construction of primary healthcare centres, to the federal government’s economic reforms.

“If I ask what future you want for your children, I’m sure you are seeing that future unfold gradually through the bold and courageous reforms of Mr President.

“It is through those reforms that enough money has been made available to all the states. Which is why in Enugu, when you look around you, you will see the Smart Green Schools, Type 2 Primary Healthcare Centres, and numerous other projects and initiatives we have undertaken in just three years.

This is happening because of the bold and courageous reforms of Mr President and we know the job is not finished yet. A good sailor does not abandon his ship mid-sea because of challenges.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“So, we must finish the journey we all started together. We must come out on January 16 with our PVC and ensure that the good work Mr. President is doing will continue.

“Don’t listen to any voice. Those voices telling us a different thing. We, the Igbos have gone to communities outside our zone to build businesses. And we also know how to build relationships. And that is being put to test. We are not a people that are ethnic bigots. We are a people that are strategic.

“And that is why we must all come out in our numbers and support Mr President to continue the good work. Support all our APC candidates to ensure that they are returned come January and February,” he emphasised.

Speaking on the empowerment programme targeting 5,000 women across the South-east, Mbah said the initiative followed the empowerment of more than 2,000 women, including payment of hospital bills, in Enugu by the First Lady, within 48 hours.

“When you empower a woman, you strengthen the family. When you empower a woman, you build a strong community,” he said.

Also speaking, Governor Uzodimma reiterated the commitment of the region to supporting Tinubu’s re-election in 2027.

He explained that Igbos had experienced marginalisation for over 60 years, but were beginning to witness a new era of political inclusion and development under Tinubu.

He commended the president for expanding the scope of infrastructure and economic development in the South-East.

“We are now seeing good roads, electricity, health reforms as well as educational reforms in the country. A winning team must not be changed,” he said.

The governor urged the electorate to sustain the current development trajectory, saying the federal government’s economic reforms had increased resources available to states for development.

“We have more money to build Okigwe to Owerri, Umuahia to Owerri, Orlu to Owerri and Owerri to Port Harcourt roads,” he said.

Like Mbah, Uzodimma added that the improved financial position of the state had enabled his administration to pay salaries and pensions consistently, including 13th-month salaries for workers.

In his remarks, Governor Nwifuru said that the number one mission for Ndigbo in 2027 elections was to re-elect President Tinubu, describing the APC as the only political party with a clear and identifiable manifesto capable of sustaining the country’s development and truly advancing the course of Ndigbo.

He dismissed suggestions of his involvement in any political coalition, stressing that his loyalty remained with the APC, urging urged supporters to vote for APC candidates at all levels in the 2027 elections.

Similarly, Soludo, represented by his Deputy, Dr Gilbert Ibezim, said the South-East had a responsibility to support Tinubu’s re-election in appreciation of his administration’s achievements, adding that the region stood to benefit more from continued collaboration with the federal government.

Also speaking, the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Hon. Benjamin Kalu, urged Igbos to embrace political inclusion by supporting Tinubu’s re-election.

Kalu said the Igbo had not produced a president of Nigeria in the past 60 years, and was therefore not party to any one-term arrangement for the Presidency of Igbo extraction by anybody.

He, however, stressed that the Igbo needed to to strengthen its political alliances across the nation to actualise a full two-term Igbo presidency in the near future.

He recalled that Tinubu, while serving as governor of Lagos State, maintained cordial relationships with Igbos and included them in his cabinet.

He commended the Tinubu administration for establishing the South East Development Commission (SEDC).

He described it as a major step towards addressing the region’s developmental challenges.

Meanwhile, addressing the rally, the First Lady conveyed President Tinubu’s goodwill message and urged Nigerians not to be discouraged by the economic challenges associated with the President’s reforms, insisting that the country was moving towards prosperity.

She likened the process to childbirth, noting that although the period of labour could be painful, it ultimately led to delivery.

“Mr. President said I should greet everyone. We have done reforms and we are now in prosperity. Don’t allow anyone to deceive you. The worst is over. We are stepping into prosperity,” she said.

The First Lady described the empowerment initiative as an indication of the APC government’s commitment to translating its promises into practical interventions, noting that the party was combining political mobilisation with economic support.

The First Lady urged the women to mobilise support for President Tinubu and APC candidates in the forthcoming 2027 general elections, asking them to hold political aspirants accountable for their records of empowerment and development interventions.

Other dignitaries at the massive rally were Wife of the Vice President, Mrs Nana Shettima; wife of the Senate President, Mrs. Uloma Akpabio; wives of the South East governors; Minister of Industry, Trade and Investment, Dr Doris Uzoka-Anite; Minister of Innovation, Science and Technology, Dr. Kingsley Udeh (SAN); and Minister of Women Affairs and Social Development, Mrs Imaan Sulaiman-Ibrahim.

Also present were the APC Deputy National Chairman (South), Dr Ben Nwoye; National Women Leader of the APC and Director-General of the Women Wing of the Presidential Campaign Council, Dr Mary Alile-Idele; South-East Zonal Woman Leader of the APC, Dr Oby Ajih; members of the National and State Assemblies, local government chairmen and other party stakeholders.

The rally by the Remi Tinubu-led Women Mobilisation Directorate of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, which kicked off in the South East, will also be held across the remaining five geopolitical zones of the country.

World.title: In Zamfara, 9 a.m is 9 a.m: How Lawal is killing ‘African time’ mentality, By Yusuf Ladan
World.content:
Nigerians are widely known for what is popularly described as “African time” a culture of lateness where an event scheduled for 9:00 a.m may not begin until 10:00 a.m or even 11:00 a.m.

Over time, this habit has become normalised in our society, with people often arriving late to appointments, meetings and official functions without considering the inconvenience it causes others.

However, my working experience as part of the press team of Zamfara State Governor, Dauda Lawal, has significantly changed my perception of time management and challenged my long-held African Time stereotype.

On my first day in Gusau, I approached government functions with the usual mindset, assuming that even when an event was scheduled for a particular time, there would always be some extra minutes before it commenced.

Like many Nigerians, I would sometimes add a few minutes to the scheduled time before setting out for an event, believing that punctuality was not necessarily a strict requirement.

But that assumption was quickly challenged.

On my first day attending an official function involving the governor, I arrived only to discover that I had been locked out just a few minutes before the scheduled commencement time.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

It was then that I was told something that has remained with me: “Governor Dauda Lawal’s 9:00 a.m. means 9:00 a.m., and his 2:00 p.m. means 2:00 p.m.” That experience became a turning point for me.

Gradually, I adjusted to the governor’s schedule and developed the habit of arriving at least 30 minutes before his expected arrival.

For over a month of observing his official engagements, I have yet to witness Governor Dauda Lawal arrive late for a scheduled function.

In fact, there was an occasion when the governor arrived ahead of schedule while some participants were yet to arrive.

This consistency has gradually influenced the conduct of government appointees, political office holders, civil servants and other participants attending official functions.

People now understand that keeping to time is not negotiable because the governor does not compromise on punctuality.

Beyond the personal discipline it demands, this culture sends a strong message about leadership, respect for other people’s time and the importance of institutional efficiency.

When a leader takes time seriously, those working with him are compelled to do the same. It also helps to change the mindset that lateness is an acceptable part of our social and official engagements.

My experience in Zamfara under Governor Dauda Lawal has taught me that punctuality is not just about arriving early; it is about discipline, responsibility and respect for others.

Perhaps, one of the less-discussed changes taking place in Zamfara under Governor Dauda Lawal is this growing culture of punctuality.

In Zamfara, at least from what I have personally observed, African Time is gradually losing its place. Governor Dauda Lawal has made it clear that when time is fixed, it must be respected.

And that is a leadership lesson worth taking beyond the walls of Government House.

* Yusuf Ladan is a Gusau, Zamfara State-based journalist

World.title: 2027: Christian, Muslim youth groups sign peace accord ahead of elections
World.content:
Christian and Muslim youth organisations in Lagos have signed an interreligious peace accord, committing to reject political violence, religious intolerance and the use of young people as political thugs ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The accord was signed on Saturday at the South-West Zonal Interreligious Peace Accord Summit organised by the Youth Wing of the Christian Association of Nigeria (YOWICAN), in collaboration with the National Council of Muslim Youth Organisations (NACOMYO).

The summit was held at the Senator Oluremi Tinubu CAN Secretariat, Alausa, Ikeja, Lagos, with the theme, “Building Bridges of Faith and Politics: Strengthening Peace, Unity, and National Development Through Christian-Muslim Collaboration.”

The groups said the 2027 elections would test Nigeria’s unity and urged young people not to allow politicians to recruit or manipulate them into violence.

In the communique issued at the end of the summit, the groups said the signing of the accord represents their collective determination to reject political violence, religious manipulation, hate speech and other divisive actions “capable of threatening the peace and stability of the country.”

They also called on Christian and Muslim youths to promote tolerance and peaceful coexistence in their communities, institutions and places of worship.

Peaceful coexistence

Speaking at the summit, the Chairman of CAN in Lagos State, Stephen Adegbite, said the peace accord aims to foster religious tolerance, reject political violence, and promote peaceful coexistence ahead of the elections.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Adegbite criticised politicians who make derogatory statements against their opponents.

“What we must do is what youths have done today; both Christians and Muslims have done well to bring peace and restore confidence in our great nation,” he said.

He urged young people to lead by example, saying the summit was intended to demonstrate that Christians and Muslims want peace before, during and after the elections.

“We don’t want anybody to be killed for any elective position,” he said.

Mr Adegbite also cited the Bible and the Quran as texts that promote peaceful coexistence.

Peace message to grassroots

The National Secretary of NACOMYO, Shehu Ibrahim, said the accord is particularly important as the country approaches the 2027 elections.

Mr Ibrahim said the organisation would take the message of peace to communities across the country, including through Imams, Friday prayers, Islamic schools and other religious gatherings.

He said the groups would mobilise young people at the grassroots to discourage violence during the elections.

Also speaking, the Lagos State APC Youth Leader, Damilare Orimoloye, said young people must understand that disagreements do not have to result in violence.

“Peace speaks against violence, how to tolerate each other, showing love amidst misunderstanding,” Mr Orimoloye said.

He added that disagreements were likely during the election period, making tolerance and peaceful communication important.

The South-West Chairman of YOWICAN, Nnamdi Obasi, said the summit was significant because Christian and Muslim youths needed to bridge existing gaps and avoid being used against one another.

He urged young Nigerians to remain united and resist attempts by politicians to exploit religious differences to create conflict as the 2027 elections approach.

What the accord says

The communique, signed by YOWICAN’s National Chairman, Orowolo Daniel, and National Secretary, Nehemiah Michael, alongside NACOMYO’s National Secretary II, Shehu Ibrahim, and its representative for the Southern Secretary, Mudashir Bello, outlined seven commitments.

Among them is a rejection of the recruitment and manipulation of young people as political thugs, as well as a commitment to religious tolerance and peaceful coexistence.

The groups also called on religious, traditional, community and political leaders to discourage intolerance, political manipulation and incitement to violence.

They said the peace message should extend beyond the summit to states, local government areas, communities, schools and religious institutions.

The groups further resolved that the peace accord should not end with its signing but should serve as a framework for continued dialogue, mutual accountability and peacebuilding between Christian and Muslim youths.

They urged Nigerian youths, political leaders, religious institutions and other stakeholders to work towards a peaceful and inclusive 2027 election.

World.title: Article of Faith: Ways of the Kingdom of God (1), By Femi Aribisala
World.content:
God specialises in the everlasting.

Jeremiah had a bone to pick with God. He asked:

“Why does the way of the wicked prosper? Why are those happy who deal so treacherously?” (Jeremiah 12:1).

God offered him no satisfactory answer. Instead, He assured him that more things would confound him. God replied Jeremiah’s question with a question:

“If you have raced with men on foot and they have worn you out, how can you compete with horses?” (Jeremiah 12:5).

The wicked prosper because the prosperity of men is not the prosperity of God. God can give what men give, and He sometimes does. But men cannot give what God gives. The prosperity that comes from men is temporal. But God’s prosperity is eternal.

It is like the current fad of regular exercise from going to the gym. Paul says instead:

Exercise yourself toward godliness. For bodily exercise profits a little, but godliness is profitable for all things, having promise of the life that now is and of that which is to come. (1 Timothy 4:7-8).

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Men give what only has value in this world. But God gives what has value in this world and in the world to come.

Different Blessings

Jesus says:

The thief does not come except to steal, and to kill, and to destroy. I have come that they may have life, and that they may have it more abundantly. (John 10:10).

Everything man values can be stolen, killed, or destroyed. But nothing like that can happen to things of God. Solomon says:

“I know that whatever God does, it shall be forever. Nothing can be added to it, and nothing taken from it.” (Ecclesiastes 3:14).

The blessings of God are everlasting, while those of men are time-bound. That means the blessings of men can be lost, and what can be lost can bring sorrow. But,

The blessing of the Lord makes one rich, and He adds no sorrow with it. (Proverbs 10:22).

The riches of this world must be relinquished.

For we brought nothing into this world, and it is certain we can carry nothing out. (1 Timothy 6:7).

That means the riches of this world are fake. They are illusory.

For riches certainly make themselves wings; they fly away like an eagle toward heaven. (Proverbs 23:5).

True riches must be eternal. They only come from God.

Habakkuk’s Dilemma

Habakkuk faces a dilemma similar to Jeremiah’s. He asks God: “Why are things so bad and You do nothing?” “How can things be this bad when You are so good?”

God does not explain. Instead, He tells Habakkuk, “Just Wait. I am going to make things so much worse.”

Kingdom dynamics refer to God’s seemingly peculiar ways. Occasionally, we can understand why God does things the way He does. But He does not owe us an explanation. The important thing is to know the ways He does things and come to terms with them.

With God, expect the unexpected. Expect the extraordinary. The commonplace is of men. God can do and sometimes does the ordinary. But He only does this to humour men. His speciality is the extraordinary. God can do what man does. But man cannot do the amazing things God does.

Moreover, if we deserve what we get, then it is unlikely to be from God. God gives what we do not deserve. He says:

I will show mercy to anyone I choose, and I will show compassion to anyone I choose. (Exodus 33:19).

Solomon throws more light on this peculiarity:

“The race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, nor bread to the wise, nor riches to men of understanding, nor favour to men of skill; but time and chance happen to them all.” (Ecclesiastes 9:11).

Therefore, with God, be ready to receive what you don’t deserve.

If you can easily understand what is happening and why, then it is likely to be of men. But if you cannot easily understand it, then it is more likely to be of God. So, don’t be surprised if what happens to you surpasses your understanding.

Believe all things. (1 Cor 13:7). That means assume the best in all circumstances, whether good or bad. God works all things together for good for His children. (Romans 8:28). Therefore, in everything, give thanks. (1 Thessalonians 5:18).

Relinquish the Past

Kingdom dynamics validate God. They make us aware that the invisible God is at work. Jesus’ kingdom is not of this world. (John 18:36). Therefore, His actions will be peculiar. They will be extraordinary. If they were normal, they could easily have been man-made. But because they are peculiar, they obviously do not originate from this world.

Do not be held captive by what happened in the past. The past is never a blueprint for the present. God says:

Behold, I will do a new thing, now it shall spring forth; shall you not know it? I will even make a road in the wilderness and rivers in the desert. (Isaiah 43:19).

Don’t complain like the church in the wilderness if there is no water. God can bring water out of the desert. He even brought water out of a rock. Job testifies to this wonderful work of God. He recalled a time:

When (his) steps through rich pasturage were washed with butter, and the rock poured out for (him) streams of oil! (Job 29:6).

God is a God of originality. No two things of God are the same. No two fingerprints are the same. No two irises are duplicates.

Jesus is the same yesterday, today, and forever. But He is the same in that He always does new things, and not that He only does the same things.

Therefore, Paul says:

Brethren, I count not myself to have apprehended: but this one thing I do, forgetting those things which are behind, and reaching forth unto those things which are before, I press toward the mark for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus. (Philippians 3:13-14).

Disregard the Flesh

Paul also counsels:

From now on, regard no one according to the flesh. (2 Corinthians 5:16).

That is the reason why many people missed Christ. He came in the flesh but was 100 per cent divine.

According to the flesh, Jesus was common. He was born in a manger of very poor parentage. His parents could not afford a lamb as a sacrifice for the male child who opens the womb. They had to make do with the poor man’s substitute of a pair of turtledoves. (Luke 2:22-24). (Leviticus 12:8).

Jesus came from Nazareth, a city not even on the map. When Philip introduced Him to Nathanael, he asked disparagingly:

“Can anything good come out of Nazareth?” (John 1:44).

Jesus did not go to school. He did not graduate from a Theological Seminary. This confounded the Jewish religious elite. They marvelled, asking:

“How does this Man know letters, having never studied?” (John 7:15).

But educational qualifications and credentials are only relevant in the world. They are irrelevant in the kingdom of God. God qualifies the unqualified and disqualified.

Paul says:

“For you see your calling, brethren, that not many wise according to the flesh, not many mighty, not many noble, are called. But God has chosen the foolish things of the world to put to shame the wise, and God has chosen the weak things of the world to put to shame the things which are mighty; and the base things of the world and the things which are despised God has chosen, and the things which are not, to bring to nothing the things that are, that no flesh should glory in His presence. (1 Corinthians 1:26-29).

When Amos was challenged because of his pedigree, he said to Amaziah:

“I was no prophet, nor was I a son of a prophet, but I was a sheepbreeder and a tender of sycamore fruit. Then the Lord took me as I followed the flock, and the Lord said to me, ‘Go, prophesy to My people Israel. Now therefore, hear the word of the Lord: You say, ‘Do not prophesy against Israel, and do not spout against the house of Isaac.’ Therefore thus says the Lord: ‘Your wife shall be a harlot in the city; your sons and daughters shall fall by the sword; your land shall be divided by survey line; you shall die in a defiled land.” Amos 7:14-17).

The Blind Eye

Don’t believe what you see, feel, or touch. That was the first contradiction I confronted in my relationship with God. He told me nothing would happen to me, and then I was shot. A bullet was lodged in my leg, but He insisted there was nothing wrong with my leg.

The naked eye cannot see what God is doing. Therefore:

Do not look at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen. For the things which are seen are temporary, but the things which are not seen are eternal. (2 Corinthians 4:18).

To see, we have to be blind. Jesus puts this cryptically. He says:

“For judgment I have come into this world, so that the blind will see and those who see will become blind.” (John 9:39).

When God sent Samuel to anoint a son of Jesse as king of Israel, He warned him:

“Do not look at his appearance or at his physical stature, because I have refused him. For the Lord does not see as man sees; for man looks at the outward appearance, but the Lord looks at the heart.” (1 Samuel 16:7).

Children of God must learn to appreciate the beauty of holiness. (2 Chronicles 20:21). CONTINUED.
