World.title: 2027: Don’t disrupt opposition campaigns — Otti warns supporters
World.content:
Gov Otti

By Steve Oko & Ugochukwu Alaribe

UMUAHIA – Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, has cautioned supporters of the Labour Party against taking the law into their hands or interfering with the campaign activities of rival political parties ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The governor warned that no political affiliation would shield anyone from arrest for disrupting the lawful activities of opposition parties, stressing that political competition must be conducted within the ambit of the law.

Otti spoke on Sunday in Umuahia while formally flagging off the Labour Party’s 2027 campaign in the state, where he declared that his administration would not tolerate political intolerance or the denial of opponents’ democratic rights.

He said opposition parties were free to use public facilities, including stadiums, provided they complied with established procedures, obtained necessary approvals and paid the stipulated fees.

Reiterating his position, the governor said security agencies had been instructed to ensure that no political group was prevented from holding legitimate rallies or other campaign activities.

“I have since given a public directive, and I am repeating it here, that opposition parties should not be restricted from the use of public facilities, including the stadium, once they apply and obtain the necessary approvals,” Otti said.

In a strong message to party loyalists, he warned against assuming that membership of the ruling party conferred immunity for acts capable of undermining the democratic process.

“You do not have my mandate to attack people or to stop people from campaigning.

“Security agencies have been mandated to arrest and deal decisively with anyone who attempts to obstruct any political group from holding their legitimate activities, even if they are Labour Party members. I hope I am heard clearly,” he said.

Beyond the conduct of campaigns, Otti challenged opposition parties to raise the quality of political debate by offering alternative policy directions rather than relying on personal attacks or recycling issues he said had been addressed by his administration.

According to him, the political conversation in Abia should now be centred on development priorities and the next phase of governance rather than basic issues such as salaries, pensions, roads and environmental sanitation.

“Do not forget that in Abia we have gone past the era of campaigning on the payment of salaries and pensions, construction of roads or urban sanitation.

“The hygiene issues have been dealt with. If you are unable to raise your campaign pitch to the development realities of our state, you will definitely struggle to convince any informed voter,” the governor said.

He urged political opponents to interrogate available performance data before making claims about the state, pointing to Abia’s ratings in the Citizen Satisfaction Index, State Performance Index and Fiscal Performance Ranking by governance-monitoring organisations.

“You should go and do your research first before coming out to open your mouth, because there are data everywhere to show what has been achieved. Evidently, the world knows that Abia is on the right track,” Otti said.

The governor also argued that the experiences of Abians within and outside the country had lent credibility to external assessments of the state’s development trajectory, adding that multilateral institutions had opened development assistance opportunities for Abia.

“It would therefore be unthinkable that anyone will ever be allowed to return us to the old era of irresponsibility and misery,” he declared.

Otti, who expressed appreciation to residents for their turnout at the campaign flag-off, called on party supporters to intensify grassroots mobilisation and take the message of the party to communities across the state.

“This is your project, and as you return to the communities, knock on every door and remind our people that we still have a job to complete. Invite them to join the campaign so that together we can conclude the journey that began 12 years ago in faith and optimism,” he added.

Highlight of the event was the presentation of the party flag to national and state house of assembly candidates of Labour Party for the 2027 polls.

The event was massively attended by party members including the candidates for the various elections and their supporters who were competing for recognition as they chanted solidarity songs for their various candidates.

World.title: Mbappe scores as Real Madrid beat Racing Santander 3-0
World.content:
Real Madrid’s French forward #10 Kylian Mbappe is challenged by Racing Santander’s French defender #24 Jeanuel Belocian during the Spanish league football match between Racing de Santander and Real Madrid CF at El Sardinero Stadium in Santander on November 1, 2026. (Photo by ANDER GILLENEA / AFP)

Kylian Mbappe moved on from a tumultuous week by scoring a penalty to help Real Madrid win 3-0 at Racing Santander on Sunday.

The French forward narrowly lost out on the Ballon d’Or to Bayern Munich’s Harry Kane on Monday and then had to apologise after a social media storm following a video in which he joked about former Chinese leader Mao Zedong.

Real Madrid’s match, along with other Spanish fixtures this weekend, was not broadcast by Chinese state television because of the fallout.

Jude Bellingham and Yan Diomande were also on target to keep third-place Madrid within three points of leaders Barcelona, who thrashed Alaves 6-1 on Saturday.

Jose Mourinho’s side have won six straight games across all competitions and are a point behind city rivals Atletico Madrid, who beat Levante 2-0.

Mbappe won a soft penalty as he went down under little pressure from Matteo Prati, smashing it home to put Madrid ahead at the Sardinero stadium in the 11th minute.

Madrid had control of the game and a fine pass from Arda Guler sent Bellingham through on goal for the second.

The England international knocked the ball past the goalkeeper and rolled home for his 50th goal since joining Madrid in 2023.

Guler spurned a good opportunity for the third after being set up by Mbappe, before Madrid’s record signing Diomande lashed home from the edge of the box.

The hosts started the second half well, pushing Madrid back, much to the chagrin of Mourinho, who yelled at his players.

Madrid regained their control and racked up several more chances, with Mbappe hitting the post and Bellingham denied by Racing goalkeeper Julen Agirrezabala.

Racing won a penalty after Madrid’s Aurelien Tchouameni handled in the box, but the award was cancelled after a VAR review.

Bellingham had a second goal ruled out in stoppage time after he strayed offside before finding the net and Endrick bent an effort narrowly wide from distance.

Hosts Racing, 16th, back in La Liga for the first time in 14 seasons, fell to their first home defeat of the campaign.

Earlier Sevilla, sixth, suffered a 3-1 loss at Getafe, who moved into mid-table.

Later Sunday Athletic Bilbao host Real Sociedad in a Basque derby and Valencia visit Elche.

Vanguard News

World.title: 2027: I’m Lion of South-East, I’m strongly behind Tinubu – Umahi
World.content:
File: President Tinubu (right) and Minister of Works, David Umahi

….as traditional rulers, religious leaders, APC stakeholders endorse Tinubu, Nwifuru, others

By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki

The Minister of Works Senator David Umahi has said that as a Lion of South East, he’s strongly behind President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for reelection in 2027 due to his indileable achievements in South East zone and across the country.

Umahi while speaking at the All Progressives Congress (APC) Town Hall meeting at Ecumenical Centre Abakaliki, Ebonyi State said that Tinubu is a blessing to South East zone and shoukd be supported for second term.

The town hall meeting was organized the office of the Senior Special Assistant to the President Southeast on Community Engagement Barr. Chioma Nweze to mobilize support for the President Tinubu, governor and other APC candidates in forthcoming election.

The former Senator representing Ebonyi Central Sen. Julius Ali Ucha moved a motion adopting APC, President Tinubu for reelection, governor Francis Nwifuru and all APC candidates in 2027 general elections.

The motion was seconded by Senator who represented Ebonyi North Sen. Anthony Agbo while Senator Umahi put the motion in voice votes and was generally endorsed.

Those who spoke at the meeting, include, Traditional rulers Ezeogo Charles Nkpume, and Ezeogo Sunday Oketa, Bishop Onyeuwa Omar and CAN Chairman Stan Nwokolo, Pastor Eunice Oyeyemi of Divine Mandate Pastors and Former Deputy of Ebonyi State Prof. Chigozie Ogbu.

Addressing the party faithful, Umahi charged the traditional rulers and religious leaders to throw full support to President Tinubu and should not sit on the fence over regional sentiments.

The Minister urged the leaders of various clans, villages, communities and local government areas to talk to their brothers contesting against the zoning arrangement already in place in the state and should the reelection of Governor Francis Nwifuru.

“I want to tell our religious leaders and Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN), do not stay on the fence. I know when I was struggling to be Governor, CAN took a descion and said justice must prevail. CAN don’t keep quiet, let us toe the path that must sustain our freedom.

“There is no way an Igbo man after staying for 60 years, will want to be President for four years. There is nobody that can accept that. The North has not accepted to be President for four years

“Somebody was telling me that Atiku”s son bought buses and donated to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and said this is personal donation.

“Igbo man needs wisdom, not sentiments. Igbo man should not allow people to be dishing hate speeches in the social media on their behalf. Today, our people in Commerce, we clear our goods with ease. Today our roads are being revived in the path of economic activities.

“Today, we can boldly say we have been integrated. The last time there were choosing service chiefs, it was Naval Chief. This time, it is Chief of Air Staff , Minister of Works, otter Ministers, SSAs, what else? When I say South East have been fully integrated and included, I mean it.

“My mouth will not shut up because I am telling our people for a reference for tomorrow. We are supporting President Bola Ahmed Tinubu to finish his remaining four years so that the South East would have strategically supported another region. So that when it is our turn, we will not get this thing by hate speeches, they will not give to us by sentiments It is strategic leaders of South East say this, you will now insult them.

“You insult anybody that is not supporting Peter Obi. Anybody that is not supporting Peter Obi, is a saboteur, you insult the person. Who is Peter Obi better than, who is he better than? Is he better than Sam Egwu? Is he better than Elias Mbam,? Is he better than the lion of South East myself? Is he better than Anyim Pius? Whom is he better than?

“So, I don’t want us to be deceiving ourselves. Traditional fathers, do not stay on the fence, religious leaders, do not stay on the fence. Our people in the North do not, our people in the South West, they do not. We should support President Tinubu for his love for South East and infrastructural development in the zone” he stated.

World.title: Tinubu Has Not Deviated An Inch from His Electricity Pledge, Says Alake
World.content:
Adedayo Akinwale in Abuja

The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council (APC-PCC) has said that President Bola Tinubu has not deviated from the 2023 campaign pledge to fix electricity.

It added that the administration’s quest to fix the electricity market and power sector is ongoing work.

It spokesperson, Dele Aleke, in a statement issued Sunday said as President Tinubu seeks Nigerians’ mandate for a second term in office, he would proudly present his scorecard in the power sector and clearly tell Nigerians what remains to be done,

Alake recalled that at a meeting with members of the Organised Private Sector (OPS) in Lagos ahead of the 2023 elections, then candidate Tinubu promised to tackle systemic problems in the power sector and end estimated billing.

His exact words, according to Alake: “Whichever way, by all means necessary, you will have electricity, and you will not pay for estimated bills anymore. A promise made will be a promise kept. If I don’t keep the promise and I come for a second term, don’t vote for me, unless I give you adequate reasons why I couldn’t deliver.

“A fair assessment of the pledge should consider the full statement alongside the administration’s record since 2023.”

The spokesperson listed measures taken by the administration to fix the sector including the signing of the Electricity Act, 2023 on June 9, within two weeks in office, liberalising the sector and allowing states to participate in generation, distribution and transmission. Lagos, Enugu, Abia, Ekiti, Oyo, Kaduna and Niger have set up their own regulatory agencies.

He recalled taking on over N6 trillion legacy debt accumulated from 2015 to 2025 and creating a N4 trillion bond programme to settle verified debts to 21 Gencos and Discos.

Alake noted that the first and second tranches have raised over N1.2 trillion.

He added: “Launching the Presidential Metering Initiative to close the over 7 million metering gap, with over 1.5 million customers metered in the last three years.

“Aligning tariffs to cost to restore market liquidity, creating Service Bands with different tariffs, while protecting low-income households.”

Alake also mentioned the Rural Electrification Agency connecting universities, hospitals and rural communities to solar power, plans to modernise the Osogbo Grid Control Centre built over 60 years ago and build an East-West super grid.

He stressed that part of government’s effort included reviewing the Presidential Power Initiative (PPI) started by former President Muhammadu Buhari; signing an Acceleration Agreement in December 2023 with German partners, with FEC approving first batch of 5 TCN substations in December 2024 and second batch of eight new substations and upgrade of four existing ones in June 2026.

Alake noted: “Fixing the electricity market and power sector is ongoing work. President Tinubu has not deviated an inch from his commitment.

“As he seeks Nigerians’ mandate for a second term in office, he will proudly present his scorecard in the power sector and clearly tell Nigerians what remains to be done.”

World.title: Delimi RISE Project Launched In Kaduna To Mobilise Youths for Peacebuilding
World.content:
John Shiklam in Kaduna

The Delimi RISE Project has been launched in Kaduna State to strengthen youth participation and leadership in peacebuilding ahead of the 2027 general election.

The initiative is supported by a civil society organisation, Strengthening Peace and Resilience in Nigeria (SPRiNG) programme, funded by the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO), and implemented by Strategy, Research and Development (SRD), a pan African peacebuilding organisation established in 2022.

Executive Director of SRD, Richard Ali, said in a statement that the project would target 80 young people between the ages of 18 to 35 in Igabi, Jema’a and Kaura Local Government Areas of the state.

Ali said the initiative would begin with a “Massive Open Online Course (MOOC) style workshop, followed by peace public squares in the three local government areas and a Community of Practice to implement peacebuilding activities”.

According to him, the project would promote inclusion across ethnic, religious, gender and disability lines.

“As a peacebuilding organization, we advocated for co-existence, spaces that create equal opportunities without bias,” the statement added.

The training will cover women, youth, peace and security, peacebuilding and conflict prevention, youth leadership and participation, inclusive governance, gender equality, disability and social inclusion, as well as safeguarding and conflict sensitive approaches.

He added that the project would create opportunities for young people to participate actively in peacebuilding and community engagement.

“The project would provide young people with opportunities to contribute meaningfully to peacebuilding, promote constructive community engagement, and strengthen local resilience ahead of the 2027 elections,” Ali said.

World.title: Oba of Benin Marks Decade on Throne with 10 Historic Golf Shots
World.content:
Felix Omoh-Asun in Benin City

History was made weekend when the Oba of Benin, Omo N’ Oba N’ Edo, Uku Akpolokpolo, Oba Ewuare II, performed a symbolic ceremonial tee-off at the Benin Club Golf Section in Benin City, Edo State.

​In a rare public appearance rich with royal heritage and symbolism, His Majesty— marking 10 years on the throne of Benin—struck 10 ceremonial golf balls as part of activities commemorating his decade on the throne.

The Oba was joined on the green by his children, including his daughter, Princess Amenaghawon, alongside his three sons—Prince Ikponmwosa, Prince Igbinosa, and Prince Idugbowa — that also took turns hitting ceremonial balls.

​The brief yet colourful ceremony drew an audience, including top Benin palace chiefs, members of the local organising committee of the tournament, captains of industry, tournament sponsors, and professional and amateur golfers from across Nigeria and beyond.

​Speaking at the event, the chief organiser of the tournament, Prince Aghatise Erediauwa, described the competition as a fitting tribute to a decade of peace, cultural renaissance and purposeful leadership under Oba Ewuare.

​Prince Aghatise highlighted that the 2026 event marks the 9th edition of the coronation anniversary series, making a grand return after its last outing in 2022.

He praised the impressive turnout of both professional and amateur players, as well as the overwhelming enthusiasm from participants.

​He said: “You can see the joy on everybody’s face today. Normally, there is a ceremonial tee-off. This has been a fantastic golf tournament where people came from all over the world—both professional and amateur players.

​”It has been going so well. We are excited that His Royal Majesty dedicated his time to be with us at the tournament. We are extremely delighted, and we thank him so much for that.”

​In an interview with journalists, the Director-General of the National Institute for Sports and former Edo Deputy Governor, Philip Shaibu, eulogised Oba Ewuare for the historic milestone, noting that the calibre of personalities present reflected the significance of the occasion.

​Shaibu commended the royal father for promoting peace and unity across Edo State, praying for prosperous years ahead on the throne of his forebears.

​”As you can see, everybody is around for this tournament. It shows the respect that we have for the Oba. May his reign continue to bring progress to all of us,” he said.

With the ceremonial tee-off concluded, the historic tournament wrapped up on a high note, leaving participants and dignitaries celebrating a decade of cultural pride, peace and progress under Oba Ewuare II, while eagerly anticipating an even grander next edition

World.title: Adesina, Sanusi, Otti, Others to Lead African Prosperity Talks in Abuja
World.content:
Michael Olugbode in Abuja

Former President of the African Development Bank (AfDB), Dr Akinwumi Adesina; Emir of Kano, Muhammadu Sanusi II; and Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, are among prominent African leaders expected in Abuja on November 3 to explore practical strategies for building a prosperous, resilient and inclusive African economy.

The second edition of the Oxford Global Think Tank (OGTT) Leadership Conference will bring together influential figures from government, business, technology, finance and civil society to examine leadership choices, institutional reforms, technological innovations and investment opportunities needed to translate Africa’s enormous potential into sustainable economic prosperity.

Adesina, who is also Executive Chairman of the Global Africa Investment Summit, will deliver the keynote address, while Sanusi and Founder of ANAP Foundation, Atedo Peterside, will co-chair the conference.

The conference, themed ‘Leadership for a Prosperous Future,’ is expected to address critical challenges confronting the continent, including the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI), changing global power dynamics, demographic shifts and evolving economic realities.

Other prominent personalities expected include Minister of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy, Dr Bosun Tijani; Minister of Women Affairs, Imaan Sulaiman-Ibrahim; Executive Vice-President of Afreximbank, Dr Kanayo Awani; Director-General of the Securities and Exchange Commission, Dr Emomotimi Agama; and Chief Executive Officer of Flutterwave, Gbenga Agboola.

A statement by the Conference Media Adviser, Comrade Chris Isiguzo, said discussions would centre on three pillars — resilience, innovation and dynamism — with participants exploring ways to strengthen African institutions, mobilise capital, improve productivity and expand economic opportunities.

A special highlight will be the conference’s focus on AI, featuring the launch of an AI report and an AI Virtual Centre, as well as an exhibition showcasing emerging technologies and their potential to transform Africa’s development.

The organisers said the gathering would move beyond broad aspirations to identify practical actions and partnerships capable of strengthening institutions, deepening productive capacity and promoting inclusive economic growth.

“Africa’s future will be shaped by the quality of leadership and the choices its institutions and leaders make today,” the organisers said.

The conference, hosted by the Oxford Global Think Tank, founded by Ms Arunma Oteh, is slated to hold at the Congress Hall, Transcorp Hilton Hotel, Abuja, from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m., followed by a cocktail reception.

The Oxford Global Think Tank is an independent, non-governmental and non-partisan organisation that promotes research and dialogue on development and supports public and private sector leaders in exploring policy ideas and strengthening institutions.

World.title: Tinubu’s Trans-Sahara Superhighway’ll Transform Northern Economy, Strengthen Security, Says Yilwatda
World.content:
Yemi Kosoko in Jos

National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, has described the ongoing reconstruction of the Akwanga-Jos section of the Trans-Sahara Superhighway as a landmark infrastructure project that will transform economic activities, improve security and deepen national integration across Nigeria.

Yilwatda stated this during an inspection tour of the project, where he expressed satisfaction with the pace of work and commended the commitment of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s administration to delivering critical road infrastructure across the country.

The APC national chairman said the project represented one of the most significant federal investments in the region in decades, noting that the corridor had suffered years of neglect despite its strategic importance to socio-economic development in the North-central and North-east regions.

According to him, the reconstruction forms part of the larger Trans-Sahara Superhighway corridor stretching from Calabar through Ebonyi, Enugu, Benue, Abuja and Jos, before extending to Gombe, Biu and Maiduguri, linking several geopolitical zones and creating a seamless transport network across the country.

He said the highway, which spans more than 1,400 kilometres, would serve as a catalyst for trade, investment and national cohesion by connecting communities, markets and businesses across the South-south, South-east, North-central and North-east regions.

Yilwatda noted that the Akwanga-Jos road, originally constructed around 1972, had not witnessed major rehabilitation for more than five decades, with successive interventions limited largely to palliative repairs and patchwork.

“For over five decades, since the days of the late Joseph Gomwalk around 1972, this corridor witnessed only piecemeal patching. Communities along the Nasarawa-Plateau axis rarely saw federal capital projects running into even N10 billion. Today, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has committed hundreds of billions of naira to build an infrastructure asset designed to endure for over a century,” he said.

He explained that the project was being executed using rigid concrete pavement technology to ensure durability and reduce maintenance requirements, adding that the road was designed to serve future generations.

“We are targeting a lifespan of over 100 years before there will be a need to consider maintaining or repairing it again. That is how you build a lasting legacy,” he stated.

The APC chairman further disclosed that the highway would incorporate modern security architecture, including intelligent surveillance systems, continuous lighting, dedicated police outposts and emergency trauma centres aimed at safeguarding commuters and communities along the route.

According to him, the 24-hour surveillance cameras would assist security agencies in monitoring vehicular movements, tracking criminal activities and ensuring rapid response to emergencies.

“This is not just a road; this is connecting communities. This is connecting customers, connecting markets, connecting people and improving security,” he said.

Yilwatda maintained that the project embodied the ideals of President Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda, adding that visible infrastructure development across the country was evidence that the administration was translating campaign promises into tangible results.

He also described the administration’s infrastructure drive as a major political asset for the ruling APC ahead of the 2027 general election, arguing that Nigerians would ultimately judge the government by projects delivered and impacts felt in their daily lives.

Earlier, the project’s Equipment Coordinator and Public Relations Officer, Mr. James Baba, said construction activities had intensified following the mobilisation of heavy equipment to the Jos axis in line with directives from the Federal Ministry of Works.

Baba disclosed that work was progressing simultaneously from both the Akwanga and Jos ends of the highway, while test-running of the rigid concrete pavement had already commenced.

According to him, about 400 metres of rigid pavement have so far been completed, with contractors targeting 10 kilometres of earthwork before Christmas and an additional 30 kilometres expected to be delivered next year.

“Our target this year is to cover about 10 kilometres of earthwork before Christmas,” he said, expressing confidence that the project would be executed in line with approved specifications and the highest quality standards.

He explained that the adoption of cement concrete pavement in place of conventional asphalt followed the Federal Ministry of Works’ specifications and was intended to guarantee long-term durability of the highway.

World.title: VivaJets Steps Up Francophone Africa Expansion, Grows Fleet to Eight
World.content:
Pan-African business aviation firm, VivaJets, has restated its expansion drive into Francophone Africa as it grows its fleet and strengthens connectivity for businesses, investors and institutions across the continent.

The company was a partner and participant at the fifth UK-West and Central Francophone Africa Trade and Investment Forum (WCAF V) that held in Conakry, Guinea in October.

Themed ‘From Cooperation to Transformation: Building the Future of Development in Africa,’ WCAF V brought together government representatives, institutional stakeholders, businesses and international partners to explore trade, investment and economic opportunities across Francophone West and Central Africa.

The engagement followed VivaJets’ recent participation at the Africa Energy Week (AEW) in Cape Town, where it met stakeholders across the continent’s energy sector.

Chief Executive Officer of VivaJets, Erika Achum, said Francophone Africa presents a key opportunity to deepen regional connectivity.

“Francophone Africa represents an important opportunity to deepen regional connectivity and support the movement of people, ideas and investment across the continent,” Achum said.

“Our participation at WCAF V was about building meaningful relationships with government and institutional stakeholders, as well as international partners who share a commitment to Africa’s economic development. As VivaJets continues to grow, we want to be a trusted aviation partner to the businesses and institutions helping shape the continent’s future,” she added.

VivaJets’ participation at the forum comes amid rapid growth for the company. Just over a year after receiving its Air Operator Certificate (AOC), the firm has expanded its fleet to eight aircraft.

The company has also secured two rounds of credit investment from London-based TLG Capital to support its expansion and advance its mission of improving connectivity through private aviation.

Chief Operating Officer of VivaJets, Tejumade Salami, said the expansion goes beyond fleet size.

“Our expansion is about more than growing the number of aircraft in our fleet. It is about building the operational strength, service capability and partnerships needed to connect businesses and people across diverse African markets.

“Our participation at WCAF V gives us an opportunity to listen to stakeholders, understand the realities of the region and explore how VivaJets can support their connectivity needs as our operations continue to scale,” Salami stated.

Head of Growth and Innovation at VivaJets, Basil Agbor, said the forum provided a platform to understand regional markets and build partnerships.

“Expanding into new markets starts with understanding the people, businesses and institutions that operate within them. WCAF V created an important space for those conversations, allowing us to engage with stakeholders who are actively shaping investment and development across Francophone Africa.

“Our focus is on translating these relationships into practical opportunities for connectivity, collaboration and long-term value. We believe innovation in African aviation must be grounded in a clear understanding of the markets we serve and the challenges our clients need us to solve,” Agbor said.

World.title: C’ River: We’ve Reduced Domestic Debt by N70bn, Governor Otu
World.content:
‎* IGR hit N46.3bn in 2024

‎Cross River State Governor, Senator Bassey Otu, Saturday, presented his administration’s record of debt reduction, asset recovery, infrastructure renewal and public service reforms as evidence of progress under the People First Agenda, declaring that a second term would propel the state from economic recovery to wealth creation and shared prosperity.

‎

‎Otu made the declaration in Calabar, while inaugurating the Cross River State All Progressives Congress (APC) Campaign Council for the 2027 general election.

He charged party leaders and campaign officials to take the administration’s achievements to the electorate, insisting that continuity was essential to consolidating the foundations already laid for sustainable development.

‎

‎Reflecting on the circumstances surrounding his assumption of office in May 2023, the governor recalled that the state was grappling with insecurity, a demoralised public service and underutilised public assets.

“We did not promise all things in one year, but we covenanted to stop the bleeding, clear the ground, recover the losses and restore abandonments,” he said, describing the administration’s first phase as one of recovery and restoration.

‎

‎On fiscal management, Otu disclosed that his government had reduced the inherited domestic debt of more than N204 billion by over N70 billion without taking fresh loans, bringing the outstanding debt to approximately N132.3 billion as of March 2026.

He also disclosed that internally generated revenue increased from N21.1 billion in 2022 to N46.3 billion in 2024.

“Every debt retired is freedom for our children and house-cleaning for fresh fiscal air,” he said, adding that improved revenue and financial discipline would strengthen investment in public services.

‎

‎The governor identified the recovery of strategic public assets as another major achievement, citing the reclamation of Tinapa from the Asset Management Corporation of Nigeria (AMCON), the recovery of nearly N1 billion from Etung Cocoa Estates and other public assets, and ongoing efforts to reclaim the state’s oil wells and secure its interests in the Bakassi axis and proposed Deep Seaport.

He also highlighted improvements in security, the lifting of the employment embargo, the restoration of more than 3,000 local government workers to the payroll and the payment of the first tranche of gratuities after nearly two decades. “The government is not just concrete — it is the people,” he said.

‎

‎On infrastructure and economic revitalisation, Otu cited the reconstruction of the Obudu Cargo Airport runway, the revival of the Teachers Continuous Training Institute in Biase, the transformation of Akamkpa College into the University of Entrepreneurship and the concessioning of the Garment Factory and Obudu Ranch through public-private partnerships.

He also pointed to road construction and rehabilitation, increased and expanded Cally Air fleet and operations, as well as the growing economic impact of Carnival Calabar. “Continuity is an attitude of maturity,” he said, arguing that completing inherited projects and sustaining viable investments were critical to the state’s progress.

‎

‎Otu also highlighted agriculture and digital transformation as key drivers of future growth, noting investments in cocoa, rice, potatoes, palm fruits and cassava to strengthen food security and rural livelihoods.

He said more than 200 kilometres of fibre infrastructure had been deployed across Calabar, over 600 residents had received ICT training, and digital platforms were improving revenue collection and public service delivery.

He further cited Cross River’s selection by the World Bank GovTech Team for its 2026 AI in Governance and Public Administration Bootcamp in Seoul, South Korea, as international recognition of the state’s technological advancement.

‎

‎Outlining his second-term priorities, the governor pledged to turn recovered assets into productive enterprises, complete major infrastructure projects, expand youth and agricultural enterprise programmes, establish industrial parks across the three senatorial districts and improve workers’ welfare.

Urging the campaign council to engage voters across the state’s 18 local government areas and 196 wards with facts and decorum, he said: “You do not change a farmer who has cleared the farm just when it is time to plant. You do not abandon a builder who has laid the foundation when it is time to raise the roof.”

He formally inaugurated the council, declaring that the campaign must be fought not for an individual, but for the future of Cross River and its people.

World.title: ADC Chides Governor Alia Over Performance in Office
World.content:
George Okoh in Makurdi

The African Democratic Congress (ADC) governorship candidate in Benue State for the 2027 general elections, Rt. Hon. Herman Hembe, has declared that Governor Hyacinth Alia is no longer electable, calling on the people of Benue State to reject him at the polls. He maintained that the governor has not performed well enough to deserve a second term in office.

Hembe made this declaration in Oju, headquarters of Oju Local Government Area, during the campaign flag-off ceremony for the ADC Benue South Senatorial candidate, Dr. David Olofu.

Addressing thousands of party faithful drawn from all nine local government areas in Zone C, Hembe said that, in all his years of political experience, he had never encountered a governor who could look his people in the eyes and tell them a lie without hesitation.

He expressed concern over what he described as the unfair distribution of the state’s financial resources, alleging that about ₦1.1 trillion accrued to Benue State over the last three years.

According to Hembe, Governor Alia stated that Zone B received ₦317 billion, representing 91 per cent, while Zone A received ₦17 billion (5 per cent) and Zone C received what he described as an insulting ₦8 billion (2 per cent).

Hembe questioned the basis for the alleged disparity in resource allocation, asking why Zone B would receive such a significant share while Zone C was left with so little.

He maintained that an ADC-led government would not practise sectional governance, stressing that development should promote unity, fairness and equal opportunities across the state.

“Even with the allocation said to have gone to Zone C, where can we point to and say that the two per cent has been invested?” he asked.

Hembe further accused Governor Alia of creating political crises rather than providing effective leadership. He alleged that the governor had lost the confidence of members of his own party, the All Progressives Congress (APC), and questioned why the people of Benue State should continue to trust a governor whose party members no longer have confidence in him.

“If his own party members do not trust him, why should the people of Benue State trust him again?” Hembe asked.

He also congratulated ADC candidates from Zone C, expressing confidence in the party’s growing acceptance across the zone and encouraging the candidates to remain committed to their respective campaigns.

Earlier, the ADC State Chairman, Rt. Hon. Samson Okwu, formally presented the party’s flags to candidates contesting various positions in Zone C. He charged them to work diligently towards securing victory for the party at all levels.

Okwu also welcomed thousands of defectors into the ADC and urged them to remain committed to the progress and success of the party.

In his remarks, the ADC Benue South Senatorial candidate, Dr. David Olofu, thanked the people of Zone C for embracing the ADC, describing it as a viable political platform capable of bringing meaningful change to the zone and Benue State at large.

He pledged to serve as the voice of the people and provide the effective representation they had long been denied.

World.title: Leon Schuster on Eugène Terre’Blanche prank: ‘I nearly died’ [video]
World.content:
Leon Schuster has claimed his candid camera prank with members of the Afrikaner Weerstandsbeweging (AWB) – whose leader was Eugène Terre’Blanche – was one of his most frightening experiences yet.

The veteran TV actor and comedian reflected on his most memorable movies in an interview with SABC’s Leanne Manas.

The 75-year-old also shared a health update and divulged some of his biggest regrets.



LEON SCHUSTER ON MOST FRIGHTENING TV PRANK

Although he pranked Eugène Terre’Blanche directly, Leon Schuster recalls setting up an elaborate prank in Ventersdorp, the home of the AWB leader.

Schuster told Leanne Manas about his early 90s fake tollgate prank, which fooled and angered many members of the AWB community.

Disguised as a black security guard, Schuster demanded that drivers pay a R50 toll for “reconciliation and development”.

He recalled: “Those okes are far, far right. They drive in their bakkies with their guns on the seat next to them; they will fire! They got so pissed off. I nearly died that day”.

The now 75-year-old said that he was threatened with an AK47, and even assaulted by a few.

The clip made it into his 1997 candid camera, Panic Mechanic.



Take a look…

BRINGING SOUTH AFRICANS TOGETHER

During his interview with Leanne Manas, Leon Schuster added that he had no ill intent behind his candid camera pranks, some of which have courted controversy for its portrayal of “blackface”.

He shared: “I’m a prankster, and I’ll die a prankster. It’s all part of the culture of this land”

“It’s important you know your audience. I try to give the people what they want. I’m so sorry I can’t make one final candid-camera movie. But one more clap and my neck will break”.

He added: “I want to be remembered as that okie from the Free State who stood firmly on the ground, who didnt a swollen head, and who contributed somehow to unify our nation through my movies”.

World.title: Da Cruz has a plan for Kaizer Chiefs’ biggest problem
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs have fallen 12 points behind Mamelodi Sundowns after another inconsistent spell in the league.

A series of draws has proved particularly costly, leaving Amakhosi struggling to keep pace with their title rivals.

FERNANDO DA CRUZ: KAIZER CHIEFS NEED WINNING RUN TO REVIVE TITLE CHALLENGE

Da Cruz admits that the situation has become more complicated following their latest setback. However, the French tactician believes the return of injured players could give his team the consistency they have lacked throughout the campaign.



“It’s more difficult today [Saturday] after this game, but the PSL is a long journey, there are 21 fixtures remaining. When we recover our injured players, where we have been unlucky since the beginning of the season, we will have more consistency in our performances, because we made a lot of draws this season,” Da Cruz said.

The Amakhosi coach believes his team have dropped points in matches where they were capable of collecting maximum points.

However, he also acknowledged that a lack of experience has contributed to their inability to turn promising performances into victories.



For Da Cruz, the immediate priority is getting his injured players back and building the momentum needed to close the gap at the top of the standings.

“Normally, many draws, we deserved to win these games but because of our lack of experience, we didn’t win these games. But we will turn it on our side when we recover our squad and for sure, in one moment we must have some positive dynamic with a few wins in a row to continue this journey. We must keep a positive mindset,” he added.

Chiefs cannot afford many more dropped points if they are serious about challenging for the Betway Premiership title.



With Orlando Pirates and Sundowns setting the pace, Amakhosi need to put together a strong run of results rather than relying on their rivals to slip up.

Da Cruz, however, remains convinced that the campaign is far from over. His message is clear: Chiefs must stay positive, recover their squad and start winning consistently if they are to make a serious challenge for the championship.

World.title: PSL coach says Sundowns are still the best
World.content:
Sundonws have set full focus and ambition on their domestic commitments after suffering a disappointing continental exit before reaching the group stages.

Miguel Cardoso described the outcome as a failure, particularly given his previous record of reaching three consecutive finals in the competition.

However, Marumo Gallants coach, Kanalelo believes Sundowns’ response to that disappointment could make them an even more difficult opponent.



MAMELODI SUNDOWNS WILL BE POWERFUL

The former Ka Bo Yellow goalkeeper admitted that the timing of their meeting with the Tshwane giants could have worked in his team’s favour.

Nevertheless, he was unwilling to assume that the continental setback had weakened the defending champions.

“It could be the right time, it could be a wrong time, are they disappointed, are they sad? Sundowns are very much sad… to be out of the Champions League, it could have been an advantage for us, but it could have been a different opportunity for them for winning this competition,” he said.



Kanalelo also pointed to the depth and quality within the Sundowns squad, explaining that even when Cardoso makes several changes, the replacements remain capable of competing at the highest level.

WARNING TO OPPONENTS

For Gallants, that presented a difficult challenge regardless of the Brazilians’ recent continental disappointment.

“They made many changes and when they make changes with the quality they have, you have players that are trying to place themselves in the squad, you can’t say it’s a right or wrong time. The quality is good and they are very strong,” he added.



The coach further explained that Gallants wanted to establish whether Sundowns had been affected psychologically by their Champions League elimination.

He acknowledged that the defending champions have experienced difficult moments before and possess the experience to recover from setbacks.

“They have suffered before, it’s not the first time, but we also wanted to see how badly they had been affected, we gave our best, it tells you they didn’t take us for granted.”



Meanwhile, Gallants have finally given themselves something to build on after securing their first victory of the season against Siwelele FC.

They came from behind to register a 3-2 win on Friday, moving away from the bottom of the Betway Premiership standings.

Kanalelo’s team will now look to make it consecutive victories when they face Golden Arrows before the next FIFA international break.

World.title: Orlando Pirates closing in on Kaizer Chiefs’ Soweto Derby dominance
World.content:
Orlando Pirates have strengthened their dominance over Soweto rivals Kaizer Chiefs following their 2-1 victory in this past weekend’s derby.

The Buccaneers are now unbeaten in their last seven league meetings against Amakhosi, further underlining their recent superiority in one of South African football’s biggest rivalries.

In fact, Pirates have won 10 of their last 18 meetings across all competitions, while Chiefs have managed just a handful of victories during that period.



Amakhosi’s most recent triumph over their rivals came in May last year when they defeated Pirates in the Nedbank Cup final. However, the Glamour Boys have since struggled to get the better of their neighbours, suffering two defeats in their next three encounters.

Despite Pirates’ recent dominance, Chiefs still hold the overall advantage in the historical head-to-head record, with 75 victories compared to the Buccaneers’ 50.

Since the formation of the Premier Soccer League (PSL) in 1996, the balance has shifted.

The two Soweto giants have met 64 times across domestic league and cup competitions during the PSL era. Pirates have claimed 27 victories, compared to Chiefs’ 23, while 14 encounters have ended in draws.

Pirates turning the tide in the Soweto Derby

For much of the rivalry’s history, Kaizer Chiefs enjoyed the upper hand, particularly during the 1980s when the Glamour Boys were among the dominant forces in South African football.

However, the balance gradually began to shift in Pirates’ favour during the 1990s, with the Buccaneers increasingly challenging their neighbours for domestic honours.



That shift has become even more noticeable in recent years, with Pirates enjoying a sustained run of positive results against Chiefs.

The Buccaneers’ dominance is also reflected in their success on the trophy front. Having collected major domestic honours and established themselves as regular contenders in African competitions, Pirates have enjoyed a successful period.

Their current run against Chiefs could therefore be seen as a reminder of the dominance Amakhosi once enjoyed during their golden era in the 1980s.

While Chiefs remain ahead in the overall historical head-to-head record, Pirates are steadily changing the narrative of the Soweto Derby.

Can Chiefs turn the tables?

World.title: SALGA urges voters to choose capable municipal leaders
World.content:
The South African Local Government Association (SALGA) has urged registered voters to prioritise the upcoming local government elections and elect ethical, capable and accountable leaders who will shape the future of municipalities.

South Africans will head to the polls on Wednesday, 4 November, to elect representatives who will serve in the country’s seventh local government administration.

SALGA CALLS ON VOTERS TO MAKE INFORMED CHOICES

SALGA said communities have a decisive role to play in building a responsive and effective local government system. It said this responsibility begins with electing leaders who are prepared to serve with integrity and put the public first.



“Voting, therefore, is more than a constitutional right; it is a civic responsibility and a vital part of the social compact through which citizens hold local government to account,” SALGA spokesperson Motalatale Modiba said.

The association encouraged voters to carefully consider the calibre, integrity and commitment of candidates seeking to represent them in municipal councils.

The elections come at a time when municipalities face persistent challenges, including poor service delivery, deteriorating infrastructure and concerns about financial management.

Municipalities are responsible for providing essential services such as water, sanitation and local roads. The leaders elected will therefore play an important role in determining how these services are managed and how communities’ needs are addressed.

SALGA said the future of local government depends largely on the choices voters make at the ballot box, adding that every vote is an opportunity to strengthen local democracy, improve service delivery and place communities at the centre of governance.

REMINDER: SPECIAL VOTES WILL BE CAST FROM MONDAY

Registered voters whose special vote applications have been approved will cast their ballots on Monday, 2 November, and Tuesday, 3 November. All other registered voters will vote on Wednesday, 4 November.



Special votes are intended to allow eligible voters who may be unable to vote on election day to exercise their democratic right.
