World.title: Mogale claims ANC has reversed eight years of neglect in Tshwane
World.content:
PRETORIA - ANC Tshwane mayoral candidate nominee Tlangi Mogale has defended the party's record in the metro, claiming the ANC has spent the past 24 months reversing years of neglect and prioritising residents' needs.

Speaking during a We The Nation Elections 2026 debate, Mogale said the party had demonstrated its commitment to residents through improved service delivery, infrastructure development and efforts to stabilise the City of Tshwane's finances.

She argued that townships, which she said had been neglected for years while service delivery focused on affluent areas, were now receiving greater attention under the current administration.

“If you check the budget that we have approved through an ANC deployee, we have provided services in the townships, the intergovernmental relations component has also been strengthened,” Mogale said.

Addressing the persistent water challenges in Hammanskraal, Mogale said the City had strengthened its relationship with national government to help deliver projects that were beyond its financial capacity.

She cited the completion of the Klipdrift package plant as one of the developments resulting from these interventions.

“Most importantly, we have undone the injustices that the people of Tshwane were subjected to in the last eight years. Townships were neglected and service delivery only focused in affluent areas,” she said.

Mogale also defended the ANC's handling of the municipality's finances, saying the City was servicing its Eskom debt and maintaining its current account.

She said the administration inherited financial challenges but managed to stabilise the municipality's finances and unlock funding for capital expenditure projects after taking office approximately a year ago.

“Currently, Tshwane is a construction site because of the ANC. I say the ANC because, in as much as we are in a coalition, we enjoy majority seats in the infrastructure structure,” she said.

Tshwane is currently governed by a 10-party coalition comprising the ANC, Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF) and seven smaller parties.

World.title: Brink accuses ANC of planning to use 'puppet' to run Tshwane
World.content:
PRETORIA - Democratic Alliance (DA) Tshwane mayoral candidate Cilliers Brink has accused the ANC of planning to use a political "puppet" to influence the running of the City of Tshwane, rather than fielding its own mayoral candidate.

Brink launched a scathing attack on the ANC, accusing the party of undermining coalition-led governments in Tshwane and other cities since losing its majority.

"Since the ANC has lost its majority in Tshwane and other cities, it has done everything either to bring down the governments that we elected in its place or to sabotage them using a network of cadres and tenderpreneurs," he said.

"That is why they don't have a mayoral candidate. They don't need one. They're going to pick a puppet to do the fronting and they'll make the decisions," he added.

Brink is seeking to reclaim the Tshwane mayoral chain, having previously served as the city's executive mayor from March 2023 until September 2024.

He said the ANC must be "comprehensively defeated", adding that the DA's priorities would include restoring accountability, improving municipal services and tackling corruption.

"Our priority will be to fire corrupt officials and tenderpreneurs and replace them with honest, hardworking people.

"We will also restore law and order using crime-fighting technology, upgrade water, electricity, waste collection and public lighting through private partnerships, and use the assets of the city to draw investment to create jobs," Brink said.

He maintained that restoring Tshwane's administration would require leaders with integrity, claiming that the DA had not been implicated in allegations of corruption or political interference.

"No one from the DA has been mentioned at the Madlanga Commission. None of the DA councillors have been cited as interfering with tenders," he said.

READ MORE | VOTING STATIONS ARE READY SPECIAL VOTES

Brink also vowed to confront what he described as the city's "water tanker mafia", arguing that residents should have reliable access to water through their taps rather than depending on tanker services.

"We have to stand up to the water tanker mafia in this city. We need water in our taps, not via tankers," he said.

World.title: Tshwane's Spies says smaller parties have a place in democracy
World.content:
PRETORIA - With just hours to go before special voting gets underway ahead of the 4 November local government elections, Tshwane FF Plus mayoral candidate Willie Spies has urged voters to choose political parties based on their principles rather than their size.

Spies argues that smaller parties should not be dismissed as offering "wasted votes", saying South Africa's political landscape has changed permanently and that no single party should expect to dominate the political scene.

He criticised parties that campaign on promises to eliminate smaller political players, arguing that such an approach undermines the principles of democracy.

“Up to 10 years ago, there was only one big party in South Africa, and that was the ANC. Every other party was a smaller party. Ten years ago, things changed, and they changed forever. There won't ever be one political party dominating the political scene anymore,” Spies said.

He added that every political party starts an election on an equal footing, with voters ultimately determining how much representation each party receives.

“In an election, every single party starts at zero percent. It is up to the voters to decide what the representation of each and every political party will be after the elections.”

Citing the Democratic Party's performance in the 1994 elections, Spies pointed out that the party secured just 1.7% of the vote before growing into a larger political force.

“Democracy should be allowed to run its course. People should be allowed to vote for principle, not for size. If size is the only thing you can offer, you've got very little to offer.”

The FF Plus is currently the fifth-largest party in the City of Tshwane. Spies believes the municipality urgently needs a change in leadership and management.

“Municipalities are about four things: water, electricity, infrastructure and safety. The past 15 years of municipal management was a dismal failure in all four respects,” Spies said.

READ MORE | PEOPLE STILL BELIEVE THAT SA CAN DO BETTER - HLABISA

He urged voters to look beyond established political power structures and consider parties offering a different approach to governance.

“You cannot keep on doing the same thing and expect any changes. People need to start voting for political parties according to principle.”

Positioning the FF Plus as a potential coalition partner, Spies said the party believes in values-driven governance and wants to see Tshwane succeed.

“The FF Plus is a reliable coalition party. We believe in principle government based on values, and we want to see this city succeed,” he said.

World.title: 2.6 million South Africans set to cast special votes
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - It's all systems go for the 2026 Local Government Elections, with 2.6 million South Africans expected to cast their special votes over the next two days.

Of those approved, 1.9 million will vote at designated voting stations, while the remainder will be visited at their registered addresses by IEC officials.

IEC chief electoral officer Sy Mamabolo said approved home-visit voters must remain available at the addresses provided in their applications on 2 and 3 November.

Voting station-based special voters must cast their ballots at the stations where they are registered.

Gauteng has the highest number of approved voting station-based special votes, at 391,000.

Voting stations will be open from 8am to 5pm on both days.

World.title: We The Nation | Election edition | Tshwane | 1 November 2026
World.content:
PRETORIA - Water. Electricity. Service delivery. These are the issues that matter most to residents of Tshwane.

With the local government elections just days away, the question is simple: who has the plan, the experience and the leadership to turn things around?

The Tshwane mayoral candidates go head-to-head in our final We The Nation Elections 2026 special, live from the University of Pretoria.

We put the tough questions to those hoping to lead the capital city. What have they delivered? What will they change? And, in a city where coalitions are likely to remain part of the political landscape, can they put politics aside and work together in the interests of residents?

With special voting underway and election day approaching on 4 November, the stakes couldn't be higher.

World.title: People still believe that SA can do better - Hlabisa
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - 'If you are tired of empty promises, choose the IFP.'

That's the message from party leader Velenkosini Hlabisa.

Hlabisa closed the IFP election campaign in Ulundi, ahead of Wednesday's elections.

"‘They are tired of failed service deliveries, of dry taps, broken roads, unreliable electricity, uncollected refuse, dark streets and municipal offices that do not respond, tired of seeing the country moving backwards.

"Through our campaign we had something profound and encouraging. Beneath the anger and disappointment, there’s hope. People have not stopped believing that SA can do better, asking for a government that works, leadership that serves and a future that children can look forward to and inherit."

World.title: 'We've heard very clearly' - ANC president tells EC supporters
World.content:
MDANTSANE - ANC President Cyril Ramaphosa said the party has listened to communities’ concerns ahead of the elections.

Speaking at a campaign rally in Mdantsane, he said the ANC heard calls for better working conditions, action against gender-based violence, and greater support for people with disabilities.

Ramaphosa pledged the party’s commitment to addressing these issues.

" We heard very clearly what the aspirations of our people are, but we also heard the enthusiasm as well as the encouragement of our people. We've heard them repeating that they want us to work diligently to advance the lives of our people. We have listened to the workers of our country talking about, yes, the need that they want to see to improve the conditions of employment.

" It is also the ANC's ability to listen and to have deep exchanges with our people. We've also gone around Simamele, Okumkani namakosi ethu, as they too were raising many issues that concern them. We have listened to the women of our country as they too have raised issues that concern gender-based violence. We have listened to people who are disabled, and we have heard too the issues that concern them."

World.title: Gachagua dismisses Uhuru reconciliation calls, says 'we are one team'
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

DCP leader Rigathi Gachagua received at PCEA Kamangu in Kikuyu constituency by former Kiambu governor James Nyoro on November 1, 2026. [George Njunge, Standard]

Former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua has dismissed calls for mediation between him and former President Uhuru Kenyatta, insisting that the two leaders remain in contact and have no differences requiring reconciliation.

Gachagua said attempts by Mount Kenya elders to broker peace between them were unnecessary, maintaining that he and the former Head of State continue to communicate, meet and share meals despite perceptions of a political fallout.

He challenged elders calling for reconciliation to instead focus on uniting the Mount Kenya community, warning that internal divisions could weaken the region's political voice and influence.

“On unity, as a community we have to remain united. Our unity is strength. Nimeona some elders in the newspaper wakisema tunataka to reconcile Rigathi Gachagua and Uhuru Kenyatta. How do you reconcile two brothers, who love one another and work together?” he posed.

The former Deputy President maintained that he and Uhuru were still on the same team, dismissing claims that their relationship had deteriorated to a point requiring third-party intervention.

“President Uhuru Kenyatta and I are one team. We work together. Please elders don’t reconcile us because there is no need for reconciliation. We are working together. There is no work there, we are one. We talk the same language, we meet, talk, we agree,” he said.

Gachagua further urged Mount Kenya elders to resist attempts to divide the community along political lines and instead promote dialogue and cohesion among its leaders.

“Our unity is our strength as a community. Please help me to unite Mount Kenya elders and tell people not to accept to be divided,” he added.

His remarks come amid growing calls by sections of Mount Kenya elders for reconciliation among influential political figures from the region following political differences that have emerged since the 2022 General Election.

Uhuru, who served as Kenya's fourth president from 2013 to 2022, remains an influential political figure in the region, while Gachagua has continued to position himself as a key voice in Mount Kenya politics.

World.title: Sifuna rallies opposition leaders to unite against Ruto in 2027
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Linda Mwananchi leader Edwin Sifuna adresses a rally at Ukunda in Kwale County on 31st October, 2026. [Omondi Onyango, Standard]

Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna’s Linda Mwananchi movement took its grassroots mobilisation tour to Kwale County, a day after unveiling its secretariat and leadership, with leaders urging the opposition to unite behind one candidate to face President William Ruto in 2027.

The unveiling had been marred by disagreement, with Wiper leader Kalonzo Musyoka jeered. Addressing a rally at Masai Grounds in Ukunda town, Sifuna said Kenyans were yearning for a single, strong opposition candidate and asked other leaders not to let them down.

“To send Ruto home, we need a strong team and a strong presidential candidate. I will ask other leaders to listen to the voices of the people politely because this is the voice of God,” he said.

The team made stopovers in Samburu, Kinango, Kwale town and Kombani during the day-long tour. Unlike earlier rallies in Mombasa, the Kwale events drew modest crowds, amid claims that local organisers had failed to mobilise supporters.

The mobilisation tour covered Samburu Town, Kinango Town, Kombani Junction, Lunga Lunga Town, and culminated in a major public rally at the Ukunda Showground.

The movement officially opened its new Kwale County office as part of a push to build county-level structures ahead of the 2027 General Election.

Addressing supporters in the rain, Sifuna declared that he will continue to build consensus among the opposition to ensure that they are united to send Ruto home in 2027. he said that divisions of the opposition leaders will guarantee Ruto a second term.

He warned against schemes to elbow local leaders out of the front lines, stressing that Kwale residents and local aspirants must drive the agenda on regional issues like water shortages and mineral exploitation. The Kwale tour marks the first public rallies after weeks without a large-scale county mobilisation exercise.

It has previously held gatherings in Mombasa and Taita Taveta as part of its plan to reach all 47 counties. The tour took place the same day the Orange Democratic Movement (ODM) was holding a rally at Jacaranda Grounds in Nairobi's Embakasi East constituency.

Embakasi East MP Babu Owino urged Sifuna, Musyoka, DCP leader Rigathi Gachagua and Jubilee leader Fred Matiang’i to agree on one presidential candidate, warning that time was running out.

“We are urging all opposition leaders to sit down and talk. We only have nine months to the General Election, and you should agree on one presidential challenger to President Ruto,” he said. “Sifuna, Kalonzo, Gachagua and Matiang’i should come together now. United we stand, divided we fall.”

isii Senator Richard Onyonka said it was time for opposition leaders to lock themselves in a room and emerge with a single candidate to face Mr Ruto. The call was backed by Linda Mwananchi chairman Godfrey Osotsi and Secretary General Caroli Omondi.

Trans Nzoia Governor George Natembeya, however, said Sifuna was best placed to challenge the President and asked Mr Gachagua and Mr Musyoka to back him.

“I want to urge Gachagua and Kalonzo to back Sifuna for the opposition to secure an easy win against Ruto. I want to assure you that there will be no rigging of the election,” he said.

Meru Governor Kawira Mwangaza said Kenyans would reject Ruto at the ballot for failing to honour pledges, including those on women’s empowerment.

Sifuna accused the President of failing to protect the Constitution and the rights of Kenyans. “He has focused more on building houses and markets and failed to protect lives,” he said.

He also claimed the government had issued title deeds for smaller parcels than residents used to own, while land was stolen. He further alleged that the government was plotting to plunder mineral resources at Mrima Hill in Kwale and demanded that an agreement with American investors be made public.

World.title: Musonye to lead AFCON 2027 preparations
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Sports Cabinet Secretary Salim Mvurya with Local Organising Committee (LOC) Standing Committee chairperson Nicholas Musonye on October 29, 2026. [Jonah Onyango, Standard]

Sports Cabinet Secretary Salim Mvurya has unveiled the Local Organising Committee (LOC) Standing Committee for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON PAMOJA 2027), with Nicholas Musonye appointed chairman to oversee Kenya’s preparations for the continental football tournament.

Musonye will be deputised by Hussein Mohammed, while Anthony Lung’aho Inzihuli, also known as Antony Emmanuel Inzahuli Lung’aho, will serve as head of the secretariat and chief executive officer.

The committee is tasked with coordinating Kenya’s preparations, including stadium renovations, infrastructure development, operational planning and logistical arrangements ahead of the tournament, which Kenya will co-host with Uganda and Tanzania.

Mvurya said the committee brings together individuals with experience, professional expertise and leadership to help deliver a successful competition that meets the expectations of football fans, participating teams and the Confederation of African Football (CAF).

“I have unveiled the TotalEnergies CAF Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) PAMOJA 2027 LOC Standing Committee, entrusting its members with the national responsibility of coordinating and overseeing Kenya’s preparations towards delivering a world-class, memorable and successful continental football tournament,” Mvurya said.

He challenged members to move from planning to implementation, emphasising operational readiness, coordination, strategic partnerships, financial accountability and adherence to delivery timelines.

“With less than eight months to kick-off, I challenged the committee to move decisively from planning to execution,” he said.

Besides Musonye, Mohammed and Lung’aho Inzihuli, the listed committee members include Football Kenya Federation (FKF) Vice-President McDonald Mariga and FKF National Executive Committee representative Robert Macharia.

Other members named in the roster are Timothy Nabea, a former FKF NEC member; Gabriel Mghendi; Peter Kamau; Kerubo Momanyi; Benard Lagat; Collins Kalee; Caleb Amwayi; Ken Rungu; and Dan Shikanda, the former AFC Leopards chairperson.

The list also includes Charles Njagi, Thomas Karugu, Evelyn Cheluget, Miriam Chepkoech, Rodgers Chimega, Diana Injendi Manyengo and Collins Were.

The 38 committee members also comprises representation across functional areas, including finance, technical matters, refereeing, legal affairs and youth development.

The committee is expected to coordinate the different aspects of tournament preparation and ensure that the relevant agencies and stakeholders work towards agreed targets.

Kenya’s preparations also include the development of Talanta Sports City, officially known as the Raila Odinga International Stadium, which is expected to strengthen the country's capacity to host major international football matches.

Mvurya said the planned high-profile encounter between German giants FC Bayern München and Dutch powerhouse AFC Ajax, scheduled for January 5, 2027, would provide an opportunity to assess the country’s readiness.

The event is expected to test security arrangements, transport and logistics, crowd management, operational systems and the overall fan experience.

The CS also disclosed that representatives of the two European clubs had visited Kenya to assess its capacity to host the proposed fixture.

He said the government was adopting a whole-of-government approach, involving relevant agencies responsible for security, immigration, tourism, travel and hospitality.

AFCON 2027 is expected to attract thousands of supporters, officials and international visitors, creating opportunities for hotels, airlines, tour operators, transport businesses and other service providers.

The government is also positioning the tournament as an opportunity to promote tourism, attract investment, develop sporting infrastructure and inspire young footballers.

Mvurya said the committee carries the responsibility of delivering an event that would bring national pride while creating a lasting legacy for the country.

“I reaffirmed their mandate and reminded them that they carry the hopes and aspirations of over 55 million Kenyans to deliver a tournament that brings pride and joy to the country while securing a lasting legacy in sports development, tourism, investment and economic opportunities,” he said.

World.title: Not so fast! Court blocks Bomas expansion
World.content:
Contractors hired are barred from clearing vegetation, cutting trees, excavating, grading, fencing, constructing routes, and undertaking any works at the disputed site. [File, Standard]

The Environment and Lands Court has blocked the government from continuing with the construction of a car park inside the Nairobi National Park.

Justice Grace Kemei, in her ruling, said that the contractors hired are barred from clearing vegetation, cutting trees, excavating, grading, fencing, constructing routes, and undertaking any works at the disputed site.

World.title: Kikuyu PCEA church loses 2.7-acre illegally acquired land
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Justice Jacqueline Mogeni, in her verdict, said the land in contention was public property and its registration in the name of the said church was irregular and fraudulent. [Courtesy, EACC]

The Presbyterian Church of East Africa (PCEA) has lost its 2.7-acre piece of land to a school.

This is after the Environment and Lands Court at Thika established that the land under the church's Ruguthi Women's Guild was a school playground and was illegally allocated.

Presiding Judge Jacqueline Mogeni, in her verdict, said the land in contention was public property, and its registration in the name of the said church was irregular and fraudulent.

According to her, the land had been reserved for use as a playground by Kanyiha, Lusigetti and Njumbi Primary Schools.

The verdict follows a case filed by the Law Society of Kenya, with the Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission (EACC) participating as an interested party.

In a statement on Monday, EACC's head of Corporate Affairs and Communication Stephen Karuga said the anti-graft agency presented evidence demonstrating that the land had been reserved for public use and therefore, any allocation to third parties was irregular. Justice Jacqueline Mogeni, in her verdict, said the land in contention was public property and its registration in the name of the said church was irregular and fraudulent. [Courtesy, EACC]

"Our investigations established that the land was set aside in 1957 by the former County Council of Kiambu for use as a school playing field," Karuga said, adding, "the investigations further revealed that there was no letter of offer or acceptance, no evidence of payment of rent rates and no proof that the Women's Guild had paid any consideration to the council for the land."

According to Karuga, the judgement safeguards a vital public facility used by more than 1,300 pupils, ensuring that the playground remains available for learning, sports and recreation for the current and future generations.

As a result, the judge said the allocation, transfer and registration of the land LR. NO KARAI/350 and subsequent issuance of a title deed in 2001 was unprocedural, illegal, null and void.

"An order of Mandamus is hereby issued directing the 3rd respondent, the Land Registrar, Kiambu Chief Land Registrar, to forthwith cancel and revoke the Title Deed and all register entries in respect of the land issued to the 1st respondent on Dec 6, 2001, or at any subsequent date," the Judge said.

The judge further ordered that the said parcel of land be handed over to the Board of Management of the two schools and the Education Ministry.

"An order of permanent injunction is hereby issued restraining the 1st respondent, whether by herself, her church officials, agents, servants, assigns or anyone claiming through her, from entering into, taking possession of, fencing, depositing construction materials upon, transferring, charging, developing or in any other manner dealing or interfering with the land," she ordered.

World.title: Sakaja protests release of 14 suspects linked to Eastleigh collapsed building
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Sakaja demanded answers from Kamukunji Police on how the suspects were arrested in June but released on Sh50,000 bail without being charged in court. [GPS]

Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja has protested the release of suspects linked to the collapsed building in Eastleigh.

While pushing for the county to have prosecutorial powers, Sakaja demanded answers from Kamukunji Police on how the suspects were arrested in June but released on Sh50,000 bail without being charged in court.

Sakaja in statement posted on his X account (formerly Twitter) said City Hall had taken enforcement action against those involved after establishing change of user from a residential property to a commercial had been approved.

According to Sakaja, architectural plans required to authorise construction had not been approved.

The Governor said County officers arrested the suspects and handed them over to Kamukunji Police Station because county governments no longer hold prosecutorial powers they previously held.

“We enforced the law and arrested those involved. However, because we do not have prosecutorial powers, the suspects were handed over to Kamukunji Police Station. They were reportedly released on a cash bail of Sh50,000 without being taken to court,” Sakaja said.

“We want the police to explain why the suspects were released without being presented in court and why construction was allowed to continue. These are serious questions that must be answered,” he added.

A police occurrence book entry from Kamukunji Police Station indicates that 14 suspects were booked into custody on June 17, 2026, over the alleged offences relating to contravention of city planning laws.

Enforcement action and arrests were made severally by the county officials and most recently in July after failing to comply with the enforcement order below. However the suspects were released on a 50k bail at Kamukunji police on the very same day. Prosecution of the same was also denied. We have repeatedly asked for the resumption of the power to prosecute such violations of such county and county related laws after this was taken away from County governments in 2024 (one such letter to the office of the DPP is attached). Meanwhile, several such cases have either been rejected by prosecutors (who are independent of the County), dismissed by the justice system or have had minimal fines imposed. Fining a developer 50k for an illegal development with hundreds of millions without orders to stop and remove the offensive development is completely unreasonable. I raised this in the Senate a fortnight ago and we shall keep pushing for a review of this position. All of these instances, where enforcement action has been curtailed, blocked or interfered with, will be published to the public. October 25, 2026

The entry, recorded under OB No. 98/17/06/2026, names the suspects and states that they were booked by Nairobi City County officers before being placed in police cells.

A separate Kenya Police Service record indicates that 10 suspects were subsequently released on a cash bail of Sh50,000.

The entry, recorded at 9.44pm, states that the release was carried out on the instructions of the Officer Commanding Station (OCS), identified in the record as C.I. Onyapidi, through Corporal Awadh.

The record references receipt number 2039434 and states that the suspects left the station without complaints.

However, the documents do not, on their own, establish the specific charges against the suspects, the legal basis for the bail arrangement or whether they were subsequently presented in court.

The discrepancy between the 14 suspects recorded as booked into custody and the 10 named in the release entry also raises questions about the subsequent status of the other suspects. Sakaja demanded answers from Kamukunji Police on how the suspects were arrested in June but released on Sh50,000 bail without being charged in court. [GPS]

Sakaja said a June 2025 enforcement notice adds another dimension to the questions surrounding the property and the enforcement of planning regulations.

The notice, issued by Nairobi City County over alleged construction works undertaken without the required development permission, cited the Physical and Land Use Planning Act, 2019, and county by-laws.

It directed the recipient to stop the works and remove the development described as illegal, warning that the County could undertake the required action and recover the costs if the directives were not followed.

The notice also provided for an appeal to the County Physical and Land Use Planning Liaison Committee.

Sakaja clarified that approval to change a property’s use from private to commercial-cum-residential does not amount to approval of architectural plans authorising construction.

He said the County approved the change of use but did not approve the architectural plans, yet construction proceeded.

I have seen some people peddling a fake approval document alleging that the Eastleigh development was approved. It is telling that this is the same document that the Eastleigh developer used to get NCA approval. They allege that the development was approved in January of 2024. This is not true. The application for development as shown below was made in November of 2024, it could not have been approved in February of the same year. Also, there is a difference between a change of user approval and a development approval. The developer applied for change of use from residential to residential & commercial in August of 2024. Change of user was approved in October of 2024. Development approval has never been granted. The developer went on to build with impunity and without building approvals despite enforcement action by the county and arrests. — Sakaja Arthur Johnson (@SakajaJohnson) October 25, 2026

“If the building had been approved for construction, I would have named the officers who approved it so that action could be taken against them,” he said.

Sakaja, in his argument, said the current arrangement creates a gap between enforcement and prosecution, leaving counties dependent on other agencies after taking action against alleged offenders. Sakaja demanded answers from Kamukunji Police on how the suspects were arrested in June but released on Sh50,000 bail without being charged in court. [GPS]

Under his proposal, appropriately authorised county prosecutors would be able to pursue qualifying county offences through the courts, subject to the law and the constitutional authority of the Director of Public Prosecutions.

He said county prosecutors previously had a better understanding of technical offences involving planning, construction and other county regulations, enabling them to handle such cases more directly.

“We want to be able not only to enforce regulations and make arrests, but also to take offenders to court and prosecute them. When counties had prosecutorial powers, we had prosecutors who understood the nature and seriousness of county offences and could ensure that appropriate legal action was taken,” he said.

World.title: Pregnant woman rescued from collapsed Eastleigh building
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kenya Red Cross workers after rescuing a man who trapped in the rubble.

A pregnant woman was on Saturday evening rescued from the multi-storey building that collapsed in Nairobi’s Eastleigh estate on Friday, October 23 and rushed to the Kenyatta National Hospital (KNH) for treatment.

She is the second person to rescued as earlier in the afternoon the Kenya Red Cross society announced the rescue of a man from the ill-fated building.

The man was also taken to KNH for treatment with the society saying that the rescue followed hours of work put in by the search and rescue multi-agency team.

“After hours of painstaking work alongside multi-agency partners, our search and rescue teams in Eastleigh brought a trapped man out of the rubble,” said Red Cross.

The rescue comes even as the fate of six people who were reported missing on Friuday remains unknown with rescue teams still continuing with the search at the site of the collapsed building along Yusuf Haji Avenue.

The society said that 66 of the 67 construction workers who were at the site had been traced and accounted for but the search continues for people who may have been near the site of the collapsed building.

The development comes as police announced that they had launched a manhunt for the for the owner and contractor of a building.

Police spokesperson Muchiri Nyaga said that officers had launched a probe in collaboration with relevant bodies to establish the cause of the collapse and determine criminal liability.

“Any individual or entity found culpable of negligence or of violating building regulations will face the full force of the law,” he said in a statement.

Nyaga called on members of public to stay completely clear of Yusuf Haji Avenue and 9th Street to give access to heavy excavators, specialised canine units and rescue personnel to perform their duties.

Earlier Saturday, at least 31 families reported their relatives missing as coordinated rescue efforts entered their second day.

No deaths have been reported so far.

The National Construction Authority (NCA) on Friday evening identified the developer, contractor, architect and structural engineer listed for the collapsed building.

The Authority has faced scrutiny over its oversight role, as Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja said the project had failed to comply with construction guidelines.

He said the county had forwarded relevant information to the Directorate of Criminal Investigations for further investigation.

In a statement, the NCA said the building was registered on July 30, 2025, as a proposed development on 9th Street in Eastleigh.

It identified 9th Street Plaza Limited as the developer and Stromax Holdings E.A. Limited as the contractor.

Emmanuel Mwangi Maina was listed as the project architect, while Joseph Muturi Mugu was named as the structural engineer.

World.title: Several feared trapped in Eastleigh building collapse
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Rescue efforts at the collapsed storey building in Eastleigh 9th street in Nairobi County. [Benard Orwongo Standard]

What was supposed to be a usually busy Friday afternoon in Eastleigh's 9th Street turned chaotic after an 18-floor building that was under construction came down, tumbling.

By Friday evening, rescue operations were still ongoing, with cries from people believed to have been trapped being heard from a distance as bulldozers and rescuers continued the search operation.

Two victims, a man and a woman, who were injured in the building had been rescued and rushed to hospital as the search continued.

Asha Jilo, one of the witnesses, said the building collapsed around 1:09 pm just after the afternoon prayers.

"Immediately after the building collapsed, we started contacting some people we know who work there, one of them was still available on the phone until around 3 pm, when his phone went offline," Jilo shared

On Fridays, Eastleigh is usually a hive of activities, being the main market day, but all the businesses were shut as police were battling rowdy youths, some of them believed to be opportunists.

The building, whose height was said to be about 15 floors, had not been cleared for occupation as required, raising questions about why the investors had allowed it to be taken.

It is said that the ground and first floors were already occupied by businesses, raising fears that the number of victims could be high. Rescue efforts at the collapsed storey building in Eastleigh 9th street in Nairobi County. [Benard Orwongo Standard]

At the time of the collapse, it is said that some construction workers were busy on the upper floors.

Governor Johnson Sakaja, who visited the scene after the collapse, was still gathering information about the building. The first priority was about saving lives.

“The building that collapsed is around 16 floors, and we have got information about the building, but what is more concerned right now is for us to save lives,” said Sakaja

Adding, “Equipment has already been mobilized, excavators and breakers, so we can be able to remove the big debris and save lives,’

The Governor said some developers engage qualified professionals to secure construction approvals before dismissing them and disregarding approved plans and safety standards.

He urged professional bodies to strengthen oversight, investigate such cases and take appropriate disciplinary action, stressing that developers must comply with approved designs, engage qualified personnel and obtain occupation certificates after safety inspections.

Rescue efforts at the collapsed storey building in Eastleigh 9th street in Nairobi County. [Benard Orwongo Standard]

Nairobi Regional Police Commander Issa Mohamud, who was at the scene, said that, according to reliable information, several people were trapped inside the debris, inside the big boulders, and the rescue effort is ongoing.

The city police boss said investigations will be carried out to ascertain who is responsible for any negligence.

“If there will be any death, that is negligence by murder. Whoever is the owner, whoever authorized the building, all of them will be charged properly. But that will come after thorough investigation is done,” he warned

Adding, “We will not excuse anybody on this matter. This has become now and then, and we will make sure that people face the law accordingly for any criminal negligence,”

World.title: Police probe Jeffrey Epstein’s time spent at Balmoral with Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor
World.content:
Scottish police are investigating the time convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein spent with Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor at Balmoral, a private royal estate in Scotland which is a favored retreat for the monarchy.

“We have received information and active enquiries are ongoing but these are at a very early stage,” a Police Scotland spokesperson told CNN on Friday, without giving details about the investigation.

“All enquiries are evidence-led, with the needs of victim survivors at the heart of those enquiries,” the police spokesperson said. “We would never confirm details of ongoing enquiries and it would be inappropriate to comment further.”

British newspaper The Daily Express reported that the investigation was related to allegations women were “trafficked” to Balmoral.

Since the release of the Epstein files, Mountbatten-Windsor, known as Prince Andrew until his brother King Charles III stripped him of his titles, has faced a slew of allegations over his links to the late sex offender. He was arrested on suspicion of misconduct in public office in February and interviewed under caution before being released.

The scandal has left Mountbatten-Windsor’s already battered reputation in tatters and plunged Britain’s royal family into crisis.

Pictures previously released by US prosecutors in 2021 appear to show Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell, the financier’s right-hand woman currently serving time in a US federal prison for sex trafficking and other crimes, at Balmoral in 1999.

This undated image appears to show British socialite Ghislaine Maxwell and US financier Jeffrey Epstein in Queen’s log cabin at Balmoral. US District Court for the Southern District of New York

Buckingham Palace has consistently said that it does not speak for Mountbatten-Windsor and does not comment on active police investigations.

Mountbatten-Windsor has vehemently denied any and all wrongdoing in his dealings with Epstein. Police have said their investigation into misconduct in public office, relating to his time as a trade envoy for Britain, is still ongoing.

World.title: Tensions over Poland’s top court ignite as the country’s prime minister and president square off
World.content:
Warsaw, Poland AP — Prime Minister Donald Tusk said on Saturday that his government would press ahead with efforts to restore the independence of Prime Minister Donald Tusk said on Saturday that his government would press ahead with efforts to restore the independence of Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal, as hundreds of protesters gathered for a second night against the suspension of the court’s president.

The pro-European government said the suspension is necessary to restore judicial independence, while critics from the opposition have likened it to a “coup d’etat.”

President Karol Nawrocki — who opposes the pro-European government — turned back his plane during a flight to Senegal on Friday evening and returned home. On Friday night, he made his way to the Constitutional Tribunal despite the chaos and said he helped the suspended court president enter the building.

Police said they detained three protesters on Friday night after some threw objects at officers and tried to break through the security fence around the court.

The dispute over the long-embattled Constitutional Tribunal is likely to deepen political polarization in Poland a year before a parliamentary election, further intensifying the standoff between the pro-European government and the national-conservative opposition party Law and Justice, or PiS.

Police block the entrance to the Constitutional Tribunal in Warsaw, Poland, on Friday. Piotr Lapinski/NurPhoto/AP

Critics in Poland and the European Union accuse PiS, which led the country between 2015 and 2023, of imposing political control over key judicial institutions. Reforms introduced under the PiS government prompted the EU to impose fines on Poland.

Tusk’s pro-European government came to power in 2023 with a promise to restore the independence of the judiciary. Since then, its efforts have been blocked by vetoes from two successive presidents aligned with PiS, including Nawrocki.

“Restoring the rule of law is our obligation,” Tusk wrote on X on Friday evening. “After years of lawlessness under PiS this is a difficult process, sometimes painful and it requires decisive action. There is no other way.”

Tusk had earlier pledged that his government would ensure the tribunal was again staffed with lawfully appointed judges while acknowledging that his methods may not be to everyone’s liking.

The functioning of the Constitutional Tribunal had been impaired for years. The Court of Justice of the European Union, the EU’s top court, had said it was no longer an impartial court after PiS appointments. Even after Tusk took power, efforts to balance the court were hampered by Nawrocki and the tribunal’s president, Bogdan Święczkowski.

On Friday evening, the Constitutional Tribunal’s website announced the suspension of Święczkowski. Shortly after, the protesters, including PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński and far-right politicians, began rallying outside the building.

Polish President Karol Nawrocki returns to Warsaw after turning a plane en route to Senegal for a state visit. Slawomir Kaminski/Agencja Wyborcza/Reuters

The government says Święczkowski repeatedly broke the law and jeopardized the tribunal’s work. Święczkowski became head of the court under the former PiS government. Tusk has accused him of blocking judges elected by the parliamentary majority from taking up their posts at the tribunal.

“Since last night, we’re dealing with a massive constitutional crisis in Poland, the result of an illegal, forceful attempt to take over an important institution,” Marcin Przydacz, a top aide to the Polish president, told The Associated Press.

Przydacz said that the president had invited all parliamentary parties to talks on Saturday in an effort to defuse tensions and find a solution to the crisis.

The government is a broad coalition made up of Tusk’s centrist Civic Coalition, the Left, and two more conservative groupings, Poland 2050 and the Polish People’s Party, or PSL. Representatives of Poland 2050 and PSL, along with several opposition parties, met with Nawrocki on Saturday, while Tusk didn’t attend.

The president’s camp is hoping that the crisis surrounding the Constitutional Tribunal will erode Tusk’s parliamentary majority.

“Everything depends on those political parties who supported Donald Tusk so far,” Przydacz said.

Speaking on Saturday night, Tusk compared PiS to a man who steals an elderly woman’s purse and then claims to be the victim when police catch him and take it back.

PiS’ response to the suspension of Święczkowski, including the attempts to forcefully enter the tribunal on Friday, represents “another stage in the process of destroying the rule of law in Poland” by PiS and the president, Tusk said.

World.title: Protests and violence now go hand in hand in France. It wasn’t always like this
World.content:
Lucas Petit was just 11 when hundreds of thousands of men and women wearing yellow vests poured onto the streets and occupied roundabouts across France in November 2018.

His memories are hazy, though stories of clashes with police left a lasting impression. If he ever joined a demonstration, he knew what to expect.

“It helped shape this whole collective image of a violent protest,” he told CNN.

Petit, now 19, belongs to a generation for whom tear gas, water cannons, rubber bullets and stun grenades are par for the course when protesting.

“We feel somewhat compelled to respond with violence because we’re facing social, institutional, symbolic and now physical oppression,” Petit said. “So I think violence has become normalized.”

Petit has been blockading his school in eastern Paris for more than a month. He’s part of a movement that started out demanding better conditions at French schools and has since swelled into a collective cry of anger, bringing together groups with different grievances.

On October 17, a day of largely peaceful nationwide protests morphed into chaotic scenes of looting and destruction: Limoges’s historic town hall went up in flames; shops were ransacked, and protesters were maimed for life.

Protesters march during a demonstration in Paris on October 17. Geoffroy Van Der Hasselt/AFP/Getty Images

Opportunistic looters joined in, alongside young protesters from various backgrounds. According to an internal Justice Ministry document, 68% of the 186 people jailed between October 18 and 21 were 25 or younger, while 52% had no previous criminal record. Nearly half were classified as looters.

Failures in the police response help explain how the situation got so out of control. Behind the tear gas and smoke, however, lies a shift in how some French protesters operate.

Over the past decade, some have developed a savoir-faire for confrontation. As riot police have adapted their tactics and weapons, demonstrators have become adept at anticipating police maneuvers and exploiting gaps in security. Methods once associated with organized radical militants have spread to a younger generation.

How Black Bloc tactics spread

They tend to gather at the front of demonstrations, dressed head to toe in black, masked and hooded earning them the moniker “Black Bloc.”

The groups first appeared in Germany in the 1980s. Associated with anarchist and anti-capitalist movements, Black Bloc is not an organization with a formal leadership; it’s a set of protest tactics. These methods gained prominence in France during the 2016 labor protests before spreading further during the Yellow Vest movement.

Demonstration the Autonomous Bloc, or Black Bloc, on the occasion of German reunification at Alexanderplatz, on October 3, 1990. ullstein bild/Getty Images

Identities are concealed and participants often act as a group, sometimes attacking symbols of capitalism such as luxury stores.

These type of protesters are often referred to as “casseurs” too, from the verb “casser,” meaning “to break” – a broad term that can be applied to anyone who vandalizes property regardless of their ideological beliefs.

“Many young people who aren’t originally from the ultra-left are now adopting Black Bloc tactics,” said Thierry Vincent, an expert on radical-left movements. “It’s a way of protesting that doesn’t shock many young people anymore.”

One Black Bloc tactic involves small, highly mobile groups breaking away from the main march, forcing police to spread their forces thin, making it harder for them to respond in a coordinated way. That was on display a fortnight ago when a group of protesters attempted to reach the Elysee Palace, drawing riot police away from the demonstration. The maneuver worked. Police resources were stretched, and it contributed to officers being overwhelmed that day.

Destroyed shop during riots and looting in the Berlins district of Kreuzberg on international labor day night, on May 1, 1987, when allegedly the Black Bloc movement started. Roland Holschneider/picture alliance/Getty Images

It’s not just their methods that have caught on. There’s also a wider willingness to confront the police.

Hugo Melchior, a historian and left-wing activist who has attended demonstrations in the northwestern city of Rennes for two decades, saw that firsthand. In the sea of masked protesters, he spotted small groups of students apparently unconnected to militant organizations.

“Sometimes it was four young friends, high-school or university students, probably affiliated with no network or organization, who had simply decided to come and demonstrate that way, with the intention of fighting,” he told CNN.

Melchior had not seen so many people prepared for confrontation since the 2006 student riots.

Police tactics are changing too

Historically, France’s crowd control doctrine was all about keeping protesters at a distance. That’s become more difficult to maintain because of violent confrontations.

Olivier Cappe, a former riot police officer with 25 years of experience who now represents the UN1TÉ police union, said officers are now facing threats from Molotov cocktails, fireworks mortars, pétanque balls and other projectiles.

“Automatically you have to send your officers out to intervene, possibly charge and confront people,” Cappe said. “That’s where people get injured.”

Staff shortages compound the problem. Cappe estimates France lacks around 800 specialist riot police officers.

“The principle of French crowd control is numbers,” he said. “The more numerous you are, the more imposing you look. The more imposing you look, the less you intervene.”

Protesters inside a bar face riot mobile gendarmes near Porte de Vincennes during a demonstration in Paris, on October 24. Aris Messinis/AFP/Getty Images

Outnumbered officers may resort more quickly to weapons such as rubber bullet launchers, he suggested. During both the Yellow Vest movement and more recently the student protests, officers without specialist crowd control training have been deployed with devastating results.

Early in the protests, a 14-year-old boy suffered smashed teeth and a fractured jaw after a police officer fired a tear gas canister at close range, striking him in the face. A 16-year-old lost the use of an eye after being struck by a rubber bullet, while a 15-year-old lost a hand to a stun grenade, prompting the interior minister to temporarily suspend the grenade’s use.

Cappe acknowledges that more forceful policing can deepen the problem. When officers confront violent groups alongside students, younger demonstrators may later come to identify with those being targeted.

For student Lucas Petit, who identifies with the far left, the debate goes beyond whether violence is justified. It’s about what that violence is intended to achieve. He’s not shocked by attacks on symbols of capitalism, as he feels these acts of violence can serve a political purpose.

A firework explodes by a burning car during protests in Paris on October 17. Dimitar Dilkoff/AFP/Getty Images

“These are not acts of violence for the sake of violence,” he told CNN. “They have a very specific political message.”

On Wednesday French President Emmanuel Macron described the escalation of violence as a collective failure.

“I don’t think any high school student started pushing for their demands expecting to suffer such terrible consequences,” he said, adding police officers hadn’t signed up to face such violent confrontations either.

When asked about a 15-year-old student who lost his hand, Macron said nothing could justify what had happened and reiterated his call for calm.

Restoring peace to the streets is a tall order right now when so many feel that the government’s efforts to contain the violence, such as curfews, protest bans and a heavy police presence, violate their sacred right to protest and amount to a denial of democracy.

And with this no longer just being a student movement, as trade unions and Yellow Vests join in, voicing grievances over the cost of living and calling on Macron to go, the anger is unlikely to subside anytime soon.

On top of all that, France is heading into a deeply divisive presidential election in April, raising the stakes even further.

A winter of discontent may lie ahead, with another protest on Saturday and a major demonstration scheduled for November 5, raising fears of a repeat of the extreme violence seen on October 17.

World.title: Reunited after 1,711 days: Oleshky evacuees return to Ukraine under Melania Trump-brokered ceasefire
World.content:
Ukraine’s border with Belarus — Dmytro had not seen his wife Larisa for 1,711 days. He had been counting.

Waiting near the border between Ukraine and Belarus, his nervous eyes were fixed on the horizon, looking for the bus carrying Larisa and others fleeing the occupied southern Ukrainian town of Oleshky.

When the couple, both 54, finally reunited on Saturday afternoon, Dmytro didn’t hold back. He kissed Larisa over and over again and held her in his arms with such a determination that it looked like he’d never let go of her again.

Hundreds of people – and many pets – arrived back in Ukraine after being evacuated from the frontline city under a ceasefire that Pope Leo XIV called for and first lady Melania Trump helped to negotiate.

Larisa’s diminished frame – she has lost a third of her body weight under the occupation – looked almost lost in Dmytro’s hands. But she held her head high and her deep set blue eyes were sparkling with joy.

Asked how she was, Larisa spoke of others who are still suffering. “It’s hard for everyone in the country; there are so many people in the same situation as me. There are people in different situations, and some are even worse off. We’re waiting for all this to end, for peace to come, and for victory,” she told CNN.

Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky announced the arrival of the evacuees on Telegram, thanking Trump for her help with the mediation.

“And I thank everyone in the world—all journalists, all political and civic leaders, and all concerned people—who drew global attention to the situation in Oleshky and the genuine humanitarian catastrophe in the territory of Ukraine temporarily occupied by Russia. When the world pays attention, people are saved,” he said.

The first lady said on X that “Oleshky proves we can raise humanity above war.”

Ukraine’s ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets traveled to Oleshky to personally escort the evacuees, becoming the first high-profile Ukrainian official to openly travel to occupied areas under Russian control and Russia since the start of the war.

Speaking to CNN after crossing the border, Lubinets said the operation was extremely difficult but he hoped it could serve as an inspiration for the future.

“Now we have a unique positive experience how to negotiate with the Russian side with the coordination role of Melania Trump,” he said.

“We have a lot of similar villages where we have right now the same problems with food and medicine. Our idea is to continue. But it doesn’t only depend on Ukraine,” he told CNN, adding that he spoke to Russia’s human rights commissioner Yana Lantratova in Oleshky on Friday.

Malnutrition and no medicine

Dmytro, whose last name cannot be published for security reasons, is a soldier in the Ukrainian military which made Larisa vulnerable when Russia took over Oleshky, their southern Ukrainian hometown.

The couple managed to get their daughter out, but Larisa was worried that if she tried to leave, she’d be picked up at a Russian military checkpoint during ‘filtration’ – the humiliating and often violent questioning Ukrainians who found themselves under Russian occupation had to undergo before being allowed to leave for areas still under Ukrainian control.

So she stayed, hoping for a miracle. Instead, her life became a nightmare.

The town was hit by a major flood in 2023 after the nearby Nova Kakhovka Dam collapsed – most likely because of a Russian explosion.

More destruction came in the subsequent years of heavy fighting in the area and the humanitarian situation deteriorated in recent months. The town was reported by Ukrainian authorities to have run out of food and other supplies in September, with no access to electricity, gas, medicine and other essentials. Reports from that time said people were surviving on grass and weeds.

A still image taken from an undated drone video released September 12, 2026, shows destroyed buildings in Oleshky. 34th Separate Marine Brigade “Borysfen”/Handout/Reuters

The evacuees speaking to CNN on Saturday said there had been no food deliveries to Oleshky since the summer. One woman said she had not had bread for more than a year and survived on vegetables she planted earlier this year – mostly tomatoes and cucumbers.

The director of the Chernihiv Regional Hospital Andriy Zhydenko was waiting at the border with his staff to provide medical assistance to the evacuees. He told CNN the the effects of prolonged malnutrition will be a key concern, explaining that the evacuees will need to be fed carefully because they have been starving for so long that consuming too much food too quickly could be dangerous.

“There are people with injuries, stroke survivors and those with limited mobility,” he said, adding that everyone at the hospital was overjoyed to be welcoming Ukrainian citizens home. “All of my staff wanted to come here. People have suffered greatly there. There is no humanity.”

Speaking to CNN after getting off the bus on Saturday, another evacuee, Oleksandr, said he has “never felt better in my life.”

“It was like I’d escaped from hell,” he said. “I didn’t go outside at all … where we were, where we lived, we couldn’t get any food. We just ate whatever people had left in their apartments – canned goods, pickles.”

There were some residents who did not want to go to Ukraine and decided to stay in Oleshky – even though the ceasefire is set to expire on Sunday. Both Ukrainian and Russian authorities said they were provided with humanitarian aid.

Another group of people chose to go to Russia. Lantratova said on Saturday that these evacuees were received at a temporary accommodation center in Simferopol in Crimea.

Evacuees from Oleshky returned to Ukrainian-controlled territory on October 31, 2026. Valentyn Ogirenko/Reuters

Long way home

Some 40% of Oleshky’s prewar population of around 24,000 managed to flee to Ukraine-controlled territory when it was still possible early in the fighting, according to the Institute for the Study of War (ISW), a US-based conflict observer. Thousands of others have escaped since then, but many remained, either unable or unwilling to leave.

Zhanna Ptakhova and her daughers Elizaveta and Daria Paliy were among those who made it out when it was still possible.

But Ptakhova’s husband, and Elizaveta’s and Daria’s father, stayed in Oleshky. He was going to taking care of their home until they could safely return.

But that has not happened. “The conditions were terrible. No electricity, no gas, no heat – but he’s a man with golden hands,” Ptakhova told CNN.

“He took a house that had been adapted for modern civilian life and turned it into a home suited for a primitive lifestyle; he built a stove, raised chickens to feed himself, planted a garden, and through his own hard work, he survived there,” she said.

The family was reunited after three years apart. “I spotted my girls right away amidst everyone else, even from the bus,” Mykhailo Paliy said.

Mykhailo Paliy was reunited with his wife Zhanna Ptakhova and daughers Elizaveta and Daria Paliy on Saturday. Daria Tarasova-Markina/CNN

Access routes to Oleshky have been heavily mined and littered with drone and vehicle debris and evacuation across the Dnipro River directly into Ukraine-controlled territory is not possible.

That made the journey out long and scary. Once a two-day demining operation was completed on Thurday, people who wanted to leave gathered on Friday and traveled through the occupied Ukrainian peninsula of Crimea to Anapa in Russia’s Krasnodar region.

The evacuees then flew from Anapa airport to Gomel, Belarus, according to the Russian Defense Ministry and Ukrainian officials, and then traveled by bus to Ukraine. Once across the border and reunited with their loved ones, the convoy of busses set off again. Strangers lined the road for miles, waving Ukrainian flags.

World.title: Reduction of electricity tariff brackets for coded meters begins in New Valley
World.content:
The Governor of the New Valley, Hanan Magdy, announced that the Ministry of Electricity and Renewable Energy and the Egyptian Electricity Holding Company have approved a reduction in the tariff rate for “coded” electricity meters issued prior to January 2024.

The rate will be lowered from 275 piasters per kilowatt-hour to 192 piasters per kilowatt-hour—a reduction of 83 piasters per kilowatt-hour.

This reduction will take effect starting November 1, in response to requests from citizens and with the aim of easing their financial burdens.

The governor emphasized that this approval comes as part of ongoing coordination with the Ministry of Electricity and relevant authorities, aimed at streamlining procedures and providing further facilitation for citizens—with due regard for social considerations and the goal of easing the financial burden associated with electricity consumption.

The Head of the Electricity Sector in the New Valley, Yasser Omar, said that charging centers have begun receiving citizens who wish to adjust their billing tier via their meter-recharge cards.

He added that the necessary executive steps to implement the reduction are being closely monitored to ensure that eligible citizens receive the intended benefits.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: Cybersecurity expert reveals how pornography ended up on a Cairo billboard
World.content:
Cybersecurity expert Haitham Salah-Eddin revealed that the breach of a digital advertising display management system in Cairo, which resulted in the broadcast of pornographic content, was the result of a cyberattack targeting the international company responsible for managing the advertising content – rather than a breach of the physical billboard itself.

During a phone interview with “al-Hekaya,” (The Story) hosted by Amr Adib on MBC Masr on Saturday, Salah-Eddin explained that the Egyptian company that owns the screen had leased it to an international firm tasked with managing the s displayed on it.

This international company manages advertising screens across four countries, he noted. The breach of its system granted the hacker remote control over the content displayed on screens in these nations, including Brazil.

Salah-Eddin further noted that there is recent information circulating suggesting that the individual behind the hack is a Brazilian national.

A common cyberattack

The export noted that this type of attack has occurred in other countries; Germany experienced a similar incident earlier this year, preceded by another in England.

The motives of the hackers vary depending on the nature of the groups carrying out the attacks, he explained.

He added that some groups – particularly those consisting of younger individuals – carry out these operations to make their presence known to the world.

Others resort to hacking to increase the financial rewards they can demand for their attacks, often by executing large-scale operations that generate significant public attention.

Salah-Eddin further observed that some attacks carry political messages intended to weaken public faith in their safety, even despite protective measures taken by their governments – he cited events that took place in France as an example.

Expanding scope

He warned of the expanding scope of unconventional cyberattacks, emphasizing that they are no longer limited to websites or traditional systems; rather, they now extend to internet-connected devices, including advertising displays, refrigerators, and various household appliances.

Salah-Eddin cited an incident that occurred in France two or three weeks ago, in which approximately 700 smart refrigerators, located in hypermarkets belonging to four major retail chains, were hacked.

This caused the internal temperatures to rise to 60 degrees Celsius, resulting in the spoilage of frozen food.

He noted that the incident affected various stores across France and other European countries, and added that a similar event had taken place a month earlier, in August.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: Economic expert reveals Egyptian pound outlook for the coming two months
World.content:
Economist Mohamed Anis has described the declines seen on the Egyptian Exchange over the past week as “paper losses” rather than actual, realized losses.

In a phone interview with “Hadith al-Qahira” (Cairo Talk), he attributed this downturn to the sale of shares, undertaken to generate liquidity for the upcoming initial public offering (IPO) of Banque du Caire, as well as the exit of foreign investments from stocks and bonds, coinciding with an outflow of “hot money.”

Anis explained that the stock market decline is linked to two primary factors.

The first factor is the behavior of individual and institutional investors, who sell off portions of their holdings to secure the liquidity needed to participate in major public offerings, a pattern observed in the Egyptian market in previous years, which is currently recurring with the Banque du Caire IPO.

Anis added that the second factor involves foreign investment managers opting to sell, alongside the withdrawal of “hot money” from bond and equity markets, a trend that has coincided with selling pressure from local investors.

The economic expert explained that a decline in the value of investment portfolios does not necessarily mean that actual losses have been incurred.

An investor who loses 90 percent of their portfolio’s value has likely chosen an unsuitable stock or made a purchase at an inappropriate price, he noted, thereby emphasizing the importance of analyzing the strength of stocks before making any buying decisions.

Anis advised investors not to rush into selling stocks out of fear during market downturns.

Instead, he suggested identifying the right time to restructure investment portfolios, rather than making sell decisions in response to short-term market fluctuations.

Regarding the foreign exchange market, the expert projected that the US dollar-Egyptian pound exchange rate would stabilize between LE 54-57 over the next two months, in light of the economic repercussions stemming from the military conflict between the US and Iran.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: Youth Ministry organizes field visits for Korean delegation
World.content:
The Ministry of Youth and Sports organized field visits for the South Korean youth delegation including the Smart Village, Zewail City of Science and Technology, and the Grand Egyptian Museum to introduce the Egyptian experience in technology and scientific research alongside its cultural and historical elements.

The delegation began at the Smart Village to explore information and communications technology institutions and Egypt’s digital transformation visiting the Information Technology Institute and the National Telecommunication Institute to understand their role in developing digital skills and preparing youth for the labor market.

The program included visiting Zewail City of Science and Technology to learn about its role in supporting scientific research, innovation, and developing Egypt’s education system.

The Korean delegation concluded with a tour inside the Grand Egyptian Museum, viewing prominent artifacts embodying ancient Egyptian civilization and exploring modern museum display techniques presenting Egyptian cultural heritage.

These visits fall under the Egyptian-Korean youth exchange program enhancing friendship, cooperation, and cultural exchange between youth from both countries to build bridges of communication.

World.title: Final Verdict: Swiss Supreme Court Upholds Alieu Kosiah’s 20-Year Sentence for Lofa War Crimes
World.content:
Court clears ex-ULIMO commander of crimes against humanity but leaves sentence intact

Monrovia – Former ULIMO commander Alieu Kosiah will serve the full 20 years in prison for atrocities committed in Lofa County during Liberia’s civil war, after Switzerland’s Federal Supreme Court upheld his war crimes conviction in a ruling made public Friday.

By Rodney Sieh



The decision makes final the first war crimes conviction ever handed down by a Swiss civilian court. It is also the first conviction anywhere of a Liberian for war crimes committed during the country’s two civil wars, which ran from 1989 to 2003 and killed an estimated 250,000 people.

Kosiah was found guilty of crimes committed in Lofa between 1993 and 1995, including killing civilians and ordering their killing, rape, using a child soldier, ordering pillage, cruel treatment of civilians, and desecrating the body of a dead civilian through an act of cannibalism.

The Appeals Chamber of Switzerland’s Federal Criminal Court had found that those crimes alone would justify 150 years in prison. The sentence was reduced to 20 years, the maximum allowed under Swiss law.

Crimes Against Humanity Charge Thrown Out

In a partial win for the defense, the Supreme Court acquitted Kosiah of crimes against humanity, a conviction the Appeals Chamber added in 2023. The court ruled that the crimes against humanity provision, which entered Swiss law in 2011, cannot be applied to acts committed between 1993 and 1995.

The acquittal does not affect his 20-year sentence or his expulsion from Switzerland once he has served it.

Lawyers for the victims welcomed the final conviction but criticized the acquittal.

“Today the survivors of Alieu Kosiah’s crimes have final justice, more than 30 years after they suffered and twelve years after his arrest,” said Alain Werner, Director of Civitas Maxima, the Geneva-based group that represents victims in the case. “When this case began, it was often their word against his, about events during a brutal and traumatic civil war. Today Switzerland’s highest court has confirmed that they were believed.”

Werner said his team was “deeply disappointed” by the acquittal, arguing that civilians in Lofa were deliberately targeted — killed, raped, looted and forced to carry loads for fighters — in a widespread and systematic attack.

“What happened in Lofa between 1993 and 1995 is the very definition of a crime against humanity,” he said.

Twelve Years in Detention

Kosiah settled in Switzerland in the late 1990s and was arrested in November 2014 after Liberian victims filed a criminal complaint through their lawyers. He has been in detention ever since.

Survivors traveled from Liberia to testify against him during the investigation and at both of his trials.

The case was built with the help of the Global Justice and Research Project (GJRP), a Liberian organization that has documented civil war crimes for more than a decade. Together, Civitas Maxima and GJRP have contributed to six criminal trials in four countries linked to Liberia’s civil wars, resulting in five convictions.

‘Our People Should Not Have to Keep Looking to Europe’

The ruling once again throws a spotlight on Liberia’s failure to try its own war criminals. More than two decades after the war ended, no war crimes trial has been held on Liberian soil. Armed groups recruited more than 21,000 children during the conflict.

Liberia has committed to establishing a War and Economic Crimes Court, but the court has yet to hear a case.

GJRP Director Hassan Bility thanked Swiss authorities for more than ten years of commitment that allowed Liberian survivors to take part directly in the trials, but said justice should be delivered at home.

“These crimes were committed in Liberia by a Liberian against Liberians, and the judgment was delivered thousands of miles away,” Bility said. “Our people should not have to keep looking to Europe or the United States for justice. It is more than time for these trials to take place in Liberia, and for the War and Economic Crimes Court to start its work.”

[OPTIONAL: Reaction from the War and Economic Crimes Court office, the Ministry of Justice, or Lofa County residents/lawmakers.]
