World.title: Dinamo Sack Mario Kovačević After Shock Defeat to Rudeš
World.content:
Dinamo have sacked head coach Mario Kovačević following Saturday’s 1-0 defeat to newly promoted Rudeš in the 12th round of the SuperSport HNL. The Zagreb club, led by Zvonimir Boban, confirmed the decision on Sunday.

B team coach Jerko Leko will take charge on an interim basis, starting with Thursday’s Europa League trip to Sunderland and followed by the league match against Varaždin.

The defeat in Velika Gorica proved the final straw. Junior Fernandes scored the only goal for Rudeš, while Dion Drena Beljo had two goals ruled out, one for offside and one for handball. Dinamo also finished with ten men after substitute Iker Almena was sent off for an elbow to an opponent’s head.

Speaking after the match, the 51-year-old said he understood the supporters’ anger and would not hide behind anyone. “If people are angriest with me, I accept the blame,” he said. Asked whether he still justified Boban’s faith in him, Kovačević pointed to his record over 16 months: a rebuilt squad, a league and cup double, and a solid start to this season. He called the Rudeš result a major slip, said four points in Europe was less than Dinamo had wanted, and insisted the season could still be turned around.

Kovačević took over in June 2025 and led Dinamo in 73 matches, winning 48, drawing 11 and losing 14. Last season he delivered the double, winning the SuperSport HNL and the SuperSport Croatian Cup.

Born in Jablanica, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kovačević played for Varteks, Belišće, Slaven Belupo, Međimurje, Slovenian side Nafta, Nedelišće and Dinamo Tirana before retiring in 2008. He began coaching in 2014 with Međimurje, and went on to work with Varaždin’s youth and senior teams, Polet Sveti Martin na Muri, Podravina Ludbreg, Mladost Ždralovi and Slaven Belupo.

In November 2023, Varaždin announced that Kovačević had been diagnosed with lung cancer. He stayed on the bench until early December before stepping away for surgery, and in late March 2024, he confirmed that the cancer had receded.

World.title: Zagreb Will Remain Directly Connected to Madrid This Winter
World.content:
November the 1st, 2026 – Zagreb will remain directly connected to Madrid this winter as Croatia Airlines decides to keep the direct link between the two capital cities open outside of summer.

The Spanish capital is one of the largest cities in the EU, a paradise for lovers of food, football, history and the irresistible Mediterranean lifestyle. Madrid, with an average altitude of 650 metres, is the second-highest capital in Europe after Andorra. Lana Mindoljevic writes for Putni kofer that this metropolis is now also available to Croatian travellers over winter. Croatia Airlines is, for the first time, opting to continue running its seasonal route between the Croatian and Spanish capitals even after the end of the summer timetable.

FLIGHTS ARE ON MONDAYS, THURSDAYS AND SATURDAYS, WITH A BREAK DURING PART OF THE WINTER

Direct flights between Zagreb and Madrid will operate until the 16th of January 2027, and then again from the 15th to the 27th of March 2027. In both periods they are scheduled three times a week, on Mondays, Thursdays and Saturdays. The only period without flights will therefore be from the 17th of January to the 14th of March. For all three days the departure and arrival times are the same. Departure from Zagreb is at 8:25, and the return from Madrid at 12:10. The flight lasts between two hours and 45 minutes and two hours and 55 minutes.

Such a schedule allows, for example, departure on Thursday and return on Monday, with four overnight stays in Madrid. For a shorter break one can combine Saturday departure with return on Monday. The morning flight from Zagreb leaves a good part of the first day for getting to know the city, while on the last day one has to count on leaving for the airport during the morning.

madrid is an excellent winter city break from zagreb

Madrid is an excellent choice for travellers who like to combine art, architecture and good food. The winter months give a special rhythm to the visit: a colder morning can be spent in a museum, the sunny part of the day in a park, and the evening in one of the city taverns. Although we associate Spain with sun and a warm climate, in Madrid in winter you should not expect spring temperatures. A warm jacket and comfortable shoes are a mandatory part of the luggage.

For art lovers the main asset is the famous museum triangle. The ‘Golden Triangle of Art’ consists of three renowned Madrid museums: Museo del Prado, Reina Sofía and Thyssen-Bornemisza, which are home to some of the world’s most valuable art collections. In the Prado one can see Velázquez’s “Las Meninas” (The Maids of Honour), Goya’s “Black Paintings” and Bosch’s “The Garden of Earthly Delights”. The Reina Sofía Museum holds Picasso’s “Guernica”, while Thyssen-Bornemisza offers an overview of European painting through different periods. Instead of trying to see everything in one day, choose the museum that interests you the most and leave it enough time.

THE ROYAL PALACE IN WHICH NOBODY ACTUALLY LIVES

A first visit to Madrid is hard to imagine without the Royal Palace, Plaza Mayor and Puerta del Sol. These places can be connected into a walk through the historic centre, with stops for coffee and exploring the surrounding streets. The Royal Palace is the official royal residence even though no one has lived in it since 1967. It has a huge courtyard and an incredible 3,418 rooms, and today it is used exclusively for state ceremonies. The building is open to the public, and for visitors to Madrid the changing of the guard, which takes place every Wednesday and Saturday, could also be interesting.

TWO FAMOUS SQUARES THAT SHOULD NOT BE MISSED

The famous Puerta del Sol square, translated as the Gate of the Sun or simply ‘Sol’, is an unmissable stop, and on it is the ‘centre of Spain’. Namely, on Sol, in front of the building of the Royal Post Office, there is the well-known plaque that marks ‘kilometre zero’ of all Spanish roads. In the centre of the square there is also a statue of King Charles III, but it is not the most popular statue on the square. It is overshadowed by the statue of a bear standing on its hind legs to feast on the fruits of the madroño tree, a sculpture that essentially symbolises the growth of the city.

Plaza Mayor, a gigantic square in the very heart of Madrid, has always been the centre of events. Kings were crowned there, but heads were also cut off. Today coffee is often drunk and time is enjoyed surrounded by beautiful buildings. This very square is also home to the traditional Christmas market, which has been held there since 1860. For a quieter part of the day there is El Retiro park, one of the favourite city green destinations. Together with the Paseo del Prado area it is part of the UNESCO World Heritage. It is nice to fit it into a day dedicated to museums: after a few hours in front of paintings a walk in the open air will be welcome.

Madrid is also discovered at the table. In the La Latina neighbourhood, especially around Cava Baja and Cava Alta streets, taverns and bars line up where you can try small bites and share several dishes. Croquettes, patatas bravas and potato tortilla are a good start to such a gastronomic tour. For a cold afternoon save a place for churros with thick hot chocolate, one of the recognisable Madrid sweet stops. If you stay in the city over Sunday, you can spend the morning at El Rastro, the famous flea market where clothes, records, antiques and various small items are browsed, and then continue for lunch in La Latina.

the city of football

Madrid is known as a city of football, and many visit it precisely to take a look at some of its famous stadiums. In the case of Real Madrid it is Estadio Santiago Bernabéu, which can hold 81 thousand people, and in the case of Atlético de Madrid Wanda Metropolitano. If you are a football lover, you can opt for one of the guided tours and look at the clubs’ memorabilia, jerseys and trophies in the museums on that topic.

IN DECEMBER MADRID PUTS ON ITS FESTIVE ATTIRE…

A trip in December brings an additional reason to come: illuminated streets, Christmas decorations and the traditional market on Plaza Mayor. A walk through the city then easily turns into an evening tour of festive scenes. For now it is known that Advent begins at the end of November and will last until the end of December, and besides the main location with more than 100 wooden stalls other locations in the city are also decorated.

World.title: Slovenia Wants a Hydropower Plant Next to the Border – Croatia Says No
World.content:
November the 1st, 2026 – Slovenia wants to construct a new hydropower plant next to the border with Croatia, but Croatia is, so far, totally against the plan.

Croatia currently completely opposes neighbouring Slovenia’s intention to build the Mokrice hydropower plant on the Sava River, which would be located about 450 metres from the Croatian border. Index reports that there is concern that the project could ecologically endanger the Sava as it enters into the territory of Croatia and call into question the supply of drinking water in that area, whose sources also supply Zagreb with water. HRT reports that energy expert Ivica Jakić and director of the Slovenian company HESS Boštjan Pišotek spoke about this topic.

potential problems for croatian drinking water

This is otherwise a hydropower plant that would be the last in a series of six facilities on the lower course of the Sava. Slovenian Minister for the Environment and Spatial Planning Polona Rifelj announced the relaunch of the procedure for deciding on the predominance of the public interest of energy production over nature conservation, reports N1 Slovenia. The Croatian Ministry of Environmental Protection and Green Transition opposes the project due to the possible deterioration of the condition of surface and groundwater downstream of the dam.

The organisations Croatian Society for the Protection of Birds and Nature, CEE Bankwatch Network and Biom have also warned of the risks. According to their claims, existing Slovenian hydropower plants have already reduced the transport of sediments towards Croatia, which has contributed to the deepening of the Sava riverbed and the lowering of the groundwater level in the wider Zagreb area. The associations warn that the construction of HE Mokrice, downstream from the confluence of the Krka River with the Sava, could further worsen the situation and endanger the sources of drinking water for Zagreb. The Croatian ministry also states that the benefits of the project would remain on the Slovenian side, while Croatia would bear the negative consequences. Among the possible impacts, additional erosion of the riverbed, endangerment of fish habitats and protected areas of the Natura 2000 network are highlighted.

slovenia: the project is in line with all rules and regulations

HESS director Boštjan Pišotek said that this is a project that is being developed in accordance with European rules. “Croatia was informed about the procedure from the very beginning, about 15 years ago when the development of the Mokrice hydropower plant project began,” Pišotek said. He emphasised that cooperation with Croatia has several levels and that this resulted in Croatia giving a positive opinion on the placement of the Mokrice hydropower plant in the space. The Slovenian Ministry for the Environment and Spatial Planning earlier stated that Croatia can participate in cross-border consultations and put forward comments, but that it does not have a right of veto on the project. The decision on issuing the permit remains within the competence of the Slovenian authorities, while respecting international and European regulations.

croatia will link up its own system

Energy expert Ivica Jakić explained how the Croatian Multipurpose Hydraulic System Zaprešić would link up with the Slovenian hydropower plant. “The Mokrice hydropower plant must come from the Slovenian side to solve for the Slovenians the problem of soil deepening and the problem of deposits. It is a logical solution that Slovenia is looking for and wants to have,” Jakić said. He added that Croatia will link up with its own system. “It will solve the stabilisation of the water flow and the deepening of the soil. It will help us, but also Slovenia in further regulating the flow of the Sava River through the Croatian part,” Jakić concluded.

World.title: Function of Croatian Judiciary Facing Serious Problems Once Again
World.content:
November the 1st, 2026 – The very function of the Croatian judiciary is facing serious problems yet again due to some judges refusing to participate in proceedings if they’re recorded.

President of the Constitutional Court Frane Staničić stated that the Court will function with great difficulty due to the decision of some judges not to participate in sessions that are audio-recorded. Index reports that in an interview for RTL Danas he revealed that he is extremely sorry that individual judges, as he believes, have stopped providing protection to citizens within the judiciary system. These are judges Andrej Abramović, Sanja Bezbradica Jelavić and Lovorka Kušan, who oppose the way in which the audio recording of sessions was introduced. They claim that no appropriate decision of the Court was adopted and refuse to participate in sessions which, in their opinion, are being recorded unlawfully.

“we really tried hard to come to an agreement”

Staničić said that the judges during the past year invested great effort so that the Constitutional Court would function normally and protect the rights of citizens. As an example he cited decisions on politically sensitive laws, among which are the Act on Building Management and the Act on Local Taxes. He emphasised that the decisions on those laws were adopted by a large majority, with only one or two votes against. He added that the number of separate opinions has significantly decreased, which according to his interpretation shows that the judges sought to reach agreement. “Unfortunately, due to the refusal of certain colleagues to participate in the work of the constitutional court bodies because of the introduced audio recording, the system will function with great difficulty,” Staničić said.

When asked why he introduced recording without a decision of all the judges, Staničić confirmed that there was no formal decision of the Constitutional Court as a collegial body. He claims, however, that there was an informal agreement and that all judges were familiar with the procurement and installation of the equipment. “I warned the judges several times that we would buy the system, that we had procured it, installed it and that we were testing it. At the session on the 6th of October, which was also recorded, I said in front of everyone that from that day, in accordance with the agreement, the sessions are being recorded. No one reacted to that,” he explained. He also commented on the appearance of judge Andrej Abramović, who had been a guest on RTL the day before. Staničić believes that Abramović should have pointed out his disagreement before the conflict among the judges arose because of the recording.

the introduction of audio recording doesn’t require the permission of all judges

“He said in your programme that he practically knew that recording was taking place, or rather that recording would be introduced, but that I am neither his father nor mother, so he would not warn me that something is not good,” Staničić said. “I’d like to openly ask the public to judge – is it in accordance with the role of a Constitutional Court judge that if he considers that something is not good, he collegially warns the President of the Court that he considers that this should not be done, or that he remains silent and then on the basis of his unexpressed disagreement creates this problem that has now occurred?” he added.

Staničić claims that he did not need a special decision of all the judges to introduce audio recording because as President he has the authority to decide on the manner of establishing the minutes. As the main reason for introducing recording he cited earlier disagreements about the content of the minutes of the sessions.

“I introduced audio recording for a simple reason: we had a series of problems with establishing the authenticity of the minutes. It happened that colleagues claim that something stands in the minutes that should not stand and vice versa,” he explained. As a particularly problematic case he cited the events from May of this year, when the judges discussed the composition of the panels of the Constitutional Court. According to his words, it was precisely the judges who now oppose the recording who at that time contested the minutes.

“The judges who today contest the audio recording at that time contested the minutes that were signed by two minute-takers and whose accuracy was confirmed by five judges. In such circumstances there is no other way to ensure an authentic record that no one will be able to contest,” Staničić said.

should some sessions be completely open to the public?

The President of the Constitutional Court believes that audio recording should contribute to transparency and the possibility of verifying what was said at the sessions. He also announced that he wants to open a discussion on the possibility that part of the sessions of the Constitutional Court will in future be accessible to the public.

“I personally believe that the Court should be more open to the public in general. I can announce that I will initiate a serious discussion at the Constitutional Court on the Court becoming more open, that perhaps even part of the sessions will be public,” he stated. He emphasised that the main task of the Constitutional Court is the protection of citizens’ rights, but he believes that due to the current conflict that task has fallen into the background. He also rejected claims that the recordings of the sessions are his private documentation.

“This is official documentation created in official premises, with official equipment, and is stored on the official servers and information system of the Constitutional Court,” he said.

Staničić claims that every judge can access the recordings and listen to them. He rejected the claim of judge Abramović that access was denied to someone, but at the same time emphasised that a distinction must be made between the possibility of listening and obtaining one’s own copy of the recording. “I received a request for a copy of the recording. Here a distinction must be made between the possibility of listening, which is absolutely not disputed, and the question of copies. I replied only to the colleague who requested it that her request will be considered in terms of scope and possibilities. Therefore, such a request has by no means been rejected,” he stated.

no agreement has been reached at all

In order to resolve the dispute, Staničić proposed the establishment of a working group that would prepare rules on audio recording. It would include him, the Secretary General of the Constitutional Court and one of the judges who oppose the recording. “Unfortunately, I did not receive a positive answer because participation in the working group is conditioned on the cessation of audio recording. I have already explained that this is impossible, because it is the only way in which I can ensure authenticity,” he said.

Staničić stated that one of the three judges who opposed the recording nevertheless participated in a session, although she retained her opposition. He believes that the remaining two judges could have done the same so that the work of the Court would not be hindered. “Unfortunately, the other two judges did not want to follow that example. They could have retained their opposition, but we want to protect citizens. However, they chose the opposite – not to protect the rights of citizens, but to deepen the conflict, which is unnecessary,” he said.

a new session has been announced for november the 13th

The President of the Constitutional Court said that he has no mechanisms by which he could force the judges to participate in the work. Nevertheless, he hopes that everyone will accept the responsibility they have towards citizens and enable the continuation of regular work. He announced that he will schedule a new session as soon as the two judges who oppose the recording return from an official trip, which he expects to take place on or around the 13th of November. In the meantime the question remains open whether an agreement will be reached on the manner of recording the sessions.

Staničić also said that the Constitutional Court has received requests from GONG, the media and citizens for access to the audio recordings. He emphasised that this is sensitive documentation that may contain secret data and that he cannot make it public on his own. Due to the great public interest he announced that he will seek the consent of all constitutional judges for the publication of the recordings. If he obtains it, he is ready to publish them, and if someone opposes it, he announced that he will publicly say who was against.

“This is a very sensitive issue and secret data that I cannot just give out. However, given the extreme importance of the issue and the interest of the public, I will propose and seek a consensus of all judges that the recordings be given to the public. If a consensus is reached, I will give the recordings. If it is not reached, if even one judge is against, I will publicly announce which judges were against it,” Staničić concluded.

World.title: Daytime Lights Now Mandatory on Roads in Croatia
World.content:
November the 1st, 2026 – Daytime lights being on is now mandatory on all roads in Croatia, with a fine of 30 euros being prescribed to those who fail to comply.

As of today (November the 1st), the national obligation to use daytime or dipped headlights while driving during the day comes into force for drivers using roads across Croatia. Index reports that this rule will now remain fully in force until the 31st of March 2027. Drivers who fail to comply face the aforementioned fine of 30 euros.

the law applies to all motor vehicles

This is an obligation prescribed by Article 102 of the Road Traffic Safety Act, which the Police Directorate also reminded of ahead of the holiday weekend. Although many newer cars have automatic daytime running lights, drivers of older models will have to make sure to switch them on. According to the law, daytime or dipped headlights must be switched on on motor vehicles while driving during the day, regardless of weather conditions and visibility. For motorcycle and moped drivers the rule is somewhat different – they are obliged to use dipped headlights throughout the year, and a fine of 30 euros is also prescribed for non-compliance.

cyclists and e-scooter owners

The police also state that there are obligations for cyclists and drivers of personal means of transport, which include electric scooters. From the first dusk until full dawn, as well as during the day in the case of reduced visibility, they must have a white light switched on at the front and a red light at the rear. The fine for non-compliance with this rule amounts to 60 euros.

caution with automatic daytime running lights

Owners and drivers of cars with automatic light switching should check how the system works on their vehicle. On some models daytime running lights illuminate only the front of the car, while the rear ones remain off. This can be dangerous in conditions of reduced visibility, such as fog or heavier rain. Daytime running lights serve for better visibility of the vehicle, but are not a substitute for dipped headlights which are necessary at night and in conditions of poorer visibility.

winter equipment on vehicles will also soon become mandatory

The beginning of November brings another change for drivers, which comes into force a little later. From the 15th of November to the 15th of April, the use of winter equipment will also become mandatory on certain sections of public roads across Croatia, regardless of the weather conditions. In the case of winter conditions, when the road is covered with snow or ice, winter equipment is mandatory on all roads nationwide. It’s important not to equate this obligation with the one on the use of lights, which begins two weeks earlier. The Police Directorate calls on drivers to respect traffic regulations and take care of safety. “Comply with traffic regulations and make sure your lights are always on for better visibility, and especially from the 1st of November to the 31st of March,” the police concluded.

World.title: New Ultra-Fast Chargers Put Into Operation on Croatian Motorways
World.content:
October the 31st, 2026 – New ultra-fast electric vehicle chargers have been put into operation on the Croatian motorways A1 and A3, with some having power as strong as 400 kW.

Petrol has put into operation 18 new ultra-fast charging points for electric vehicles on the Croatian motorways A1 and A3, among which are six charging points with a power of 400 kW intended for heavy electric trucks. Poslovni reports that the new connections have been installed at the Janjče west, Dragalić south, Dragalić north and Desinec north rest areas, the company announced. This therefore expands the network of charging stations on important transport routes towards the Adriatic and on the motorway that connects Slavonia with Zagreb.

there are now 70+ ultra-fast connections across croatia

During the summer, Petrol already opened new ultra-fast charging stations at the Vrata Jadrana north and south and Dragalić north rest areas, and the latest investment also includes infrastructure for electric freight vehicles. The company now has more than 300 charging points for electric vehicles dotted all over Croatia, of which more than 70 are ultra-fast. At the regional level its network covers approximately 1,300 connections. Particularly significant is the installation of 400 kW charging points for electric trucks, which due to the large capacity of their batteries require more powerful infrastructure than passenger cars.

Nevertheless, the actual charging speed depends on the capabilities of the vehicle, the state of charge of the battery and other conditions, so the nominal power of the charger does not mean that every vehicle will be able to charge the battery at a power of 400 kW.

eu cash helped to expand the network

The new charging stations are part of Petrol’s OneCharge network and the European CROSS-E project, which is co-financed with European Union funds through the Connecting Europe Facility (CEF). The project includes the development of infrastructure for ultra-fast charging of passenger cars and electric trucks on important transport routes in Croatia and in neighbouring Slovenia. Within the scope of this particular project, Petrol plans to install a total of 98 charging points at 22 locations in the two countries. Part of the infrastructure will be intended for electric freight vehicles.

These considerable investments are also linked to the European Alternative Fuels Infrastructure Regulation (AFIR), with which the European Union is gradually introducing requirements for the availability of charging stations on the main transport corridors. The overarching goal is to facilitate travel by electric cars on longer routes, reduce the need for detours for charging and enable the development of electric freight traffic.

World.title: Croatian Railway Projects Totalling €1.7 Billion Are Now Underway
World.content:
October the 31st, 2026 – Croatian railway projects totalling €1.7 billion are currently underway as part of a major investment cycle.

The Croatian railway network is currently in the middle of a major investment cycle. Index reports that large projects worth €1.7 billion are underway, and by 2035 additional investments of around six billion euros are planned. The goal of the modernisation is to ensure faster, safer and more reliable transport of passengers and freight and to strengthen the competitiveness of Croatian ports.

State Secretary in the Ministry of Maritime Affairs, Transport and Infrastructure Žarko Tušek, member of the Management Board of HŽ Infrastructure Marijan Ćužić and professor from the Faculty of Transport and Traffic Sciences Mladen Nikšić spoke on HRT about the current projects, traffic safety and the deadlines for the first results. State Secretary Žarko Tušek emphasised that the modernisation of the railway is a continuation of major investments in transport infrastructure, after road, maritime and air transport. “It is the turn of the railway, without which there is no development of the economy, port capacities, logistics, rural areas and regional transport,” Tušek said.

a lowland railway to rijeka

He noted that projects worth more than a billion euros have been completed, and almost 700 million euros have been invested in the maintenance of the sector in the last eight years alone. “The value of active, contracted projects currently amounts to €1.7 billion,” he said. Among the largest projects are the reconstruction of the Dugo Selo – Novska railway, worth 900 million euros, and the Hrvatski Leskovac – Karlovac section of 350 million euros. Investments are also being made in the Podravina and Istrian railways and the Zadar – Knin railway, while the Vukovar – Vinkovci section has been completed. Long-term plans envisage investment of another around six billion euros by 2035, and the modernisation of the entire 2,600-kilometre network will continue after that as well. As a key future project Tušek singled out the lowland railway towards Rijeka, estimated at around five billion euros.

the dugo selo-novska railway is becoming double-track

“Just yesterday we selected international consultants who will accompany us in the negotiation procedure so that within a year we can reach the conclusion of an Alliance contract for the construction of that major project,” he announced. Member of the Management Board of HŽ Infrastructure Marijan Ćužić said that the reconstruction of the Dugo Selo – Novska railway, worth almost 900 million euros, will bring a significant step forward in the development of transport. “That section is the only one on the former tenth international corridor that has remained single-track. With the completion of the works we will have a double-track electrified railway from the border with Slovenia to the border with Serbia, with speeds of up to 160 kilometres per hour,” Ćužić explained. He compared the importance of the second track with road traffic, where an additional lane increases throughput. He emphasised that this will enable Croatia to reach the standards of modern European railways and ensure faster and safer travel.

croatia will need to wait a decade before it notices a difference

Professor Mladen Nikšić from the Faculty of Transport and Traffic Sciences believes that the current investments will bring significant improvements, especially after the completion of all projects. “I believe that we will have higher-quality railway traffic, shorter journey times and greater track capacity for the transport of passengers and freight. This will also make our ports more prominent,” Nikšić said. He assessed that the modernisation should significantly shorten journeys. “I believe that when those projects are completed, we will be able to reach Slavonski Brod or Vinkovci in two to two and a half hours, and we will travel faster towards Rijeka and the Adriatic cities as well.

That takes time, but I think the full effects will be visible in about ten years,” he said. Nikšić added that investments in infrastructure must be accompanied by better quality of transport, especially the punctuality and reliability of trains. “Work needs to be done on the quality of transport, punctuality and reliability. We also have new vehicles, and all of that together with a quality timetable must form a complete whole,” he said.

Professor Nikšić also commented on recent railway accidents in Croatia. He pointed out that the causes can be divided into two groups: non-compliance with procedures and problems in communication, and shortcomings in vehicle maintenance. “The number of freight train accidents on the Rijeka railway is particularly worrying.

With the liberalisation of freight traffic the state has lost part of its influence on the maintenance and control of vehicles,” he warned. He believes that the Railway Traffic Safety Agency should intensify extraordinary and unannounced inspections, and that for the prevention of human errors the key are the education of employees and compliance with procedures. “Administratively everything can be in order, but vehicles can be better or worse maintained. Work must certainly be done on that,” he emphasised. Marijan Ćužić from HŽ Infrastructure said that preliminary checks of recent accidents have not shown irregularities on the infrastructure, but that investigations are still ongoing.

the rijeka railway can’t deal with all the freight

“Our first preliminary investigations have shown that there was no error on the infrastructure. The railway systems, including tracks and switches, are correct,” Ćužić said. He added that the education and communication of all participants in railway traffic need to be improved in order to reduce the risk of accidents. Žarko Tušek emphasised that investments in the railway have a key role in strengthening the competitiveness of Croatian ports. As an example he cited Rijeka, whose traffic is growing, but the existing railway cannot accept all the freight, so it ends up on the roads. Marijan Ćužić continued and explained that the construction of the second track will enable significantly greater freight transport. “We calculate that with the new railway we will be able to transport to Europe all the additional quantities of freight that the Port of Rijeka plans in the next ten years or so,” he stated.

could rijeka become a bigger logistics centre than trieste and koper?

Mladen Nikšić believes that along with Rijeka it is also necessary to develop the Dalmatian ports, modernise the Lika railway and better connect Zadar, Šibenik and Split. He also warned that the future lowland railway towards Rijeka will require additional port capacities.

“When the lowland railway is built, its capacity will be 30 million tonnes, which Rijeka alone will not be able to generate. That is why we already need to think about a new port on Krk, a railway connection and a new bridge that would connect the island with the mainland,” Nikšić said. Tušek confirmed that the lowland railway, a new terminal on Krk and a large freight centre in Zagreb are part of the Government’s strategic plans. “Krk is not any fantasy, but a project that needs to start being elaborated urgently. Its potential is such that Rijeka could become a stronger logistics centre than Koper and Trieste together,” Tušek concluded.

When asked when the general public and the economy will feel concrete benefits, Marijan Ćužić replied that the first results will be visible in two to three years, and that the Croatian railway in the next decade should reach the European level. “The first advances will be seen on the section from Zagreb to the Hungarian border, but also on the railways in Istria, in the Knin and Zadar area and on the Podravina main line. Already in a relatively short time our users will be able to use the advantages of a modern railway,” he concluded.

World.title: Social Democrats council endorses Jonatan Vseviov's prime minister bid
World.content:
The Social Democratic Party (SDE) council has formally endorsed Jonatan Vseviov as their party's candidate for prime minister in the 2027 Riigikogu elections.

Vseviov, who stepped down as secretary general at the Foreign Ministry to run in next spring's elections, will head the party's list in Electoral District 4, which covers Harju and Rapla counties.

On the proposal of party leader Lauri Läänemets, the council approved his nomination as the Social Democrats' candidate for prime minister on Sunday.

Läänemets said the party will campaign as a united team.

"Our goal is to win these elections because the Social Democrats are offering the people of Estonia the best possible candidate for prime minister and a strong team to bring Estonia back to the heart of Europe," he said.

The party chair noted that the SDE's support has tripled since the last Riigikogu elections in 2023, crediting the work of both longtime party members and new recruits.

"Now it's up to us to grow that support even further," he added.

Social Democratic Party (SDE) council meeting. November 1, 2026. Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

'We alone are responsible for us'

In his address to the council, Vseviov called for Estonia to pursue a more ambitious foreign policy and play a greater role in shaping Europe's future. He said Estonia must have a strong and influential voice in decisions affecting the continent.

"We alone are responsible for both telling our own story and ensuring there is room for our freedom in the Europe of the future," Vseviov said. "We cannot assume that questions affecting Estonia's future will stay off the international agenda just because we meekly keep our mouths shut."

Such matters will come up regardless, he stressed, adding that "the less weight our voice carries in those discussions, the more likely others are to decide our future without us."

The next Riigikogu elections will take place on March 7, 2027.

World.title: Estonia's Selevko wins bronze, Petrõkina third ahead of free skate in Canada
World.content:
Estonia's Mihhail Selevko struck bronze at Skate Canada International in Kelowna, where Niina Petrõkina heads into Sunday's free skate in third after setting a personal best.

Fifth after the men's short program, Selevko climbed to third overall by winning the free skate with 169.08 points, just shy of his personal-best 169.78, set a month and a half ago. The Estonian skater finished with 248.66 points across the two programs.

Selevko also became the third Estonian figure skater to reach the podium at an International Skating Union (ISU) Grand Prix event, joining his older brother Aleksandr and training partner Niina Petrõkina.

"I fought through the entire program and was more nervous before the competition than I had been for the short program, because yesterday's event was difficult," he said. "Today I needed and wanted to do better, so I focused on every jump. I'm very happy it worked."

While placing second in both programs, France's Kevin Aymoz won his second career Grand Prix event with a combined 258.43 points, earning 168.17 for his free skate to Estonian composer Arvo Pärt's "Spiegel im Spiegel."

Japan's Rio Nakata, a two-time world junior champion, slipped to fourth in the free skate with 156.61 points but held onto second overall with 249.25 in his senior Grand Prix debut.

Niina Petrõkina competing in 2026 Skate Canada International, part of the ISU Figure Skating Grand Prix in Kelowna, Canada. October 31, 2026. Source: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect/Scanpix

Personal-best short program

In the women's event, two-time European champion Niina Petrõkina sits third heading into Sunday's free skate after setting a personal-best 77.24 in the short program, edging out her previous best of 77.20 set in Italy six weeks ago.

Petrõkina delivered a clean program, executing all her jumps without error and earning the highest rating, Level 4, on all her other elements.

Japan's Mao Shimada, a four-time world junior champion who turned 18 on Friday, won the short program with a personal-best 82.11 points, including 49.23 points for her technical elements, the third-highest score ever.

American Isabeau Levito, another former world junior champion who won gold in Tallinn in 2022, was second with 78.50 points in her first competition of the season.

The 2026 Skate Canada International is the second of seven events in the 2026 ISU Figure Skating Grand Prix series, which concludes with the final in Chongqing, China, in December.

The women's free skate in Kelowna begins Sunday at 10 p.m. Estonian time.

World.title: Veteran diplomat warns Estonia's 'predictable' Russia message losing impact
World.content:
Former longtime diplomat Jaap Ora says Estonia should carefully calibrate its public statements on Russia to avoid being sidelined internationally by predictable rhetoric.

Ora, who recently joined Isamaa, criticized Prime Minister Kristen Michal's (Reform) response to recent reports that the U.S. had asked the Baltic states to tone down their rhetoric about the threat posed by Russia.

He also warned that Estonia's foreign policy messaging has become predictable, risking fatigue among international partners.

"Foreign policy is not the place to speak your mind," Ora wrote on social media, adding that diplomats have to think carefully about what they say and calibrate their message each time accordingly.

"Words are an important tool in diplomacy, but they have to serve a purpose," he said. "Your heart may be burning, but your public message should be measured."

Ora said treating foreign policy as simply "expressing positions" is an oversimplification.

"Our message has gotten predictable, and there's a risk that people will grow tired of hearing it," the ex-diplomat said, warning that Estonia could lose its seat at the table for important discussions.

"Those invited are expected to bring fresh ideas and something valuable [to the discussion]," he explained. "If our message is already predictable, there may be less interest in having us there."

Prime Minister Kristen Michal (Reform). Source: Siim Lõvi/ERR

Estonian leaders stand firm

Citing several anonymous sources, Reuters reported Friday that the United States had asked the Baltic states to tone down their public statements about Russia and put less emphasis on the threat it poses.

Michal responded that he had no intention of holding back, saying pressure on Russia should be maintained instead.

Other Estonian officials echoed the prime minister's sentiments, including outgoing Foreign Ministry Secretary General Jonatan Vseviov, who snoted he was not aware of any official requests from U.S. officials for Estonia to change its Russia rhetoric.

"Perhaps also because a proposal like that would always and in any case get rejected," Vseviov said.

"Estonia's voice is our most important trump card, the most important weapon for taking part in international politics," he emphasized. "And while that voice must be used wisely and never belligerently, surrendering that voice is something we should never even consider."

World.title: Gallery: AI revives Estonian artist's lost 19th-century masterpiece
World.content:
A reproduction of a massive long-lost painting by Estonian master Johann Köler is on view in Viljandi, brought back to life using AI and a single black-and-white photograph.

The painting, "Waking from Charmed Sleep" ("Ärkamine nõidusunest"), dates back to 1864 and measures 4.3 by 3.2 meters. Viljandi Museum exhibition curator Kristjan Mändmaa describes it as a politically charged work highlighting native Estonians' lack of land ownership under Baltic German rule.

The painting depicts a German nobleman opening a tomb and reaching for an amulet worn by an Estonian woman representing the people emerging from 700 years of serfdom. The amulet, Mändmaa explained, symbolizes Estonian land, which was largely controlled by Baltic Germans at the time.

"Köler saw this as a tremendous injustice, and this was his way of fighting against it," he added.

The work sparked a major scandal when it was first shown, drawing furious reactions and threats from the Baltic German press.

"Legend has it that the Baltic Germans somehow arranged to have the painting destroyed, which would explain why it disappeared," Mändmaa said.

Anniversary shows draw large crowds

Viljandi Museum program director Signe Susi said three major exhibitions marking the 200th anniversary of the birth of Estonia's first professional artist drew large crowds to Viljandi this year. The Kondas Center welcomed nearly 11,000 visitors, Rüki Gallery 2,500 and the Viljandi Museum itself expects more than 13,000.

Music educator and orchestra conductor Harry Illak, who also took part in events marking Köler's 190th, said his interest in the artist's life and work had only grown since.

"After all these visits, my understanding of Köler and his work has changed considerably from what it was ten years ago," he added.

The AI-restored reproduction of "Waking from Charmed Sleep" remains on view at the Viljandi Museum on Sunday.

World.title: Justice chancellor nominee pledges nonpolitical office, social rights focus
World.content:
Supreme Court Justice Oliver Kask, nominated as Estonia's next chancellor of justice, says he will protect the office's political independence while focusing on social rights.

President and previous justice chancellor Ülle Madise has nominated Kask for the seven-year post, which is appointed by the Riigikogu. Parliamentary groups plan to meet with him before making their decision.

Kask said he took time to consider the offer, given the importance of the issues handled by the office. He plans to focus on social rights, particularly where people struggle to defend their interests or take cases to court, as well as protecting democracy and the rule of law.

"It's important to me that the institution of the Chancellor of Justice not be political," Kask said. Political questions, he added, should be left to the Riigikogu and the government to decide.

Kask has worked at the Ministry of Justice, served as a Tallinn Circuit Court judge and chaired the National Electoral Committee (VVK). He is currently a Supreme Court justice serving on the court's Administrative Law Chamber.

Riigikogu parliamentary groups have outlined several priorities for their meetings with him.

Isamaa MP Lea Danilson-Järg pointed to the state's obligations to citizens, including 2,000 people waiting for special care services. "The state has failed to meet its obligations there," she said.

Danilson-Järg also cited the official status and role of the Estonian language as another party priority.

Transparency and quality

The Social Democrats (SDE) want the justice chancellor to continue working on data protection issues. Party leader Lauri Läänemets said growing volumes of personal data must be protected without obstructing law enforcement.

"We don't need haste here; we need balanced and considered decisions," he said.

Conservative People's Party of Estonia (EKRE) MP Anti Poolamets said Kask must demonstrate the office's independence and commitment to fundamental rights — "with conviction, not just as a formality."

He also called for safeguarding the transparency of online voting and the ability to file election complaints.

Reform Party MP Madis Timpson, chair of the Riigikogu's Legal Affairs Committee, said the justice chancellor's focus should be on better laws, not more of them.

"We need better-written legal provisions and a state where everyone can understand they aren't being subjected to unjustified restrictions," Timpson explained.

The parliamentary groups are scheduled to meet with Kask the week after next.

World.title: Enefit Power invokes exemption for shale oil use at Balti Power Plant
World.content:
Starting Sunday, Enefit Power will start using shale oil at its Balti Power Plant if its Unit 11 is out of service or uncompetitive on the electricity market.

Enefit Power CEO Raine Pajo informed Environmental Board Director Rainer Vakra and Climate Minister Erkki Keldo (Reform) that the company would use shale oil in the plant's reserve boilerhouse under an exemption granted by the board on October 21.

The order permits the preventive use of shale oil if natural gas supplies are at risk of disruption or restriction, or if district heating risks becoming unaffordable for Narva residents.

In his letter, Pajo said price volatility, rising winter demand and the risk of further supply disruptions threatened both natural gas security and the affordability of district heating. He warned that heating could become unaffordable even without an actual interruption in gas supplies.

"Given the current geopolitical and economic situation, Narva also considers it necessary to start using shale oil," the CEO wrote, pointing to Europe's lower-than-usual gas storage levels, high natural gas prices and winter supply risks.

He also cited the ongoing Middle East crisis, which drove European gas prices to a four-year high in October.

Shale oil use 'temporary and preventive'

Paju called the measure temporary and preventive, saying it would reduce Narva's dependence on volatile imported gas and help keep district heating affordable.

The amount of shale oil used, he added, would depend on gas supply conditions and the city's heating demand.

Enefit Power said the gas market situation and Narva residents' vulnerability justified using shale oil from November 1 if Balti Power Plant's Unit 11 was uncompetitive or out of service, formally notifying the Environmental Board of its plans.

World.title: Prime minister: I will not remain silent about Russia
World.content:
Prime Minister Kristen Michal (Reform) said Russia is killing women and children and he will not hold back when speaking about the Russian threat, after reports that U.S. officials had asked the Baltics to tone down their statements.

Reuters news agency reported on Friday, citing several anonymous sources, that the US had asked the Baltic states to tone down their rhetoric on Russia and reduce their emphasis on the threat posed by Russia in public statements

Michal said no requests have reached him.

"No such complaints have come directly to me. The last time we were together with Trump was in Ankara in the summer at the NATO summit, and the message from the Americans has rather been that European countries must take their own defense against the Russian threat seriously and put more money into defense, and Estonia is certainly doing that. We are rather a strong contributor to security and a security partner for the United States," he told ERR on Friday.

Estonia will continue to raise awareness about Russia's aggression and its crimes in Ukraine, the prime minister said.

"Even before Russia's full-scale aggression against Ukraine began, we warned about the plans and wishes of Russian dictator Putin. And we have continued to do so, and I will continue to do the same. I do not intend to hold back, because pleasing dictators or remaining silent is certainly not the solution. Rather, we must continue the pressure and support Ukraine – that is the only way to force Putin to change his objectives," Michal told ERR.

"Ahead of this winter, on Putin's orders, electricity infrastructure and heating infrastructure are currently being destroyed and bombed. Now the Russians have targeted water supplies and sewage systems. They are killing women and children. What words can European leaders even use to describe this? All words are too mild for this. The reason Putin is currently being portrayed as cornered is that there is no real progress on the battlefield, and therefore Putin is carrying out various hybrid attacks and essentially behaving like a terrorist. We certainly cannot, and I certainly do not intend to, soften my tone or remain silent about Russia," he continued.

"Who else, if not Estonia's leaders – the prime minister in public appearances or private conversations, or Estonian defense and security officials in various appearances or discussions – should directly describe what Russia is doing? As John McCain once said when he was a US presidential candidate, Russia is a gas station pretending to be a country, and today it is led by a dictator who kills women and children. And in my opinion, all words are indeed too mild to describe this," Michal added.

World.title: Police catch teenagers who deliberately left scooters on 70 km/h road
World.content:
Police have identified several young men who deliberately left electric scooters on a 70 km/h stretch of road near Keila, endangering people's lives. The company that owns the vehicles has temporarily suspended operations in the area.

Officers received a report in late September that an electric scooter was lying on the road near the Mudaaugu bus stop on Paldiski Highway, the Police and Border Guard Board (PPA) said on Saturday.

According to Hisko Vares, head of the investigation unit at Lääne-Harju Police Station, several reports of similar incidents were received over the course of the month. "Police have been informed on 10 occasions that an electric scooter had been left on the road. In one case, a car hit a scooter, but fortunately no one was injured," he said.

The head of the investigation unit said police officers gathered additional information from residents, but the investigation was complicated by the lack of surveillance cameras in the area. There were also no eyewitnesses, as far as police are aware.

"After extensive work, the perpetrators were identified as three young men aged 17, 18 and 24," Vares said.

He stress that deliberately leaving objects on the road is extremely dangerous. "The speed limit on this stretch of road is 70 km/h, and hitting an electric scooter in the dark at that speed could end extremely badly. The young men endangered other people through their actions, and it is only fortunate that no one was injured," Vares said.

The PPA has launched misdemeanor proceedings, during which all the precise circumstances will be established.

Company suspends scooter parking in the area

Hoog Mobility, the company that owns the electric scooters, told ERR it is aware of the incidents, is cooperating with police and has temporarily removed its electric scooters from the area.

"Yes, we are aware of these incidents and take them very seriously. These are not incorrectly parked scooters. The scooters were in a parking area and locked, but someone deliberately carried them from there onto the highway. This is vandalism that endangers the lives and health of drivers. Nothing like this has happened to us before, and the incidents have been confined to one area," said Drevor Rudnevs, Hoog Mobility management board member.

Several of the company's scooters have been damaged as a result of the incidents, but he did not say how extensive the damage was. "Scooters can be repaired or replaced, but a person's health cannot," Rudnevs added.

The board member said police are aware of the incidents and proceedings are ongoing: "As a precautionary measure, we have temporarily removed the parking areas in this region. We are grateful to local residents who have informed us of their observations"

World.title: Iraq to keep oil output unchanged in December 2026
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – During a virtual meeting on Sunday, seven OPEC+ nations, including Iraq, Saudi Arabia, Russia, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria, and Oman, agreed to maintain their required September 2026 production levels through December 2026.

Iraq’s required allocation remains unchanged at 4.43 million barrels per day.

The decision comes as OPEC+ seeks to maintain market stability amid regional disruptions.

Iraq has been working to push for higher production baselines—including ambitions toward a six million barrels per day baseline in future negotiations—while balancing export flows through alternative routes.

The group is scheduled to hold its next review meeting on November 29, 2026.

In early September, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi called for an increase in oil output to reach 10 million barrels per day by 2030.

According to al-Zaidi, Iraq’s oil output should be proportionate to its reserves, oil production capabilities, and the growing number of the population, allowing it to satisfy its residents’ needs as well as development requirements.

Iraq’s oil production reached approximately 4.5 million barrels per day by the end of 2025.

Iraq is a founding member of the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC), which was established in Baghdad in September 1960.

Iraq currently ranks as the second-largest crude oil producer in OPEC after Saudi Arabia.

World.title: Iraq, Saudi Arabia to revive joint oil export pipeline
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Saudi Arabia has given preliminary approval to revive the joint oil export pipeline project with Iraq, sources told local news outlet Shafaq News on Saturday.

The original 1,568-kilometer pipeline—which runs from Iraq’s Zubair oilfield in Basra to the Saudi Red Sea port of Yanbu and has been idle since 1990.

Riyadh argues that rehabilitation would cost nearly as much as constructing a new line, and Iraq would have to cover part of the cost for its section.

Understandings with Saudi Arabia have emerged as one of the most significant paths through which Iraq intends to revive a historic pipeline that has been idle for more than three decades. The step is part of a larger effort to increase the country’s oil export flexibility.

The pipeline passes through key stations in Saudi Arabia, making it one of the longest oil pipelines in the region.

Following the Gulf War, the pipeline was shut down in August 1990. It remained out of operation for decades, despite Iraq’s several attempts to restart it.

According to reports, the project initially cost over $2.6 billion and features an advanced infrastructure of storage tanks and loading terminals. The infrastructure makes it a compelling option for reuse, contingent upon an agreement between the two parties.

This pipeline is a strategic option to export oil through the Red Sea, lessening Iraq’s dependency on the Strait of Hormuz and providing more flexibility in regulating export flows.

The revival of the pipeline may boost economic connections between Iraq and Saudi Arabia and offer new options for collaboration in the energy industry, given the rising demand for secure and dependable export routes.

World.title: Iran’s gas supplies to Iraq fall to 10.5 million cubic meters
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iran’s gas supplies to Iraq have fallen to 10.5 million cubic meters per day—a development likely to exacerbate the challenges facing the electricity sector in the country.

An Iraqi source told Attaqa News that Iranian gas supplies to the southern region have ceased, with flows now limited exclusively to the central region.

Iranian gas flows to Iraq are currently less than 20 million cubic meters per day, as reported roughly a month ago.

The decline in supplies comes at a time when Iraq’s electricity sector relies on Iranian gas to operate several power plants—a situation complicated by pressure from Washington on Baghdad to halt these imports.

A month ago, gas supplies from Tehran ranged between 15 and 20 million cubic meters per day before dropping to their current level—a decline attributed to Iran’s rising gas demand amid falling temperatures.

Tehran is facing a domestic supply shortage, which has compelled it to reduce export volumes, particularly during cold weather.

The decline in supplies to Iraq affects several provinces, as Tehran typically meets between 30 and 40 percent of the requirements for several Iraqi power plants.

Gas supplies have experienced frequent interruptions in 2026, compelling the Iraqi Ministry of Electricity to implement emergency measures.

These measures include utilizing domestic gas and working with the Ministry of Oil to get alternative fuels, such as red diesel.

In March 2026, the suspension of Iranian gas supplies to Iraq—following an attack on the South Pars field—resulted in the loss of approximately 3,100 megawatts of power capacity.

According to agreements between Baghdad and Tehran, supply levels must be between 25 and 35 million cubic meters per day in the winter and around 55 million cubic meters per day in the summer.

World.title: IMF prepares new lending program for Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The International Monetary Fund (IMF) is preparing a new lending program for Iraq after starting formal discussions with authorities in Baghdad.

IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva confirmed that Iraq submitted an official request for a new support program during the IMF’s annual meetings in Bangkok.

The IMF forecasts that Iraq’s economy will contract by 16 percent in 2026, heavily impacted by regional conflict and disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz, which constrains its vital energy exports.

IMF spokesperson Julie Kozack stated that the fund is engaging directly with Iraqi authorities to understand their economic priorities, address structural vulnerabilities, and shape the structure of the financial support package.

Iraq’s last formal program with the IMF concluded in 2019, and the country is scheduled to pay approximately $428 million in interest to the institution through 2030.

Since the outbreak of conflict in the Middle East on February 28, Tehran has almost completely restricted navigation through the Strait of Hormuz.

Iran now mandates that vessels follow specific routes, occasionally targeting those that attempt to pass without prior coordination. In response, Washington has imposed a blockade on Iranian ports.

The Iraqi economy relies heavily on energy exports, most of which transit through this strait.

World.title: Trump slams former Iraqi lawyer Alina Habba over controversial $50M deal
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Former U.S. President Donald Trump launched a sharp public attack against his former personal attorney of Iraqi descent, Alina Habba Meldon, describing her acquisition of a financial contract exceeding $50 million as “provocative and completely unacceptable,” following an investigative report by The New York Times exposing her agreement with a firm tied to the family of a pardoned Venezuelan banker while holding senior positions inside the U.S. Department of Justice.

Speaking to reporters on Saturday evening from his Mar-a-Lago club in Palm Beach, Florida, Trump said he directly informed Habba that he did not want her taking any compensation, calling the episode “horrible, totally outrageous, and completely unacceptable.”

The remarks mark a stark reversal after years of public praise in which Trump regularly lauded her courage and fierce loyalty across high-profile legal battles and media appearances.

According to details reported by The New York Times, the agreement was executed with Concord Partners, an entity affiliated with the family of Venezuelan banker Julio Herrera Velutini, who previously faced federal bribery charges in the United States before finalizing a misdemeanor plea deal in August 2025.

The multi-year retainer granted Habba a compensation package exceeding $50 million over four years, structured as $10 million annually alongside performance bonuses.

The report traced the timeline of Habba’s government tenure and concurrent corporate engagements:

Late October 2025: Habba signed the lucrative contract while serving as Acting U.S. Attorney for the District of New Jersey, days after the corporate entity was registered.

December 8, 2025: Following a judicial ruling challenging her acting tenure, Habba resigned from the post and was appointed on the same day as a senior counselor to the U.S. Attorney General.

January 1, 2026: Habba officially commenced her compensated work for the corporate vehicle while remaining in her executive Department of Justice advisory role.

January 15, 2026: Trump issued a full presidential pardon to banker Julio Herrera Velutini.

Habba firmly rejected the allegations last week, stating that she never solicited or received funds to lobby for a presidential pardon, never met with White House or Justice Department officials regarding the matter, and took no official actions associated with any pardon petition.

The public fallout marks a contentious rupture between Trump and his former attorney, whose Iraqi heritage and prominent courtroom profile had made her one of the most visible figures in his close legal and political circle.

World.title: Economist Al Marsoumi warns of flawed assumptions in 2027 budget
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi economic expert Nabil Al-Marsoumi warned on Sunday, November 1, 2026, against the federal government’s reliance on “unrealistic projections” to estimate revenues for the 2027 sovereign budget—the largest in Iraq’s history at over 174 trillion Iraqi dinars ($114.6 billion).

Al-Marsoumi argued that the fiscal calculations rely on unattainable baselines, including crude export targets of 4 million barrels per day (bpd), optimistic collections from domestic refineries, and an aggressive doubling of non-oil revenues.

In an analysis published on his official social media channels, Al-Marsoumi laid out the structural components of the projected 174.233-trillion-dinar fiscal revenue framework:

Total Non-Oil Revenues: 29.513 trillion dinars

Total Hydrocarbon Revenues: 144.720 trillion dinars Crude export sales: 127.020 trillion dinars Crude sales to domestic refineries: 17.000 trillion dinars Mineral and associated resource sales: 700 billion dinars



Al-Marsoumi noted that aggregate revenue projections for 2027 surpass those in the previous three-year budget framework by roughly 40 trillion dinars and exceed actual realized revenues from 2025 by nearly 50 trillion dinars.

World.title: Anbar launches expanded afforestation campaign to combat desertification
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Contemporary Environmental Team in Al-Baghdadi subdistrict, Anbar Governorate, has launched an afforestation campaign under the direct supervision of the Anbar Environment Directorate and the Hit Environmental Unit, in coordination with the local administrations of Al-Baghdadi and Jubba subdistricts and the Al-Baghdadi Municipal Directorate.

The initiative falls under broader Ministry of Environment efforts to execute sustainable ecological initiatives across the governorate.

Ahmed Al-Mahmoud, head of the Contemporary Environmental Team in Al-Baghdadi, told the Iraqi News Agency (INA) that the campaign involves planting diverse climate-resilient tree and shrub varieties suited to local environmental conditions. The project aims to expand green cover, enhance air and environmental quality, and combat desertification across western Iraq.

Al-Mahmoud stressed the critical role of inter-agency cooperation among municipal departments, local administrative units, and grassroots volunteer initiatives in executing successful afforestation projects. He emphasized that these greening efforts should be continuous rather than seasonal, noting that the campaign will expand into other areas of Anbar Governorate in upcoming phases.

He also highlighted that long-term campaign viability requires continuous care, systematic irrigation networks, and ongoing maintenance to guarantee sapling survival, transforming planted zones into sustainable green spaces capable of restoring ecological balance and mitigating climate vulnerabilities.

World.title: US dollar edges down in Baghdad, holds steady in Erbil at 167,900 IQD
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate of the U.S. dollar against the Iraqi dinar edged down slightly across Baghdad’s main currency exchanges on Saturday, October 31, 2026, while holding steady in Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan Region, at the opening of the weekly trading cycle.

According to market data, wholesale rates at Baghdad’s central Al-Kifah and Al-Harithiya exchanges slipped to 167,900 dinars per $100, marking a slight decline from 168,000 dinars recorded at the close of trading on Thursday.

Retail exchange desks across local markets in Baghdad saw retail selling rates stabilize at 168,500 dinars against buying bids of 167,500 dinars per $100.

In Erbil, parallel trading counters maintained flat levels, quoting selling prices at 167,750 dinars alongside purchase bids of 167,650 dinars per $100.

World.title: Three held over pro-Khalistan graffiti at Delhi Metro stations after Diljit concert
World.content:
The arrests come days after singer Diljit Dosanjh performed in New Delhi.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Three people, including a woman, have been arrested for allegedly writing pro-Khalistan slogans at two Delhi Metro stations, police said on Sunday. The graffiti also carried a message targeting singer Diljit Dosanjh.The arrests come days after Dosanjh performed in the national capital on Friday as part of his Aura India Tour. The singer is scheduled to take the tour to several other cities over the next two months.The graffiti was found at Jahangirpuri and Shastri Nagar Metro stations on October 29 and 30, respectively. Police said the accused were allegedly promised substantial financial rewards for defacing public property at prominent locations in Delhi.The arrested persons have been identified as Sumeet alias Raftar (30), a resident of Panipat in Haryana, and Sumit Kumar alias Kaka (22) and Gurpreet (22), both from Punjab.According to Deputy Commissioner of Police (Special Cell) Narra Chaitanya, the investigation revealed that Sumit Kumar was allegedly the main instigator.Sumeet allegedly painted the slogans near Gate No. 1 of Jahangirpuri Metro station and recorded a video of the act to send to his handlers.Kumar and Gurpreet allegedly defaced a staircase wall near Gate No. 2 of Shastri Nagar Metro station."In both instances, the graffiti read "Diljit Singh quam d gaddar khoon d badla SFJ Khalistan", expressing support for the banned separatist organisation Sikhs For Justice (SFJ) and Khalistan ideology. These acts defaced public property in Metro stations and posed a threat to public order and national integrity," the police said, ANI reported.Police said Sumit Kumar had been in contact with SFJ sympathisers in Ludhiana and Gurdaspur before an associate allegedly instructed him to download an encrypted messaging application.A member linked to the banned separatist organisation Sikhs For Justice (SFJ) allegedly shared graffiti templates through the app and offered him financial rewards for carrying out the activity at prominent Metro stations.Kumar then allegedly recruited Gurpreet and Sumeet to execute the plan. The three travelled to Delhi on October 28, police said.Police said Sumeet ad come in contact with Kumar through online platforms and had visited Ludhiana about a week before the incident. The trio travelled to Delhi by taxi and reached ISBT Kashmere Gate on October 29.Investigators also found that Kumar and Gurpreet had known each other for around four years. Kumar allegedly persuaded her to travel to Delhi on the pretext of shopping before informing her about the plan, police said.Police further alleged that Kumar had painted graffiti near the GTK Bypass, under the jurisdiction of Samaypur Badli police station, on October 30. That incident is being investigated separately.Two FIRs were registered at the Metro Azadpur and Metro NSP police stations under Section 3 of the Delhi Prevention of Defacement of Public Property Act, 2007, and Section 62(2) of the Metro Railway (Operation and Maintenance) Act, 2002."Further investigation is underway to identify other persons involved in the network and establish the role of the handlers behind the alleged operation," the officer said.

World.title: Bhutan dedicates Buddhist stupa to PM Modi; Rijiju calls it ‘huge honour’ for India
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Bhutan's King Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck has dedicated a sacred Buddhist stupa to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, recognising his contribution to strengthening friendship between the two countries.

The dedication of Stupa number 76 took place during a ceremony to raise and consecrate 108 stupas in Gelephu Mindfulness City on Sunday.

According to news agency ANI, Union minority affairs minister Kiren Rijiju represented India at the ceremony and expressed gratitude to Bhutan for the gesture, describing it as a "huge honour for India". He also conveyed gratitude on behalf of Prime Minister Modi to the Bhutanese King.

In a post on X, Rijiju said, "It's a huge honour for India that very sacred stupa 76 is dedicated to Hon'ble PM Narendra Modi ji for his outstanding vision and commitment to friendship between India and Bhutan. On the auspicious occasion of Lhabab Duchen, joined the sacred ceremony in Gelephu Mindfulness City, Bhutan, marking the raising and consecration of 108 stupas, accompanied by the blowing of Dungchens."

He further said, "Paid my respects and offered prayers in the presence of His Majesty the King of Bhutan, Her Majesty the Gyaltsuen, H E Dasho Tshering Tobgay, Prime Minister of Bhutan & the people of Bhutan.





A deeply meaningful spiritual occasion, reflecting Bhutanâs rich Buddhist heritage and the enduring bonds of friendship between our two nations."

Stupas are sacred Buddhist structures associated with the teachings and life of Gautama Buddha. Traditionally, they were built to preserve the relics of the Buddha and other revered Buddhist figures, including their ashes and remains. Over time, they became important places of worship, meditation and religious devotion.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The 108 stupas in Bhutan are known as Jangchub Chortens, or Stupas of Enlightenment. The number 108 holds special significance in Buddhist traditions and is associated with religious practices, including the use of 108 beads in prayer malas. The structures are intended to promote peace, harmony and spiritual well-being.

Rijiju is visiting Bhutan from October 31 to November 2. Earlier on Sunday, Rijiju met Bhutanese Prime Minister Tshering Tobgay in Gelephu. The two leaders discussed strengthening the India-Bhutan partnership and exploring the potential of the Gelephu Mindfulness City project.

World.title: CM Mann says opposition parties have nothing to offer Punjab, eyes AAP's return to power in 2027
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann on Sunday alleged that the Shiromani Akali Dal, Congress and BJP had nothing constructive to offer the people of the state. He accused his opposition of prioritising political power and personal interests over public welfare.

Addressing a gathering in Punjab, Mann said people had witnessed the difference between self-serving politics and development-driven governance. He also expressed confidence that the

(AAP) would get another opportunity to govern the state in 2027.

Taking aim at the Akali Dal, Mann alleged that the party had failed to answer for the painful incidents of sacrilege and had been reduced to the Badal family and a handful of close associates.

He described the Congress as a "divided house", where leaders were constantly at loggerheads with one another.

"These political parties are hand in glove with each other, with their sole agenda being to grab power and protect their vested interests," he alleged.

Mann said people had trusted his government so far and expressed hope that they would continue to support it. "The people have witnessed the difference between politics driven by personal interests and governance driven by public welfare.





They have trusted me so far, and I hope they will continue to repose their faith in me in the future as well," he said.

The chief minister also highlighted the government's Mukh Mantri Mawan-Dheeyan Satkar Yojna, under which Rs 1,291 crore was transferred to the bank accounts of more than 37.43 lakh beneficiaries.

World.title: Coal India records highest-ever monthly supplies at 70.3 MT in Oct, up 19%
World.content:
New Delhi: Public sector Coal India Limited (CIL) recorded its highest-ever monthly supplies at 70.3 million tonnes (MT), registering a robust 19% growth over the 59.2 MT supplied during the corresponding period in FY26, despite operational challenges posed by unseasonal rainfall, Puja festivities and the impact of a cyclone, amid rising power demand.

The previous monthly record of 69.4 MT was achieved in March 2026, CIL said in a statement. Its subsidiary Mahanadi Coalfields Limited also crossed the 20 MT monthly supply mark for the first time in Oct.

Responding to demand for additional coal from thermal power plants, CIL said it supplied a record 57.1 MT to the power sector, 19% higher than the 48 MT supplied in Oct FY26. On average, 310 rakes were loaded per day during Oct, the highest-ever, surpassing the previous record of 303 rakes a day achieved in March 2025.

Coal production in Oct reached 67.2 MT, setting a new record for the month and surpassing the previous high of 62.4 MT recorded in 2024, the company said, adding that the production was around 19% higher than the 56.4 MT achieved in Oct 2025, reflecting a sharp acceleration in mining activity following the monsoon season.
